You were so deep asleep when I left, you looked so beautiful. Do you miss me?" "I do," I said. "I miss you more." He laughed softly. "I'll call you before bed, okay? Don't stay up too late." | cursed under my breath and started to type an apology. And the man on the podium raised his voice. : "It is my great honor," he said, "to invite to this stage, for the first time in public, the chairman of Veil Holdings. Please. Give it up for Chairman Dominic Ford." 19

chapters.title: Chapter 16
chapters.content:
Chapter 016 CELESTE I stopped on the pavement of Helix and looked at them, all of them, lined up in the early morning light, clapping for me, and something cracked open in my chest in a way I was not prepared for. I walked down the line. I shook hands. I accepted the hugs. I said thank you, genuinely, to each of them, because they had kept this place alive through years when keeping it alive had seemed like stubbornness rather than strategy. When I reached Pat she pulled me into a hug so tight I felt it in my spine.

"I don't know how you did it," she said, her voice muffled against my shoulder. "I don't know how, but thank you. Thank you, Celeste." I hugged her back. "We did it," I said. "All of us." She pulled back and looked at my face with wet eyes. "Was it Julian? Did he pull strings?" I laughed. I could not help it. The question was so far from the truth that it came out as a laugh before I could shape it into anything else. "No," I said. "It was not Julian." "Then how?" "I promise I will tell you everything. Once everything is in place. The whole story." I squeezed her hands.

" But not yet." She searched my face for a moment. Then she nodded. I thought about the day Seraphine had left. I had not been there for it properly, had been too caught up in Julian's world to see how much it had broken Pat, how much she had absorbed the loss of her colleague and just kept going because there was no other option. Pat had held Helix together in the years of my marriage almost single-handedly, had kept the research moving forward on a budget that should have made it impossible, had refused to let the work die.

Seeing her face this morning was worth every single thing I had done that brought me here. An hour later, the grants and administration coordinator appeared in the doorway of the meeting room where Pat and I were going over preliminary plans. "It dropped," she said. We both looked at her. The money It just dropped. Into the account." Pat made a sound I had never heard her make before. Something between a gasp and a laugh. She covered her mouth with both hands. +15 Bonus I stared across the table. I had not signed the contract yet.

Dominic had told me it was prepared and I could sign whenever, and I had assumed that meant after signing, not before. But the money was there In the account. Five billion dollars sitting in Helix Research Laboratory's bank account on a regular morning before nine o'clock. I called a meeting immediately. The whole team crowded into the conference room that had never felt so small I told them the grant had transferred.

I watched their faces do the same thing mine had done, the disbelief, the recalculation, the slow dawning understanding that everything was different now We talked for over an hour New facility Higher pay Better equipment Research expansion. Hiring The possibility of taking the work further than we had ever been able to take it.

The women who would benefit, eventually, from the treatments and therapies that proper funding would finally let us develop I sat at the head of the table and listened to my team talk about the future and somewhere in the middle of a discussion about laboratory locations I thought about Dominic pressing me against the glass while Julian moved through the crowd outside, searching, and felt the warmth of it move through me like a second heartbeat. I pushed the thought away It came back. I pushed it away again. My phone buzzed on the table.

I glanced at the screen Dominic I excused myself from the meeting. "Seraphine is in my lobby," he said when I picked up. "She has been here since this morning and she is refusing to leave Would you like to come and irritate her a little?" I looked back through the glass panel at my team, still talking, still planning, still flying. "With all pleasure," I said I told Pat I needed to go and review the contract documents with Veil Holdings. She nodded without question I took a cab straight from Helix to Veil Holdings.

I saw Seraphine the moment I walked through the lobby doors She was in the waiting area, her posture rigid, her jaw tight, the expression of a woman who had been sitting somewhere too long and was furious about it. She looked tired. She looked, for the first time in all the years I had known her like a woman who was not in control of something She saw at the same moment I saw her "Celeste I looked at her.

I saw the recognition in her eyes, the relief, the reaching out of a woman who needed an ally in a lobby where she had none I saw Seraphine, who had been my sister, who had stood beside me at my wedding who had spent six months in my husband's bed I turned and walked to the elevator I did not say a word I did not look back The elevator doors closed and I allowed myself the small, private smile I had been holding since the moment I heard her voice call my name Dominic's office was on the top floor His secretary met me at the elevator and walked me through a corridor that felt more like an art gallery than a place of work, all clean lines and carefully chosen pieces and the particular hush of serious money The office itself was large and spare and entirely him Floor to ceiling windows looking out over the city A desk that could have served as a dining table Bookshelves that had actually been read.

No clutter No performance He got up when I walked in, and looked at me and I opened my mouth to say something clever about Seraphine's face in the lobby Then his gaze moved down the length of me in that slow, thorough way and I forgot what I had been about to say He crossed the room toward me "Look at what you do to me," he said I looked down Then back up "Let me take care of that for you," I said, and started to lower myself His hand caught my arm 1 have a much better idea He walked to the door and locked it Made a call to his secretary, brief and final Not to be disturbed Then he turned back to me and went to his desk and opened a drawer He set a box on the desk and opened it atared at what was inside +15 Bonus "A gift," he said.

"I bought it for you." "I have never used one before," I said. "There is always a first time." He pushed the things on his desk to one side and took off his jacket and lifted me onto the edge of the desk and kissed me, and the clever thing I had been going to say about Seraphine dissolved completely I lay on the desk after we were both spent. He had pushed off me gently and was straightening his clothes. I sat up slowly, my legs still unsteady. and looked around for mine. The office had been tidy when I walked in.

It was slightly less tidy now I gathered my clothes from where they had ended up, and started putting myself back together He was at the desk already, moving papers back to where they belonged, restoring the order I watched him for a moment. The same controlled efficiency Like nothing had happened Like he had not just made me cry on his desk. I reached for my blouse My hand touched paper. I looked down A document Several pages, held together with a metal clip. It had been under my clothes, face down, and when I lifted my blouse it turned over in my hand I saw two names. Dominic Ford.

Ruby's writing style is bold and irresistible-perfect for those who crave intense, addictive love stories.

chapters.title: Chapter 17
chapters.content:
Chapter 017 CELESTE I stared at the document in my hand. Then I stared at him Dominic. He crossed the room and took it from me, looked at it, and smiled. Not the smirk from the stage. Something quieter than that. "We are still married," he said. "But not for much longer." "I don't understand," I said. "She signed divorce documents and you are still married?" He set the document on the desk and leaned against the edge, crossing his arms. "When I first found out about her affair with Julian, I was furious," he said. "I wanted it done immediately.

I drafted the documents that same week, signed my portion, and went to find her." He paused. "She was getting ready to go out. In a rush, distracted, already halfway out of her own mind. I told her I had something for her to sign. I told her I had already signed it and it only needed her signature." "You didn't tell her what it was?" "I wanted her to read it." His jaw shifted slightly. "I wanted her to see the words right there in front of her and question me about it. And I would have told her exactly why. Right then and there." I waited.

"She didn't read it." He let out a short, humorless laugh. "She didn't even look at it. She said she was meeting an old friend, flipped it open, signed the empty space, and walked out the door." I stared at him. "She signed divorce documents without reading them." "Without reading a single word." He picked up the document and looked at it again. "I found out later that the old friend she was in such a hurry to meet was your husband." The room was quiet for a moment. "So I kept the documents," he said. "She is out there right now believing she is the wife of a billionaire.

Very soon, I will have this processed and make sure she receives her copy." "And the settlement?" "There is no settlement. She gets nothing." His voice was flat and final. "She doesn't deserve a single penny hapter 013 +15 Bonus He set the document aside. "I have already moved out of the house we share. She has no idea. The lease runs out in a year. She can enjoy it until then." I looked at him for a long moment. "Wow," I said. "You are quite swift and efficient." I picked up the iPad from the desk.

On the screen, the lobby feed showed Seraphine still in the waiting area, her posture rigid, her foot tapping, her jaw tight with the effort of waiting for a man who had already decided she did not exist. I shook my head slowly. "But then again," I said, "in this day and age, who signs a document without reading it? Her excitement level must have been at an all time high." He chuckled. "Tell me about it." I set the iPad down. "She would have signed it even if she had read it. She always acted like she was doing you a favor by being with you." I paused.

"She must have been really blind." "And why do you say that?" he asked. I looked at him. My eyes traveled over him the way they always did when I thought he was not paying attention, which was never, because he was always paying attention. "Have you looked at yourself?" I asked. He moved toward me, slow and deliberate, stopping with his lips almost brushing mine. "What about me?" he said, his voice low. "Do you find me irresistible?" I bit my lip. "You are definitely in that category," I said. I wanted to kiss him.

I wanted to pull him back to the desk and demand a repeat of everything that had happened minutes ago, and the fact that I wanted that so badly was exactly why I stepped back and reached for my jacket instead. I began to get dressed. What was wrong with me? It was as though Dominic had unlocked something deep inside me, something I had never known was there. Was this what it meant to suddenly develop a high libido? Because that was the most generous interpretation I had for whatever was happening to my body every time this man looked at me. And he was the same way. Worse, maybe.

But he was a man. Men were naturally highly sexual. Many men That was normal and expected and nobody questioned it. 217 +15 Bonus Was it supposed to be the same with women? "Celeste." I looked up. He was watching me with that fixed, intent gaze, his eyes on mine. I changed the subject immediately. "The money dropped this morning," I said, straightening my jacket. "Before I had even signed the contract. I hadn't signed anything yet and five billion dollars just appeared in the account.

"I know." "You sent it before the contract was signed." "I trust you," he said simply "That was enough." I looked at him for a moment. Then I nodded "Get dressed," he said. "I will take you somewhere to sign the contract properly. It has already been prepared." We both stood looking at the lobby feed one last time before we left. Seraphine was still there. Still waiting. Still rigid with the particular fury of a woman who could not understand why the universe was not cooperating. I thought about how she would look at me when I walked through that lobby. She would see my jacket.

She would see my hair. She would notice, the way Seraphine always noticed everything about other women's appearances, that most of my lipstick was gone and that I had been alone with her husband in his private office for the better part of an hour. The thought almost made me smile. "We are leaving through a different route," Dominic said. I looked at him. He was already moving toward the elevator. The elevator did not go down.

It went up I watched the numbers climb and said nothing, and when the doors opened it was to a rooftop that looked out over the entire city, the skyline spread in every direction under a sky that was still blue and bright and sitting on the landing pad in the center of it was a helicopter. stopped +15 Bonus "A helicopter." "Yes." "You are taking me somewhere in a helicopter." "Is that a problem?" I looked at the helicopter. Then at him. "This is my first time." Something shifted in his expression. Not quite a smile. "Then I will make sure it is a good one" It was.

We flew over the city and then beyond it, the buildings giving way to water, the water giving way to something I had not expected An island I pressed closer to the window as we descended. The water surrounding it was the kind of blue that did not look real, deep and clear and shifting between shades in a way that made me want to keep looking. The beach below was white sand, unmarked, curving around the edge of the island in a clean arc.

The trees beyond the beach were dense and green and completely undisturbed And sitting back from the beach, half-covered by the trees, was a mansion Not the aggressive kind of mansion that announced itself from a distance and demanded to be admired. This one sat quietly in its surroundings as though it had grown there Wide and low and perfectly proportioned, all pale stone and glass, with a terrace that faced the water and large doors I could see even from the air We landed and stepped out onto the grass and I stood there for a moment just looking at it.

"Why did you bring me to an island?" I asked. "Why not?" He looked at me "It is one of my properties. "It looks nice," I said, which was the most inadequate thing I had ever said in my life. "Especially for business," he added. Here we can work without disturbance." He led me inside The interior was the opposite of what the exterior had suggested and somehow exactly right. It was simple Clean lines and high ceilings and rooms that felt large without feeling empty.

The furniture was chosen for comfort rather than display The colors were pale and natural, sand and white and the faint grey green of sea glass Every window faced the water and the light that came through them was soft and constant and changed the room slowly as the sun moved +15 Bonus It was the most beautiful house I had ever been in and it looked almost nothing like a billionaire's property, which I suspected was entirely intentional. He showed me a bedroom on the upper floor. "In case you need to sleep," he said. I looked around the room. The bed was wide and low, dressed in white linen.

The window looked directly out at the water. "I would love a bath first," I said. "Go ahead. I will work in the living room." I went to the wardrobe. His clothes. Only his clothes. I went through the rail slowly, not finding anything that would fit me, and somewhere between the dress shirts and the jackets I found myself smiling. No clothes for me here. Good. It would have been genuinely alarming if he had prepared a wardrobe on a private island for me. The closet at the hotel was already enough to think about.

I ran a bath and stayed in it longer than I needed to, listening to the sound of the water outside and trying not to think about how natural all of this felt, which was exactly the kind of thought I was not supposed to be having. When I got out I went back to the wardrobe and looked at it again. Then I took one of his white dress shirts off the hanger and put it on. It swallowed me. The shoulders dropped halfway down my arms and the hem stopped at the tops of my thighs. I rolled the sleeves up twice and looked at myself in the mirror. It would do.

He was in the living room when I came downstairs, sitting on the sofa with his laptop open, his jacket gone, wearing only a white singlet and his trousers. I stopped at the bottom of the stairs and looked at him for a moment before he heard me. The singlet The way his arms looked in it. The way he sat, relaxed and focused at the same time, his brow slightly furrowed at whatever was on his screen. I was biting my lip before I realized I was doing it I shook the thought off and walked toward him.

He heard my footsteps and looked up His eyes went immediately to my legs, to the hem of his shirt stopping at my thighs, and I watched his throat move as he swallowed. +15 Bonus I liked that. I liked it more than I should have. "You look beautiful," he said. His voice was slightly lower than it had been upstairs. "You wear it better than I do." I laughed and sat beside him. "Thank you." I leaned over and kissed his cheek, close to the corner of his mouth, and felt him go very still for a half second before he relaxed again. He picked up a folder from the table and handed it to me.

I opened it. The contract. All the terms laid out cleanly, the investment structure, the conditions, the timeline. I read through it carefully, every clause, every paragraph, taking my time It was fair. More than fair. It was the kind of contract that protected Helix rather than extracting from it, that gave us the funding without surrendering control of the research direction I looked up at him. "This is good," I said. "I know I signed it. He signed his portion.

We looked at each other across the table with the signed contract between us and something settled in the room, something that felt like the end of one thing and the beginning of something else. He moved closer He kissed me, soft and unhurried, his hand coming up to the side of my face. When he pulled back he looked at me with that quiet, intent expression. "Stay tonight," he said My heart picked up We were getting too close. That was the thought that moved through me before anything else.

Too close, too comfortable, too easy together in a way that had nothing to do with the game we were supposed to be playing I did not answer He moved closer and kissed me again, slower this time A sound came from the direction of the front door We both stopped +15 Bonus We both looked. "What was that?" I said. He was already still, his head turned toward the door, listening. Something had changed in his face. The ease was gone. "The pilot went out for a run," he said, his voice low and careful "We are not supposed to have company He stood up. "I will check" I watched him cross the room.

He moved differently now, quieter, more deliberate He reached the door and put his hand on it. He opened it. The sound was sharp and immediate and wrong Shots I heard them before I understood what they were, a crack and then another, and then Dominic was spinning away from the door and dropping to the floor beside it, his back against the wall, his hand going to his arm. Blood I saw the blood on his arm and I was already moving, already across the room and on my knees beside him before I had made the decision to move. "What is going on?" My voice came out high and strange.

chapters.title: Chapter 18
chapters.content:
Chapter 018 CELESTE The shots kept coming. Each one hit somewhere outside and I flinched at every single one, my back pressed against the wall beside Dominic, my heart doing something violent and irregular in my chest. "Why would anyone want you dead?" I asked. He did not answer immediately. He was looking at the door, listening, calculating something I could not see. "Dominic." "It is a long story," he said. Another shot. I flinched again. "What do we do?" I asked. He looked at me. "Come with me." He took my hand and moved.

We went fast, through the corridor that ran along the left side of the house, away from the front door and the sound of the shots. He snatched his phone from the table as we passed it without breaking stride. We reached a door at the end of the corridor, plain and unremarkable, and he pressed a button set into the wall beside it. The door clicked open. We went inside and he locked it behind us. I stood in the middle of the room, panting, and looked around. A bedroom. A completely normal bedroom.

Wide bed with clean white linen, two nightstands, a lamp, a wardrobe, a window on the far wall looking out at the water. The window was shut tight, the glass thick in a way that ordinary glass was not. "Your bedroom too?" I said. "Everything in here is bulletproof." He was already at a monitor mounted on the wall, picking up a remote from the dresser. "The glass, the walls, the door. Do not worry. We are safe in here for now." He pressed a button and the monitor came on. I looked at the screen and my stomach dropped.

The feed was split into sections, each one showing a different angle of the island's exterior. And on 1/5 +15 Bonus every single feed there were men. Armed, moving through the trees, taking positions at the edges of the property. I counted quickly and lost count. He was already on the phone. "Sparrow." His voice had changed. All the ease was gone, all the warmth. What was left was something cold and precise. "We have a situation at the island. Someone's trying to kill me. I need you to move." A voice on the other end, sharp and clipped.

"How many men?" He looked at the monitor, his eyes moving across each feed with the systematic efficiency of someone who had done this before. "More than ten," he said. I stared at the screen. More than ten armed men on a private island, shooting at a house I was standing in, and Dominic was on the phone with someone named Sparrow discussing it the way other people discussed traffic. The call ended. "Who is Sparrow?" I asked. "The head of my security detail." He set the phone down. "He handles the difficult situations." "Difficult situations," I repeated.

"You mean like this." "Among other things." He looked at me. "Sparrow is a dangerous man. He is very good at what he does. Do not worry, Celeste. You are my ally. You are safe." I looked at him. Then I looked at the monitor, at the armed men moving through the trees outside this bulletproof room on this private island, and I thought about the fact that three hours ago I had been in a cab on my way to Helix Research to celebrate a funding announcement. What kind of man was Dominic Ford? What had I walked into? We sat on the edge of the bed and waited.

The shots continued outside, distant and muffled through the bulletproof walls, and every time one sounded I felt my shoulders go up toward my ears. Dominic sat beside me, still and quiet, watching the monitor with that expression that gave nothing away. My heart would not slow down. He must have seen it on my face because he said, "Don't worry," and put his arm around me and pulled me into his side 215 +15 Bonus I let him. I was not too proud to admit that his arm around me was the only thing keeping my breathing even. Then I saw his arm.

The wound from the shot that had grazed him at the door, which I had been so frightened that I had almost forgotten about. The makeshift pressure I had applied earlier had not been enough. The blood had spread. "Is there a first aid box in here?" I asked. He pointed to the wardrobe. I got up and found it on the lower shelf, white with a red cross, fully stocked. I brought it back and sat in front of him and opened it and began to work. He was quiet while I cleaned the wound.

I focused on my hands, on the task, on doing it correctly, and tried not to look at the injury directly because every time I did something cold moved through me that I did not want to examine too closely. What if it had not been his arm? What if it had been his head, or his neck, or his chest? What if he had opened that door half a second sooner or been standing half a step to the left? What if the shot had not grazed him but gone straight through? I shuddered. I pressed the gauze carefully against the wound and taped it down and sat back and looked at my work.

And then, because I was apparently incapable of staying on task, my eyes traveled up his arm. To his shoulder. To the bicep that the singlet did nothing to hide. To the architecture of him, the muscle and the line of it, the way he was built in a way that suggested the body was not decorative but functional. He is jacked, I thought, with absolutely no dignity whatsoever. Such strong arms. So incredibly, unfairly sexy. "Hey." His voice, quiet and close. "Are you okay?" I blinked. He was watching me with that careful attention, his eyes on my face.

"I'm worried about you," I said, after a pause that was slightly too long. He studied me. "Why?" "Well." I stopped. Started again. "I don't know. Shouldn't I be worried about you?" He looked at me for a moment. Then his other arm came around my waist and he pulled me close, his lips near my temple. "Where were we," he murmured, "before we were so rudely interrupted?" 315 +15 Bonus I pulled back and slapped his arm. Not the injured one. "Stop it." He kissed me anyway. And then the sound changed. It was not a single shot this time.

It was everything at once, a full exchange of gunfire that filled the air from every direction, so loud and so close that I felt it in my chest. My eyes went wide. My hands went to his arms without thinking. He moved before I could process it, both his hands coming up to cover my ears, holding them gently but firmly, his eyes on mine. I looked at him. He looked at me. His hands were warm against the sides of my head and the sound was reduced to a muffled roar and his eyes were steady and I focused on them the way you focus on a fixed point when the ground is moving under you.

The minutes passed. And then, gradually, the sound faded. It stopped. Complete silence. "It is over," he said, dropping his hands from my ears. "It is over now." I let out a breath I had been holding for what felt like the last ten minutes. His phone rang. He answered it, listened, said, "Okay," and hung up. He stood. "I need to go and speak with Sparrow." "Now? Out there?" "It is safe now." He looked at me. "Stay here." He left I stayed in the bulletproof bedroom for approximately two minutes before I got up.

I went carefully, the way you move when you are not entirely sure the danger is over even though someone you trust told you it was. I came out of the corridor and went upstairs to the room where I had bathed, the white shirt of his still on my body, and I found my bag on the chair where I had left it. I took out my phone 4/5 +15 Bonus I had put it on silent before we left Dominic's office and I had not looked at it since. The screen showed missed calls stacked on top of each other. Julian. Pat. Julian again. Seraphine. Julian. A number I did not recognize. Seraphine again.

I scrolled through them. Then I saw the voicemail notification. I pressed play and lifted the phone to my ear. Seraphine's voice came through. "Listen to me and listen well." Her voice was very calm. The particular calm of someone who was holding something much less calm underneath it. "I don't know what game you are playing. But I am warning you. Stay away from my husband. Otherwise, I will destroy you." The message ended.

chapters.title: Chapter 19
chapters.content:
Chapter 019 CELESTE I sat on the edge of the bed and stared at my phone. Julian had sent text messages. "Where are you, baby. I'm worried." "Please call me when you get this." "I miss you so much. You are the love of my life." "Please just let me know you are safe." I read them one by one and felt nothing except a mild, distant irritation, the way you feel about a noise that has been going on too long. I rolled my eyes and put the phone face down on the bed. Then I picked it back up and scrolled to my mother's name. She answered on the second ring.

"Celeste." Her voice was warm and immediate, the voice she had used my entire life, the one that made me feel twelve years old in the best possible way. "My daughter. A millionaire. I always knew you had big dreams and I always knew you would fulfill them." I laughed. "Mom." "Don't Mom me. I am allowed to be proud. Your father is so proud too." A pause. "Where are you? I feel like I haven't seen your face in so long." "I know. I'm sorry. I've been so busy, especially now with trying to set up the lab at the new location.

Everything is moving so fast." "You will come and visit?" "Next week," I promised. "I will come next week." "I will hold you to that promise, Celeste." "I know you will." After the call ended I sat there for a moment with the phone in my hand and felt the warmth of her voice settle somewhere in my chest. Then I scrolled to my brother. He picked up immediately "There she is," he said "The woman of the hour. I saw you on the news. On a stage with the richest man in the country My sister" 1:7 -15 800s "Stop," I told him, but I was smiling. "I'm serious. Congratulations, Celeste Genuinely.

You worked for this." "Thank you." There was a pause. Then, "Was that Seraphine's husband? The chairman. Dominic Ford. The name and the face, it's definitely him, isn't it. Sera's husband." I went still for a half second. I had almost forgotten. My brother had carried a quiet thing for Sera years ago, back when the three of us were still in university and the world was smaller and simpler. Sera had never looked at him twice. When she eventually married, he had moved on and never mentioned it again. I had not realized he still kept tabs on her life closely enough to know her husband's face.

"It doesn't matter," I said carefully "My lab got the funding. That's what's important." "You're right, you're right. Congratulations again. Another pause "How is Sera doing these days? I looked at my phone screen for a moment I thought about the voicemail I had just listened to Sera's calm, threatening voice Stay away from my husband Otherwise I will destroy you. My lips curved up slowly "Why," I replied without missing a beat. "Of course my best friend is doing perfectly well After the call ended, I was still pacing the room when the door opened and Dominic walked in. I stopped.

I looked at him, checking automatically, the way I had been doing since the shots, looking for new damage, new blood, anything wrong He looked intact Tired around the eyes but intact Something unknotted in my chest that I had not realized was knotted. "Sparrow will take us back to the hotel," he told me I nodded Then I stopped "Wait The hotel with the glass room?" 'Yes' Okay I pulled out my phone and held it out toward him.

"You should listen to this first He took the phone I pressed play and watched his face as Seraphine's voice came through He listened to the whole thing without expression Then he handed the phone back and chuckled "Interesting What would you like me to do? +15 Bonus "Nothing yet." I took the phone back. "I can handle Seraphine. I'll keep you posted if she does more than leave voicemails." He nodded. Then his expression shifted, the ease going out of it, replaced by something more careful. "Sit down," he said. "There is something you need to know." We both sat.

He was quiet for a moment, the way he got when he was choosing his words rather than just producing them. "Sparrow thinks the attack today was not something to take lightly," he began. "In the past, there were many men who tried to take my father's company. After my parents were killed, they came for me too. Sparrow handled them, one by one. That is why I stayed hidden all these years. I could not surface until they were all dealt with." "But someone got through?" I pressed. "Not really. The son of one of them." He looked at his hands briefly, then back at me.

"Sparrow believes he has been waiting. Watching. And now that I have shown my face publicly for the first time, he has made his move." I sat with that for a moment. "So what happens now?" I asked. "What measures?" "I will need to appear less in public until the threat is neutralized." He paused. "And we will need to stay away from each other for now." I looked at him. "If the enemy saw you with me today, he would likely assume it was coincidence," he continued. Unfortunate timing. But if he saw you with me repeatedly, he would realize you are important to me.

I cannot put you in danger." Hearing this, something moved in my chest that I did not have a name for and was not ready to look at directly. Important to me. Was I really important to him? And somehow I was standing here with nothing to say while she looked at me like I was the one who had done something wrong. She turned away from me and walked to the wardrobe and began pulling out her pajamas. Calmly. Like the conversation was finished. Like I was finished. "Celeste." My voice came out rough.

"I am not done talking to you." She stepped into her pajama bottoms and pulled the top over her head and ran her fingers through her wet hair. Then she turned and looked at me with those flat, unbothered eyes. "By the way," she said, "if you must know, the ice cream I had earlier is what stained the dress." I stared at her. "Ice cream?" She did not answer. She picked up her phone from the nightstand and walked out of the bedroom. I stood there 215 +15 Bonus The dress was still on the floor between us. I looked at it for a moment. Then I picked it up. I brought it close.

I touched the stain with my finger. I smelled it. Then I touched it to my tongue. I spat immediately, the taste hitting the back of my throat, and I stood in the middle of my bedroom and stared at the dress and felt something cold and certain settle in my chest like a stone dropping into still water. That was not ice cream. I knew what ice cream tasted like. I knew what this was. And she knew exactly what this was. And she had looked me in the eye without flinching and said ice cream and walked out of the room. My wife. My Celeste. The woman I had built my entire life around.

The woman I had chosen above everyone else. The woman I had controlled and shaped and kept and protected and loved in the only way I knew how to love, which 1 was completely and without question and with the absolute certainty that she would never, not in a million years, do to me what I had done to her. I dropped the dress. I walked out of the bedroom. She was in the living room. Standing in front of Seraphine with both of Seraphine's hands held in hers, her voice soft and warm, her expression open and kind. "I am sorry for slapping you," she was saying. "It was not intentional. Pure reflex.

I walked into my own home and your hand came at my face and my body reacted before my mind could catch up." She squeezed Seraphine's hands gently. "You know I am not a violent person. But I will never allow anyone to raise a hand to me. Not even you." I moved closer. "Wait." They both looked at me. You slapped my wife?" I turned to Seraphine. My voice came out harder than I intended. "You put your hands on her?" When I had seen Celeste slapping Seraphine earlier, I had not stopped to think about who started it. The anger about the dress had been too loud.

But now I was looking at the faint redness along Celeste's jaw 3.5 +15 Bonus and understanding the sequence of events and feeling a different kind of rage start to climb. "It is true," Celeste said quietly. "Seraphine slapped me first. But I am sure she did not mean it. She was probably upset about something." I looked at Seraphine. She looked back at me. Before she could speak I raised my hand and slapped her. The force knocked her sideways and she hit the floor with a yelp, her hand flying to her face. "Julian!" Celeste shoved me, both palms flat against my chest, pushing me back a step.

"How can you raise your hand to my best friend? Forgetting everything else, Sera is a woman. And her husband is my benefactor. How could you?" "She hit you first," I shot back. "That is not the point." She turned away from me and knelt beside Seraphine, helping her up from the floor, her hands gentle. "I am so sorry," she said, guiding her back to the sofa. "Are you okay?" There was blood at the corner of Seraphine's mouth. Celeste reached for a tissue and dabbed at it carefully. "I want to thank you," Celeste said, her voice full and warm. "I know you must have spoken to your husband.

Put in a good word for me." She shook her head like she was still absorbing something wonderful. "You are a true friend, Seraphine. All this time you never once mentioned that your husband was the richest man in the country. You just quietly went ahead and convinced him to invest five billion dollars into my small lab." She squeezed Seraphine's hand. "What would I do without you?" I watched this. I watched every word of it. And I knew. I knew Seraphine had not convinced her husband of anything. Seraphine had not known who her husband was any more than the rest of us had.

The idea of Seraphine quietly pulling strings for Celeste out of friendship and generosity was so far from the Seraphine I knew that it might as well have been a fairy tale. But Celeste was saying it with such warmth and such sincerity that for one half second I almost wondered if I was wrong. I watched Seraphine's face go through several things in quick succession. The surprise. The calculation. Something hardening behind her eyes. She pushed Celeste's hands away.

The past few days, I have been at my mother's place. She has been sick. I turned off my phone so I could care for her properly." I nodded slowly, letting her continue. "My husband could not get through to me," she pressed on. "He thought I was still with Helix Research Laboratory. That is why he pumped five billion into it. That money was actually meant for Ford Biosciences. For me. I want you to return it. In turn, Ford Biosciences will collaborate with Helix. We will make sure you also benefit from the funding." I let out a sigh and nodded.

"You make a good point." I walked to the armchair and sat down. I crossed my legs too, tapped my chin, and pretended to think. Every dime leaving that account would have to be discussed with the team. I cannot just move the money on my own. That could land me in jail.

It would be considered criminal." Sera chuckled. "No one at Helix would dare get you arrested. First of all, your husband is Julian, the amazing millionaire." He wanted you to have your own space. Your own name on the door. Ford Biosciences. And that was why he got you a space that was five times the square footage of Helix Research Laboratory." I paused and let that sit "So what exactly happened?" I went on. "Initially, I thought maybe your husband felt guilty that he separated you from us after so many years and opened a much better lab for you.

I also thought you put in a good word for us out of love and that was why your husband funded our research." I tilted my head and looked her straight in the eye. I do not want to be guilty of holding back your money if the five billion was initially meant for Ford Biosciences." Sera gritted her teeth. "Yes. My husband, Dominic Ford, is forgetful. He made a mistake." I tilted my head. "Did your husband say that?" "He is my husband," Sera snapped. "I know him. I know how he thinks. I know exactly when he has made a mistake." I sighed. "But if it was because your husband forgot he had opened a new lab for you, how come your name did not reflect in the contract that was signed?" She raised her brows. I ignored her expression and pressed on.

"I signed the contract earlier today. Under the space where the lab owners should be, only my name and Pat's name were mentioned. I did not see your name anywhere. "I looked at her steadily. "Could your husband have forgotten your name as well? Since you say he is a forgetful man?" "Enough!" Sera's voice came out loud and sharp. "You are being greedy. You just want to keep all the money." I put my hand over my chest, feigning an aggrieved expression. "How can you say such a thing about me, Sera? I am your best friend.

I just want to understand what is going on." She waved her hand dismissively. "It does not matter. Keep the money. But I need to find out one thing." She locked her eyes on mine. I reached into my pocket, pulled out my new phone, and handed it to Julian. He stared at it in surprise. "Whose phone is this?" "Mine," I replied. I took a deep breath and launched into the story I had prepared.

"I was at home when a courier delivered a parcel to me. It was an invitation to a party. I would not have gone, but the name of the recipient was Helix Research Laboratory. How could I ignore that?" When it was time, I went to the party, got the shock of my life when I was called on stage and Helix received that funding." I paused and looked at Julian. "I did not even know you were there. You told me you were traveling out for business." Something flickered across his face. Guilt, maybe. I did not care. "The whole crowd and glamour got to me. I had to flee the scene. I am not used to such attention. I quietly exchanged clothes with a random waitress and left the hotel." I let out a shaky breath. "I was so excited by the funding. I had not been to the lab in a while, so I decided to go there. When I arrived, I realized I had lost my phone. I could not remember how or when I just lost it. Chapter 025 DOMINIC

I drove back to the hotel, lay on my bed, and gazed at the ceiling. The room was serene, as was the city outside. There was no logical explanation for my wakefulness, yet I remained so. Thoughts of her persisted. Not in an irritating manner, nor like an unresolved issue nagging at me. She reappeared like a melody or a fragrance, unbidden and all-encompassing, making everything else seem slightly less tangible.

Her gaze lingered in my mind, the way she looked at me after, still breathless, her eyes questioning without words. I chuckled softly to myself. That woman was going to be my undoing. But it wasn't solely that. It was more than that. It was the way she conversed with me in the closet when I shared about my parents, how she didn't fill the silence with unasked-for sympathy. It was how she fed me dinner nonchalantly, as if it meant nothing.

It was how she stood on that stage in the red dress, locking eyes with me across the stunned room, as if I were the sole fixed point in her world. She stirred something within me that I never thought possible. For years, I had believed that my emotions, the mild interest, controlled appreciation, and mild satisfaction, were all that a man like me could experience. Seraphine hadn't altered that. Nor had the women before her. Celeste had.

I glanced at my arm. The dressing she applied was still intact. I needed a doctor to examine it to prevent infection. The memory of her presence beside me, her careful movements and concealed fear, lingered. I had been scared too, not for myself, as I had faced danger before, but for her.

The idea of her being harmed evoked an unfamiliar protectiveness in me. I didn't want to reveal it. If she sensed my burgeoning emotions, she might withdraw. For her, this was a game, a form of retribution. I was a tool she wielded skillfully. I accepted my role but needed to ensure my feelings didn't complicate matters.

I rose from the bed, pondering the situation at her house. Julian was confirmed to be home. Seraphine's unexpected presence there was better than I could have orchestrated. Two guilt-ridden individuals and a wife biding her time. Celeste could handle herself. She had taken self-defense classes years ago, skills that wouldn't have faded entirely. But what if Julian resorted to violence?

I hesitated to call her, fearful of disrupting a crucial moment. Then I remembered the phone she had given me, keeping her new one secret from Julian. I powered up the old phone, only to power it down promptly. Respecting her privacy was paramount, regardless of my desire to ensure her safety.

I strolled to the balcony, peering out at the city, contemplating Julian. Specifically, Julian beholding Celeste in that black dress. The image of her in that dress, leaving me momentarily paralyzed, flashed vividly in my mind. The surge of rage I felt was intense, unlike anything I had experienced before.

Returning inside, I attempted to quell my concerns, reminding myself of Celeste's resilience. However, leaving her alone with Julian for two weeks seemed reckless. I contacted Sparrow, instructing him to expedite our plans.

Upon ending the call, Celeste unexpectedly rang. Her voice, a blend of fatigue and composure, reassured me. After our conversation, I relished the tranquility of the room, my mind finally at ease.

At dawn, the CEO alerted me of Seraphine's strategic move, positioning herself as the cherished wife of the influential Dominic Ford. I devised a plan, leveraging Seraphine's actions to ensnare my adversary.

I instructed Sparrow to use the press conference as bait, ensuring Seraphine's safety. Sparrow's quiet chuckle hinted at his tacit approval. I then informed the CEO to abstain from commenting on the situation, entrusting the matter to me.

As I gazed at Seraphine's confident image on my screen, I contemplated her impending revelation. The audacity of her actions intrigued me, and I awaited the unfolding events with anticipation. "Let us see," I murmured to the empty room, "if you still wish to be Mrs. Ford publicly after today."

The chandeliers alone cost more than most people's houses. The women adorned themselves with jewelry that had no price tags; if you needed to ask, you couldn't afford it. The men exuded an air of ownership, not only of the room but everything beyond it. And there she was, on Julian's arm, wearing a black dress worth seven hundred thousand dollars, every bit worth its price. It was a victory.

Leslie was back in the room where Julian usually kept her between uses, while Seraphine was at the most significant party of the year, capturing attention with every move she made. He was asleep on his back, one arm across his stomach, the sheet pulled to his waist. In sleep he looked different. The controlled stillness he carried when he was awake became something softer, something unguarded. His jaw was relaxed.

His breathing was slow and even. He looked like an angel who had appeared in my life from nowhere. I looked away. That was exactly the kind of thinking I could not afford. I knew better. I had told myself I knew better, and then I had spent the night in his bed, and now I was lying here at five in the morning watching him sleep and thinking about angels. I needed to be careful. A game with rules and an end date and no room for the kind of soft, stupid feelings that got women like me hurt.

I was not going to get hurt. I got up slowly, careful not to disturb him, and padded across the room to where my phone was charging on the kitchen counter. The screen lit up. Fourteen missed calls from Seraphine. Eight from Julian. Two from my mother. One from my brother. I stared at the screen for a moment. Then I set it back down and went to shower. The bathroom was warm and quiet, the marble still faintly steamed from the night before.

"Eventually it became enough of a bother that I turned 2/4 +15 Bonus off my phone." "Smart" I paused at the door to the private exit. What was wrong with me.

I had a full day ahead of me, a lab full of people waiting, a funding announcement that had apparently made national news overnight, two family members I needed to call back, and I was standing at a door I should already be through, hesitating. I will call you later, I promise.

The news coverage must have reached them overnight, my name and my lab's name attached to Dominic's announcement, the Veil Holdings grant, five billion dollars flowing toward reproductive research.
