I was just quiet, listening to the sound of him breathing.

Then I hung up and deleted the call history. I drew the covers up, exhaustion taking over. I yawned and felt my eyelids grow heavy. I drifted off to sleep with the ghost of his voice still in my ear. +15 Bonus It was late into the night when I felt something on my skin. Warmth. Pressure. A mouth on my breast. I smiled at first. I bit my lower lip, my body responding before my brain caught up. My mind went somewhere warm and familiar, a glass room, dark eyes, hands that knew exactly what they were doing, and I let out a soft moan. Then my eyes flew open.

Julian was crouched over me in the dim light of the bedroom, wearing only his briefs. He had pushed off my pajama top and his lips circled one of my nipples while his hand worked my other breast. I jerked backward so fast I hit my head on the headboard. "Relax. It is me," he said calmly. A loving smile spread across his face. Desire flickered in his eyes. I stared at him in disgust. My heart pounded against my ribs. "I have missed you so much, baby," he murmured, moving closer. His hands reached for me again.

chapters.title: Chapter 62
chapters.content:
Chapter 62 DOMINIC I drove back to the hotel, lay on my bed and stared at the ceiling. The room was quiet. The city outside was quiet There was no reason for me to still be awake. I was still awake. She kept coming back. Not in the way that annoyed me, not the way a problem returns when you have not solved it. She came back the way a song does, the way a smell does, without warning and without permission and with a completeness that made everything else feel slightly less real. The office. The table.

The way she had looked at me afterward, still catching her breath, her eyes asking a question she had not put into words yet. The car. I laughed quietly at the ceiling. That woman was going to be the end of me. But it was not only that. It was not even mostly that. It was the way she had talked to me in the closet when I told her about my parents, the way she had not filled the silence with sympathy I did not ask for. It was the way she had fed me dinner with a straight face and pretended it meant nothing.

It was the way she had stood on that stage in the red dress and looked at me across the whole shocked room like I was the only fixed point in it. She excited me in a way I did not believe was possible. I had spent years believing that what I felt for most things, the low-grade interest, the mild satisfaction, the controlled appreciation, was simply what feeling things felt like for a man like me. Seraphine had not changed that. The women before Seraphine had not changed it either. Celeste had. I turned my head and looked at my arm. The dressing she had applied was still intact.

I needed a doctor to look at it, just to be safe. Infection was a real risk and I was not interested in being taken out by something as undignified as an untreated graze wound. I thought about her face when she had stayed beside me in that room. The way her hands had moved, careful and focused. The way she had tried not to let me see that she was frightened. I had been frightened too. Not for myself. I had been in dangerous situations before. My body knew how to respond to danger and it had responded without asking my permission. I had been frightened for her.

The thought of her being hurt had done something to me that I was not prepared for. I had not wanted to show it. If she sensed too much from me, if she felt the weight of what I was starting to feel, she might pull back. For her this was a game. A revenge. A delicious, satisfying reversal of everything that had been done to her. I was a tool she had chosen well and was using effectively I was fine with being the tool. I just needed to make sure the tool did not develop feelings that complicated the arrangement. I sat up and swung my legs off the bed. What was happening at her house right now?

My sources had confirmed Julian was home. Seraphine had been there too, which I had not planned for but which was, honestly, 1/2 Chapter +15 Bonus better than anything I could have arranged. Two people with guilty consciences and one wife who knew exactly what they had done and was choosing her moment. Celeste could handle herself When I had done my research on her, I had found that she had taken self-defense classes as a teenager. Years ago, yes, but those things did not entirely leave the body. Still. What if Julian decided to use his hands instead of his words? What if he hurt her?

I reached for my phone before I finished the thought. Then I stopped. What if my call came at exactly the wrong moment? What if she was in the middle of something and her phone rang and Julian saw my name? I set the phone back down. Then I remembered she had given me her old phone. She had turned it off before handing it over and told me she had gotten a new one. I had asked why and she had laughed and said she did it for the fun of it, for the thrill of having a second phone that Julian did not know existed, for the pleasure of operating on a frequency he could not tune into.

chapters.title: Chapter 63
chapters.content:
Chapter 63 I picked up her old phone and turned it on. Then I turned it off again. It was not right. Whatever was on that phone was hers. Her messages. Her history. Her private life before all of this. I had no business going through it regardless of how much wanted to know she was safe. I put it down. Stood up. Walked to the balcony and stood in the night air and looked out at the city and thought about Julian. Specifically, I thought about Julian looking at Celeste in that black dress.

She had come out of the wardrobe and she had been wearing it and I had felt the entire functioning of my brain temporarily suspend. And she had gone home in it. Walking through that front door in it, with her heels clicking and her hips doing what they did, and Julian was going to see her. Julian, who still believed she was his. The rage that moved through me was disproportionate and I knew it was disproportionate and I stood on the balcony and breathed through it. I had barely blinked when Seraphine started sleeping with Julian. I had been hurt, yes. I had been angry. But not like this.

Not this particular heat that had no good name for itself and did not respond to reason. I went back inside. I lay down. I told myself that worrying accomplished nothing. That Celeste was a grown woman who had survived two years in a marriage to a man like Julian and had come out of it not broken but sharpened. That she knew what she was doing. That she had a plan and she was executing it and she did not need me pacing hotel rooms on her behalf. I closed my eyes. Then I sat up again. One to two weeks away from her.

That had been my assessment of the situation and I stood by it as a tactical decision. But I had made the assessment before I had properly considered something. Celeste, before all of this, had been a woman who dressed the way her husband told her to and went where her husband told her to and wanted what her husband approved of wanting. That woman had a particular kind of containment built into her, a lid on everything. That lid was off now. I had helped take it off. And now I was proposing to leave her alone in a house with Julian for two weeks.

Julian, who had presumably noticed that something had shifted in his wife. Julian, who was not a stupid man. Julian, who would do whatever it took to keep what he believed was his. If he turned that attention toward her. If he found the right moment. If Celeste, who had been in love with this man for years, found herself weakening in a moment of vulnerability or exhaustion or loneliness. Chapter +15 Bonus 1 got off the bed, picked up tny phone, and called Sparrow. He answered on the second ring. "Boss." "Where are we on the attack?" Tasked. "Still working on a location.

We're close but not there yet." "You have three days." Silence on the other end. Then, "Three days is not a lot of time for something like this." "I cannot spare a week or two," I told him. "With respect," Sparrow said carefully, "you have stayed hidden for years when the situation called for it. What is two weeks compared to that?" I sat with that for a moment. Then I said, "I cannot stay away from her for two weeks." He paused for a moment. "Who are we talking about here?" Sparrow asked. "Your wife, or the woman you fucked in the car?" "I already told you," I said, my voice going flat.

"I do not have a wife anymore. Do not bring up that whore's name unless it is absolutely necessary." "My apologies," he said quietly. "It will not happen again. But I do need to know who you mean." I exhaled. "Yes. The woman from the car." He paused for longer this time. "That is easy enough to solve," He responded finally, and I could hear the smile in it even though he would never actually smile while we were discussing operational matters. "I can get you to her in disguise. Handyman. Delivery guy. Plumber. No one would know.

chapters.title: Chapter 64
chapters.content:
Chapter 64 "What would | do without you?" "Just doing my job, boss," he returned. After the call ended, | lay there feeling significantly less like the walls were closing in. Then her call came through, as though she had somehow known | needed to hear her voice. | picked up before the first ring had finished. We talked. She sounded tired and unbothered in equal measure, which meant she was fine, which meant whatever had happened in that house she had handled. After she hung up | lay there in the dark and felt the particular quiet of a room that had just had something good in it. I slept.

The CEO called at seven in the morning. "Check the trending news, Sir," he said, without greeting. "Number one. Right now." | reached for my phone and opened the app. Seraphine's face looked back at me from approximately thirty different angles across the top of my feed. | sat up and read. Mrs. Seraphine Ford, scientist and founder of Ford Biosciences and wife of the country's richest billionaire and chairman of Veil Holdings, Dominic Ford, is set to hold a press conference at two this afternoon.

She aims to answer questions about her marriage, how she and her husband met and fell in love, and how he grew to become the number one billionaire in the country. 5 I scrolled to her personal page. She had posted it herself. With a picture. Professionally taken, which meant she had planned this in advance. She was wearing the black dress from the party, and she was smiling the smile of a woman who believed she had already won. | put the phone down. "Seraphine," | said to the empty room. "Desperate much? It was almost impressive.

| had just revealed my face to the public for the first time, and she had taken a few hours to pivot from hiding on Julian's arm to positioning herself as the beloved wife of the country's most powerful man. She was claiming territory she had already signed away, in a document she had not even read, in front of an audience of millions. 2 | had to give it to her. The audacity was extraordinary. My expression relaxed and | smiled slowly. "Who told you that you were allowed to be Mrs. Ford in public, without my consent? + Sparrow called before | had finished the thought.

"Have you seen the trending news about you-know-who? "You can say her name," | told him. "| am not going to dissolve." "Right." There was a beat. "Have you seen what Seraphine is doing?" "1have." "And?" "And we are going to let her do it," | replied. "Since she is so desperate for the public to recognize her as Mrs. Ford, let us use her." "Use her how?" Sparrow asked. "As bait." | kept my voice even. "If | am right, my enemy will see the press conference as an opportunity. He will assume | care about what happens to her.

He will make amove." 2 "You want to let the press conference happen." "| want to let everything happen naturally. With one condition." | paused. "She cannot die. | do not want her dead. Whatever happens at that press conference, she walks away from it. Injured is acceptable. Dead is not. Because it would affect Celeste." "This is for someone else?" He asked. | did not confirm it. "Use the press conference to set a trap. If we can take my enemy there, | do not have to spend two weeks pretending to be a plumber." Sparrow let out a short, quiet laugh.

It was the closest he ever came to genuine amusement. "Understood, boss. | will not fail you." After the call, | rang the CEO back. "The company makes no statement about the press conference," | told him. "No confirmation. No denial. No comment of any kind. Leave everything to me." "Understood, sir." | ended the call and looked at Seraphine's picture still on my screen. She was smiling that smile. Confident. Certain. Already counting the money she thought she was about to reclaim and the status she thought she was about to cement. | set the phone face down on the nightstand.

"Let us see," | said quietly to the empty room, "if you still want to be Mrs. Ford publicly after today."

chapters.title: Chapter 65
chapters.content:
+15 Bonus Chapter 65 CELESTE I did not let Julian touch me. The moment his hands found my waist again, moved away from him, putting the length of the bed between us. "I am exhausted," I told him. "The only thing on my mind right now is the lab expansion. I cannot think about anything else until that is where it needs to be." Julian looked at me the way he always looked at me when I was not doing what he wanted. That particular combination of confusion and displeasure that he dressed up as concern. "You know I have never liked how that lab drains you," he said.

"And the way you have been dressing lately, Celeste. You know that is not like you." "When you met me," I replied evenly, "I was dressing exactly like this. I stopped for your sake. Mostly because I was at home with nowhere to go and no reason to get dressed at all." He opened his mouth, but I kept going. "You made the decision that we would wait five years before having children. Your words. You said you wanted us to enjoy our life as a couple before third parties entered the picture. I agreed. I went on the pill. I did everything you asked." I looked at him steadily.

"But my life now feels empty, Julian. Without a career I am just here. Existing. That is not enough for me." "I provide everything you need," he said. "This is not about money." I kept my voice patient and clear, the way you speak to someone who keeps missing the point. "Your work exhausts you every single day. The contracts, the meetings, the travel. But you do not stop. Because it gives you something money cannot replace. Fulfillment. Purpose." I tilted my head slightly. "It is the same for me. I want my career. I have always wanted it. Before, I was working on a small scale.

Now, with this funding, I am ready to give everything I have to it." The displeasure on his face had settled into something harder "And the dressing?" he pressed. "I am in the spotlight now. I have cameras on me. I love looking good on camera and I love looking sexy and I am not going to apologize for that." I held his gaze. "You have to trust me. Building this lap is the only thing on my mind." He was quiet for a moment. Then he shifted, the hard line of his shoulders softening slightly, moving toward me. "Okay," he murmured. "Enough about work." He leaned in to kiss me.

I put my hand flat on his chest and pushed. "Did you not hear a single word I just said?" "What does any of that have to do with us?" he asked, his brows coming together. "I am not asking you to stop working. I am asking for my wife." "We have barely touched each other in months," I replied. "Your work kept you exhausted and unavailable and I understood that. I adjusted. I took my mind off sex completely and I focused on other things. Now I do not even remember what sex feels like." I looked at him. "All I am asking is for you to extend me the same understanding. I am exhausted.

Sex is the last thing on my mind. I want to build my lab." "We cannot live as a married couple without sex, Celeste." "We have been doing exactly that," I pointed out. "And you were the one who said our sex life would resume once you Chapter +15 Bonus completed the contract you were chasing. You have not even completed it yet. So what exactly are you saying to me right now?" His jaw tightened. He reached for the hem of my pajamas top, I stepped back. "Julian." He stepped forward. His hands found the fabric again, pulling it upward, his head dipping toward my chest. I shoved him.

chapters.title: Chapter 66
chapters.content:
Chapter 66 I did not look back. I went down the hall to the guest room, stepped inside, and turned the lock. His knock came almost immediately. Three sharp raps. I sat on the edge of the guest bed and looked at my nails. He knocked again. I said nothing. After a while, the knocking stopped. +15 Bonus I was up before him the next morning. I showered, dressed, and was in the living room when I heard him come out. He looked surprised to find me already ready, which told me he had expected to find things back to normal. Breakfast on the table. A wife who had softened overnight.

"What are we having?" he asked. I picked up my bag. "I have no idea. I stopped cooking a few days ago. You would have noticed if you had been home." He stared at me. "Hire a maid," I told him, and walked out. The day was long and full and exactly what I needed. The new lab location consumed everything. There were contractors to meet and equipment lists to approve and decisions that needed to be made immediately and decisions that could wait and Pat moving through all of it beside me with the particular energy of a woman who had been waiting years for this exact problem to have.

I drove home late, my feet aching, my mind still running through the list of everything that needed to happen before the end of the week. I opened the front door. And stopped. Suitcases in the hallway. Two of them, large, the kind people bring when they intend to stay. Julian came out of the living room and when he saw me his expression did something careful and deliberate. "My mother and sister are going to be staying with us for a few months," he announced. I looked past him into the living room. They were both there.

Julian's mother, sitting with the particular posture of a woman who has already decided she owns the room she is in. Julian's sister, standing with her arms crossed, looking at me the way she always looked at me. Like I was something stuck to the bottom of a shoe. They had never liked me. From the first time Julian brought me home, they had looked at me with that same expression, a mixture of judgment and dismissal that they did not bother to conceal. Julian had always kept them at a distance for my sake, managing them carefully, making excuses when he had to. He had stopped managing them.

I understood exactly what this was. A retaliation. A punishment dressed up as a family visit, delivered with a straight face 1/2 Chapter, +15 Bonus because Julian always delivered his punishments with a straight face and called them something else. I looked at his mother. I looked at his sister. They looked back at me with the combined glare of two women who had been waiting a long time for an opportunity exactly like this one. My phone rang. I turned away from all three of them and looked at the screen. Dominic.

I answered immediately, walking toward the far end of the hallway, my back to the room. "I will be sending a handyman to your home early tomorrow morning," he said, his voice low and even. "When he arrives, take him into your bedroom and lock the door. The message I am sending is confidential and for your eyes only. Your bedroom is the only place you can receive it privately. Can you do that?" I stood there with Julian's mother's eyes on my back and Julian's sister's silence pressing against the room and a smile pulling at the corner of my mouth that I was glad nobody could see.

Ruby's writing style is bold and irresistible-perfect for those who crave intense, addictive love stories.

chapters.title: Chapter 67
chapters.content:
Chapter 67 SERAPHINE I left that house seething. My jaw was tight the entire drive home, my hands gripping the wheel harder than necessary, replaying every single moment of that evening on a loop that would not stop. Both of them had put their hands on me. Julian, who I had knelt in front of. Who I had swallowed for. Who I had let use my body against a wall in his own living room while his wife was God knows where doing God knows what. That same Julian had slapped me hard enough to knock me to the floor, and for what? For Celeste? And Celeste. I balled my fist against the wheel.

The Celeste I had known for over a decade would never have raised her hand to me. If I had slapped her, and I admitted to myself that perhaps I should not have done it the moment she walked through the door, she would have asked me why. She would have listened. She would have apologized for whatever she thought she had done to upset me and then she would have offered me tea. That was the Celeste I knew. The woman who had looked me in the eye tonight and slapped me twice without blinking was somebody else entirely. And I did not like her. I hated her, actually. Both of them.

But Celeste more, because at least with Julian I understood the transaction. With Celeste I felt something I was not used to feeling, and it took me the full drive home to name it. I felt outmaneuvered. She had lied to my face. Beautifully. With tears and everything. The exit door story, the fainting, the ice cream. It was all constructed and delivered without a single tremor in her voice. I knew she had seen me at Veil Holdings. I had been sitting twenty feet from the elevator when she walked past me. We had made eye contact.

There was no exit door she had conveniently used that meant she had not seen me. And she knew that I knew. She had just not cared. I went round that building afterward, all the way around, looking. I had not found any alternative exit. Which meant either she had lied or she had somehow vanished through a wall. And Celeste was many things but she was not magic. I had not pushed the issue because Julian would have sided with her. The fool was so desperate to believe his wife was innocent that he would have called me a liar to my face and I was not going to give him that satisfaction.

But what Julian had said before that stuck with me. 'Dripping with another man's cum.' I sat with that phrase in the quiet of my apartment. Was he right? The Celeste I knew was pathetically faithful. She had loved Julian in that exhausting, total way that some women loved men, the kind of love that made you reshape your whole life around someone else's preferences. She had given up her clothes, her career, her independence. She had gone on the pill because he wanted to wait. She had stayed home because he preferred it.

She had done all of it without complaint because she believed he deserved it. 10 +15 Bonus That woman would not cheat. But the woman I had met tonight was not that woman. So who was she sleeping with? I thought about Dominic's company. About how long she had been in that building. About the way she had walked past me without a word, calm and unhurried, like she had every right to be there. Something cold settled in my stomach. No. I pushed the thought away before it could fully form. Celeste and Dominic was not a thought I was going to entertain. Dominic was mine.

chapters.title: Chapter 68
chapters.content:
Chapter 68 A press conference. +15 Bonus If I held a press conference as Mrs Dominic Ford, everyone would know my position. Socially, publicly, undeniably. No one could take that from me once it was out there in front of cameras and journalists and the entire country. And Dominic would have to show up. He was a public figure now. He had revealed himself. He had a reputation to maintain and a company that lived on its image. His wife holding a press conference about their marriage and him not appearing would raise questions he could not afford. He would come. He would have no choice.

I stopped pacing. "Wow, Seraphine," I said to myself quietly, a smile spreading across my face. "You are bursting with ideas today." I picked up my phone and started making calls. "༼Xou The press conference was arranged within the hour. Two in the afternoon tomorrow. A hotel ballroom with enough seats for press from every major outlet. The news would go viral by morning. I already had the perfect pictures. I posted on my social media, carefully composed, professionally photographed, the caption announcing the event and the time and the subject matter.

Then I watched the notifications begin to climb and felt some of the evening's humiliation lift off my shoulders. One problem handled. I scrolled through my contacts. Now for the other one. Kingsley Duke answered on the second ring. He was a young PhD, sharp and ambitious, somewhere in his late twenties, with the specific hunger of a man who had the qualifications and none of the opportunities. He had been trying to get into Ford Biosciences since I opened it, sending emails, making calls, turning up at industry events where he knew I would be. He wanted a position as lead research associate.

He wanted it badly enough that he had been professionally persistent for the better part of the month. "Dr. Duke," I said when he picked up. "Seraphine." His voice lifted immediately. "Are you finally giving me a chance?" "Not at Ford Biosciences," I replied. "I still have no vacancy and my entire team holds doctorates. You understand." The lift in his voice flattened. "Then why are you calling?" "Because I know somewhere better," I told him. "Helix Research Laboratory. I have connections there. With your qualifications, I can get you in as senior research associate. It is a good position.

The lab has just received significant funding and it is about to become very high profile." There was a pause. Then, with the particular excitement of a man trying not to sound too excited, "Are you serious?" "Completely." "Why would you do that for me?" Suspicion underneath the excitement. Smart man. "Because I need something in return." "What kind of something?" "There is a woman at Helix," I told him. "Her name is Pat. She is about thirty, dedicated, focused, not much of a social life 1/2 +15 Bonus outside the lab. I need you to get close to her." There was silence.

"Get close," he repeated carefully "You mean date her." "I mean whatever it naturally becomes," I said "You are an attractive man. She is a lonely woman. These things happen." "Seraphine." His voice had gone careful and flat. "That is not something I am comfortable with. It is not right." "Then I cannot help you." There was another silence. Longer. I waited. "Why Pat?" he asked finally. "What do you want from her?" "Not from her," I replied. "From the woman she is closest to. Once you are in Pat's life, information flows naturally.

That is all I need." He was quiet for long enough that I thought he might actually refuse. Then he said, "Fine. I will do it." "Good." I kept my voice warm and brisk. "You will reach out to my contact at Helix tomorrow. By afternoon you will have an invitation." After the call ended, I set my phone down and began preparing the notes for my press conference. The questions they would ask. The answers I would give. The story of how Dominic Ford and I had met and fallen in love, polished until it shone.

chapters.title: Chapter 69
chapters.content:
Chapter 69 The morning arrived bright and full of noise. +15 Bonus My social media had gone exactly as I had planned. The notifications were in the thousands. Every major outlet had picked up the story. My name was trending and Dominic's name was trending beside it and anyone in the country who had not known who I was yesterday knew who I was today. I went out and found a dress. Deep blue, fitted, the kind of cut that held everything in place and made everything look intentional. I had my hair done by the woman who always got it right, soft waves pinned back on one side.

My makeup was precise and camera-ready, a bold lip, defined eyes, the face of a woman who was exactly where she was supposed to be. I looked at myself in the mirror before I left. The hotel ballroom had been set up with rows of chairs facing a low stage. A long table on the stage, microphones, name plaques, a backdrop with the Ford Biosciences logo that I had arranged to be printed and delivered that morning.

The room was already filling when I arrived, journalists and photographers and camera operators setting up their equipment, the particular energy of a crowd that had come specifically to look at something. They looked at me when I walked in. I heard the whispers follow me to the stage. "She is beautiful." "She looks exactly like you would imagine his wife to look." "That dress." I sat down at the table and adjusted the microphone and smiled at no one in particular and felt, for the first time since that party, like myself again. I scanned the room for Dominic. He would come.

I was certain of it. The first journalist raised her hand. "Mrs. Ford, how long have you and your husband been married?" "We dated for almost two years," I told her, keeping my voice warm and practiced. "We have been marriet for almost a year now." "And how did you meet?" I smiled. This was the question I had prepared for. The one I had rehearsed until the words came out sounding like memory rather than performance. "We met in a bar," I began. "I walked in and he was already there, sitting quietly, just having a drink. The moment I came through the door he turned toward it.

And our eyes met." I paused and let the smile stay on my face for a moment. "It was the best moment of my life," I said. "Because it was the day I met the love of my life. My heart was racing and we just stood there, looking at each other, and I thought, this is the person. That memory never stops making me smile. We were just..." A figure at the back of the room caught my eye. I stopped talking. 1/2 Chapter o +15 Bonus He was tall, Dark suit. The particular way of standing in a crowd that made the crowd seem smaller than him. Dominic.

I started to rise from my chair, my mouth already opening to say his name. The gunshot split the air before I had fully stood. Something slammed into me from the side, a body, moving faster than I could process, and the floor came up hard and fast and I hit my side and the glass behind where I had been sitting exploded in a shower of fragments. The room erupted. Screaming. Running. The crash of chairs.

chapters.title: Chapter 70
chapters.content:
Chapter 70 CELESTE After the call, I turned around. Julian's mother was sitting in my living room-like she had always lived there. Julian's sister was standing by the window with her arms crossed, looking at me like I was something that had wandered in from outside and could not be removed quickly enough. Julian was watching me with the particular expression of a man who was waiting to see what I would do. I looked at him. "Can we talk? Alone?" He followed me to the bedroom. I shut the door and turned to face him. "Why did you bring them here?" I asked.

"You know exactly how they feel about me: You know what it is like when they are in the same space as me. You made me a promise, Julian." "They are my family," he said simply. "I missed them. I have every right to invite them to my own home without asking anyone's permission." "Nobody is stopping you from being close to your family," I replied. "You can visit them. You can have them over for dinner. You can spend the weekend with them. All of that is fine." I kept my voice even. "But you gave me your word that they would never live under the same roof as me. That was not a small promise.

So I am asking you again. What are they doing here?" He smiled. It was not a warm smile. "What matters," he said, "is that I want them here." "And what I want doesn't matter?" "You chose to pour all your attention into that laboratory." His voice had taken on the tone he used when he wanted to sound reasonable while saying something unreasonable. "You chose to wear clothes I have made clear I do not approve of. These are not things I wanted, Celeste. But you are doing them anyway!" He spread his hands slightly. "So let everyone do what they want.

Without caring about what the other person wants." I looked at him for a long moment. "Okay," I said. "As long as we are on the same page," he added, and walked out. The door clicked shut behind him. The frown I had been holding fell off my face. A smile replaced it. す "Oh, Julian," I murmured to the empty room. "You are making this so easy." I went to the closet and started pulling things out. Everything I actually wanted, everything I cared about keeping, I set aside and began loading into boxes. My good clothes. My shoes.

What is it?" sighed, putting just the right amount of heaviness into my voice. "It's about Celeste. Mom, I don't know what's going on with her lately. She's been acting very strange. She moved into the guest room.

She locks herself in there with men..." "With men?" "I'm not accusing her of anything, but Mom, she brought a handyman into the house today. A tall, handsome man. She locked herself in the guest room with him for over thirty minutes. My mother and sister were here. They heard things. Moaning sounds. And when I got home, there was... evidence. On the bed." There was silence on the other end. "I know Celeste isn't like that," I continued. "I know she's a good woman. But something is wrong. She's not herself. I thought you should know. Maybe you can talk to her.

Knock some sense into her." My mother-in-law's voice came back, horrified. "Celeste? My Celeste? Julian, that doesn't sound like her at all. She would never..." "I know, Mom. I know. That's why I'm worried. Something must be wrong. She's been different ever since 1/3 +15 Bonus that investment from Veil Holdings came through. The money changed her." "Oh my God. Oh my God. I'll call her right now. I'll talk some sense into her. Don't worry, Julian. I'll handle this." "Thank you, Mom. I knew I could count on you." "Of course, sweetheart. Of course. Let me call her immediately." She hung up.

I smiled down at my phone. That should do it. Celeste could ignore me all she wanted, but she couldn't ignore her mother. Not for long. I pocketed the phone and headed back into the house. I needed a shower. I needed to clear my head. The scent of that redhead was still on my skin, and I didn't want anyone asking questions. I walked into the living room and stopped. Riley was sitting on the couch, staring at her iPad with a dazed expression on her face. She looked like someone had hit her over the head with a frying pan. Her mouth was slightly open, her eyes wide, her body completely frozen.

"Earth to Riley," I said, snapping my fingers in front of her face. She blinked. Looked up at me. The shock was still written all over her face. "I don't believe it," she said. "You don't believe what?" My mother walked in from the kitchen, a dish towel in her hands. "This... this man." Riley turned the iPad around. "This is the man that just left. The man who pretended to be a handyman. How can he be a billionaire? And the richest in this city?" "What?" I snatched the iPad from her hands. Staring back at me from the screen was a face I recognized immediately. Clean-shaven. Sharp jawline.

Expensive suit. Standing at a podium with the Veil Holdings logo behind him. Dominic Ford. I scoffed. "How can this be? This is Dominic Ford. The richest billionaire in the city. Why would he sneak into my house as a handyman? Do you think Celeste can even afford to pay him?" "I'm not joking, Julian," Riley insisted. "When he first came, he had a beard on. I kept staring at his face because I found him very handsome. When he was leaving, his face looked like he'd just taken a shower. He'd taken off the beard. I was at the door.

chapters.title: Chapter 88

This is the man I saw coming out of Celeste's guest room." The words hit me like a physical blow. I shook my head. "No. No, you must be mistaken." "I'm not mistaken, Julian. I saw him clearly." My mind was spinning. Dominic Ford. The richest man in the city. Seraphine's husband. My wife's best friend's husband. He had been in my house. In Celeste's room. Alone. With the door locked. And then the memories started creeping in.

Seraphine. She'd accused Celeste of going into Dominic's office and not coming out until it was dark. I'd dismissed it as jealousy. As paranoia. As a woman drinking too much wine and letting her imagination run wild. But now... The five billion. Why would Dominic invest five billion dollars in Celeste's lab? Why not his own wife's company? What was the bargain between them? My stomach turned. No. I couldn't bear it. I couldn't stand here and think about my wife with another man. With Dominic Ford. The man who had everything.

The man who was richer, more powerful, more successful than I would ever be. I ran. Out of the living room. Out of the front door. My mother and sister called after me but I didn't hear them. I couldn't hear anything over the roaring in my ears. If there was an affair, there was one person who could confirm it. One person who would know the truth. One person who had just as much reason to want to know as I did. Seraphine. I got into my car and started the engine. I pulled out my phone and called her number. It rang twice before she picked up.

"What do you want, Julian?" Her voice was flat and unimpressed. "Are you still at the hospital?" "Who wants to know? And why?" +15 Bonus I snapped. "Don't play games with me, Sera. This isn't a game. My call concerns my wife and your husband." There was a pause. Then her voice came back, suddenly interested. "I just got home from the hospital" "I'm coming." I hung up before she could respond. I drove. Fast. Through traffic. Running red lights. None of it mattered. The only thing that mattered was getting to Seraphine's house and finding out the truth.

My phone buzzed as I pulled up to a red light. A notification. A video file from an unknown number. I frowned and opened it. The video started playing and my blood ran cold. It was me. On that bed in the VIP room. The redhead was on her knees in front of me, my cock in her mouth, her head bobbing up and down. The footage was crystal clear. High definition. Shot from somewhere in the room I hadn't noticed. A hidden camera. The video kept playing. Me fucking her tits. Me pushing her face down and pounding her pussy from behind. Her riding me. Me coming on her face. Every second of it. Recorded.

A message appeared below the video. "You have two hours to send fifty million dollars worth of Bitcoin to this wallet address. If we have not received the Bitcoin in two hours, this video will go viral and will be shared on all social media platforms. The clock is ticking." A wallet address followed. A string of letters and numbers. I stared at the screen. My hands were shaking. My heart was pounding so hard I could hear it in my ears "what the hell!" I yelled, my voice echoing inside the car. The light turned green. The car behind me honked. I didn't move.

chapters.title: Chapter 89
chapters.content:
Chapter 89 CELESTE I did not look back when I reversed out of the driveway. I had seen Julian's face through the windshield, red and furious, standing on his own front step like a man who could not understand why the world was not rearranging itself around his feelings. I had seen it and I had looked away and I had driven. The morning was bright. The city was already moving. I rolled the window down and let the air hit my face and thought about Dominic's hands and the way Julian had come flying through that gate like he had been launched. I smiled.

The man had left the house last night, and come back this morning reeking of another woman's perfume, with his eyes red and his jaw tight and the very particular energy of a man who had been doing something he was planning to deny. And he had stood in my guest room looking at evidence of my own actions and decided I was the one with explaining to do. His level of hypocrisy was genuinely impressive. Artisanal, almost. The kind of thing you had to work at. As for Elizabeth and Riley, I simply did not have the bandwidth.

They were exhausting in the specific way of people who had decided that causing problems was a personality. In any other chapter of my life I might have engaged. I might have tried, the way I had always tried, to smooth things over and find a way to make everyone comfortable at my own expense. Not anymore. The new lab had accommodation. I had already asked Pat to prepare one of the rooms. As far as Julian's family was concerned, they could have the house. I had better places to be. Which brought me to the other thing sitting in the back of my mind. The five billion.

Dominic had invested five billion dollars into my research. His reasons were his own and I was not naive enough to think it was purely altruistic, but that money was real and it was sitting in Helix's account and it was waiting to be turned into something that actually mattered. Women with endometriosis going undiagnosed for years. Unexplained infertility cases collecting dust on underfunded lab shelves.

I had spent years watching Pat keep this work alive on the budget of a small family restaurant and now we had five billion dollars and if I came out of this whole arrangement with nothing to show for it scientifically, I would never forgive myself. Dominic had his reasons. Fine. I had mine too. And speaking of Dominic. What a man. 1/2 +15 Bonus I had thought about it more than was probably healthy, and I had arrived at the conclusion that if I had married him from the beginning, even if I had believed he was completely broke, we would have had an extraordinary time.

He was the kind of man who made things interesting without trying. Who knew how to read a room and a person and decide exactly what was needed. Who showed up at your house in a fake beard with a toolbox because he missed you and made the whole absurd operation feel like the most natural thing in the world. I caught myself imagining it sometimes. Us. Together. Properly. Not this game we were playing but the real thing. Then I caught myself catching myself and snapped out of it. Unrealistic. Dumb.

We had an arrangement and arrangements had end dates and I needed to keep that clearly in view or I was going to end up in a different kind of mess entirely. I pulled into the lab car park and sat for a moment with the engine off. Dominic had taken a risk coming to the house this morning. A real risk, with his security situation, with the assassination threat, with everything Sparrow had said about keeping a low profile. He had shown up anyway in a disguise with a toolbox because he wanted to see me.

chapters.title: Chapter 90
chapters.content:
Chapter 90 Maybe he just missed me. The way I missed him, which was more than I was comfortable admitting even to myself. I got out of the car and walked toward the entrance and yawned so hard my jaw cracked. Too many orgasms on an empty stomach, it turned out, was not the ideal preparation for a full day of research. Noted. I would file that under lessons learned and absolutely not change my behavior. Pat was already inside, moving through the new space with the energy of a woman who had been waiting years for a building this size and intended to make the most of every square foot of it.

She looked up when I walked in and immediately read my face. "You need breakfast," she said. "I need breakfast," I agreed. We sat in the small kitchen area and I ate and she talked and I felt some of the morning's chaos settle. Pat had always had that effect on me. She was steady in the way that certain people were steady, not because nothing affected them but because they had decided a long time ago that falling apart was not particularly useful. I told her I was going to use one of the bedrooms for a while. Late nights, early mornings, I wanted to be close to the work.

She looked at me over her cup. "How late are we talking?" "Very late," I said. She nodded slowly. "And this has nothing to do with anything going on at home." "It has everything to do with the work," I said, which was at least partially true. She let it go. The day moved quickly after that. We had decisions to make and equipment to order and a team meeting that ran two hours over schedule because everyone had opinions and the opinions were mostly good ones. I was in the middle of signing off on a procurement list when my phone rang. My mother. I stepped out into the corridor and answered.

"Hi, Mum." "Celeste." Her voice was not the warm hello I was used to. It was careful. Worried. "Are you cheating on Julian?" 1/3 +15 Bonus I closed my eyes briefly. Of course. *Julian called," she continued. "He said you moved into the guest room. That you invited a man over. That he heard things, Celeste. And there was evidence..." "Mum," I said. She stopped. "In this whole world," I asked, "who knows me better than anyone else?" A pause. "It's me," she said quietly. "Do you think I am capable of doing something like that?" "No," she said immediately. "That's why I'm so shocked.

But Julian sounded so worried. He said the five billion was going to your head. That you were not yourself." I sighed. Julian using my mother as a weapon. Of course he was. Of course. "I will come and visit you this weekend," I told her. "We will sit down and talk properly. But I want you to know that I have not done anything wrong." Her exhale was audible and relieved. "I feel better hearing you say that. I will be waiting for you." "Get some rest, Mum. I love you." "I love you too, my darling." I ended the call and stood in the corridor for a moment. That was it.

That was the moment, if I had needed one, that confirmed everything. Julian had called my mother. Had performed the worried husband routine for her. Had used her love for me as a tool to apply pressure, exactly the way he used everything, quietly and with a smile on his face. I had been planning to take my time. To control the timing. To let things unfold at the pace I chose. I was done waiting. I called Dominic. He answered on the second ring. "I want Julian to catch us," I told him. "In the act. In person. No more hints or suggestions or evidence on bedsheets.

Chapter 91 There was a pause on the other end that lasted slightly too long. "Are you sure?" he asked. "Positive." Another pause. I frowned at the phone. "Dominic." "I hear you," he said. But something in his voice was off. Something careful and measured in a way that felt different from his usual controlled calm. I could not put my finger on it and I did not have the time to examine it properly. "We will talk about the details," he said finally. "Okay," I replied.

We ended the call and I stood there for a moment longer than necessary, the phone in my hand, thinking about the pause and what it might mean and telling myself I was definitely overthinking it. I spent the rest of the day working. By evening I was ready to go back to the house briefly, collect the things I had moved into the guest room, and bring them to the lab. I did not intend to spend another night under the same roof as Elizabeth and Riley if I could help it. I was gathering my things when Pat appeared in the doorway.

"You have a visitor," she said, with a tone that suggested she was not sure how to characterize the visit. I looked up. Seraphine was standing behind her. Pat stepped aside and Seraphine walked in. She looked like she had been through something. Her hair was done and her clothes were put together but underneath all of it she looked tired and tight and stretched thin. Pat's face opened into a smile and she moved forward and hugged her. Seraphine accepted the hug without returning it properly. "I almost died," Seraphine began, looking between the two of us. "The news was everywhere.

And neither of you called. Neither of you checked on me." Pat's face fell immediately. "Sera, I am so sorry. I have been so buried in the setup here I have not had time to look at my phone properly. I should have reached out. I am really sorry." 1/2 +15 Bonus Seraphine looked at me. I said nothing. She waited. I kept saying nothing. She exhaled sharply and looked away. Then she squared her shoulders and turned back to me with the expression of a woman who had come here for a specific reason and was not leaving without it. "I need a favor," she said. "I have not been able to reach my husband.

I do not know why. I need you to contact him for me, Celeste." I looked at her for a moment. Then I smiled. "Okay. But how exactly would I be able to reach your husband when you cannot?" "You have a partnership with Veil Holdings," she said. "You can use official channels. The CEO, the office line, whatever it takes." Her voice shifted slightly, taking on the particular tone she used when she was trying to make something sound reasonable that was not. "This is really important to me, Celeste. My husband invested in this lab.

The least you can do is help me reach him." I opened my mouth to speak. "This does seem serious," Pat said, stepping in before I could respond. She was looking at Seraphine with genuine concern, the concern of a woman who had been friends with her for years and had not yet updated her files. "Let's try reaching her husband through the official Veil Holdings channels, Celeste. It cannot hurt." I looked at Pat. Then I looked at Seraphine, who was watching me with the carefully arranged expression of a woman waiting to see which way the wind was blowing.

"No matter what it takes, find them." The men hurried out, spreading to search the surrounding area. I stayed in the apartment, staring at the bracelet, my mind spinning. Then my phone rang. I looked at the screen. Private number.

I let it ring. Once. Twice. Three times. Finally, with no other choice, I answered. "Hello, Julian. Did you miss me?" Her voice. That same playful, teasing tone from last night. Scarlett. I gritted my teeth. "I should have known." "Oh, shut up and listen to me. Your two hours have elapsed. And you should have just sent the money quietly. But you had to act like a hero and come after me, didn't you?" "Where are you?" "That's not important. What's important is that there's a punishment for your little stunt. Since the two hours elapsed and you didn't send the money, the price just doubled.

One hundred million dollars. Send it to the same wallet address. You have ten minutes." "Ten minutes?" "And I promise you, if in ten minutes that money doesn't drop, your video is going to be all over social media. Every platform. Every site. Your wife. Your family. Everyone will see it. This is the last time you hear from me. Goodbye." "Hold on. Hold on. Wait.. She hung up. I stared at my phone. One hundred million dollars. Ten minutes. I screamed. The sound tore out of my throat, raw and furious. I punched the wall, my knuckles cracking against the drywall, leaving a dent.

chapters.title: Chapter 95
chapters.content:
Chapter 95 SERAPHINE The ceiling tiles of St. Catherine's Private Wing had exactly forty-three hairline cracks. I counted them twelve times between the moment I woke up and the moment I finally accepted that Dominic was not coming. Fifteen hours. That's how long I lay in that hospital bed, waiting for him. Fifteen hours of nurses checking my vitals, of doctors telling me how lucky I was, of reporters camped outside the entrance hoping to catch a glimpse of the wife of the richest man in the city. I remembered everything. The press conference. The questions.

The flash of movement in my peripheral vision. The crack of the gunshot that arrived a full second after the bullet had already torn through me. And I remembered him. The hands that grabbed me. The body that covered mine. The voice that shouted for help. Dominic He pulled me down. He saved my life. I knew it the way I knew my own heartbeat. No one else would have moved that fast. No one else would have cared enough. But if he cared, why wasn't he here? The nurse came in at six AM. She had a clipboard and a practiced smile that didn't reach her eyes. "Good morning, Mrs. Ford.

How are you feeling today?" "Like someone shot me." She laughed like I'd made a joke. I hadn't. "Your vitals look excellent. The bullet passed clean through. No major damage. You're cleared for discharge whenever you're ready." "And my husband?" Her smile flickered. "I'm sorry?" "Has my husband called? Left a message? Sent someone?" She looked at her clipboard like it might save her. "I don't have any record of..." "Forget it." I turned my face to the window. The sky was gray. The city looked like it always looked. Indifferent. I signed myself out at nine AM. No car. No driver.

No one to pick me up because I hadn't told anyone I was being discharged. 1/4 +15 Bonus I called an Uber like a peasant. The ride home was twenty minutes of silence. I watched the city scroll past the window and tried not to think about the fact that my husband had not called. Had not texted. Had not sent so much as a single flower to my room. When I walked through the front door of our house, the silence hit me like a wall. No Dominic. No note. No sign that anyone had been here at all. 1 I stood in the living room and I let myself feel it. The emptiness. The rejection.

The cold, hard truth that the man I married was avoiding me. And then I got angry. Julian showed up an hour later. I still hadn't eaten. Still hadn't showered. I looked like hell and I didn't care. "What do you want?" I asked the moment I opened the door. He looked rough too. Dark circles. Tension in his jaw. Whatever was eating him, it was big. "We need to talk." "So talk." "Inside." I stepped aside. He walked past me into the living room and I closed the door behind him. "Pour me a drink," he said, dropping onto the couch. "Excuse me?" "I'm exhausted. Pour me a drink." I glared at him.

He didn't flinch. In the end, I walked to the cabinet, grabbed a glass and a bottle of whiskey, and dropped both on the table in front of him with more force than necessary. He poured. He drank. He poured again. "It's about your husband," he said. My heart stopped. "What about him?" I explained everything to her. "Why are you telling me this?" "Because my sister recognized the man. She says it was Dominic." 2/4 +15 Bonus I laughed. It came out sharp and bitter. "You're joking." "Do I look like I'm joking?" "Dominic would never..." "He was seen, Sera. In my house. In my guest room.

With your best friend." "Celeste is not my best friend." "Whatever she is to you, she was locked in a room with a man who looked exactly like your husband." I shook my head. I couldn't accept it. Not Dominic. Not the man who cooked for me, who cleaned for me, who worshipped the ground I walked on for years. "If a man like Dominic wanted to have an affair, he wouldn't go to a married woman's house and sneak into a guest room. It doesn't sound like something he would do." "People change." "He hasn't changed." I said it firmly, like saying it hard enough would make it true.

"All the years of our marriage, the only complaint I ever had about Dominic was that he didn't have money. He wasn't lacking in any other way." "Money changes people." "You don't know him like I do." "Maybe not. But I know what my sister saw." I stood up. My legs were shaking. My heart was pounding. But I held myself together because falling apart in front of Julian was not an option. "Your sister and your mother hate Celeste. You said it yourself. There's bad blood between them. What if they made it up?

What if they picked my husband's face and pretended he was the one who was there just to turn you against Celeste?" He opened his mouth. Closed it. "You never even saw him," I pressed. "You don't have cameras in your home. You were the one who decided not to have cameras because of our affair. Remember?" He sat back. The anger in his face flickered into something else. Doubt. "That actually makes me feel a whole lot better," he admitted. "Good." Julian got to his feet. "I know her. She's not the type to cheat and be so nonchalant about it. This is all an act.

But I still feel uneasy." He walked to the door. Paused. 3/4 +15 Bonus "Thank you for your time. And if you get really lonely... don't forget to give me a call." I didn't respond. When the door clicked shut behind him, I stood there for a long moment, staring at the wood grain, trying to breathe. Dominic. Cheating. With Celeste. No. I refused to believe it. I didn't check social media until after Julian left. I should have checked earlier. I should have known. The interview was everywhere. Dominic, standing with the Veil Holdings logo behind him. A reporter asking him about me.

About the shooting. About why he hadn't visited his wife in the hospital. And his response. "So if a random person appears and claims to be my wife, that automatically makes me a married man?" I watched it three times. Each time, the words hit harder. A random person. He called me a random person. I felt the room spin. My stomach lurched. I made it to the bathroom just in time to throw up. When I came back, my phone was exploding. Notifications pouring in. Comments. Messages. Tags. Fraud. Gold digger. Social climber. She staged the shooting for attention. Of course he didn't visit her.

chapters.title: Chapter 96
chapters.content:
Chapter 96 SERAPHINE My mother called at exactly the moment I was about to lose my mind. "What is going on?" she demanded. "I'm seeing people bashing your social media. Claiming you're lying. That you're not Dominic's wife." "Mom, I don't know. I'm going crazy." "Explain it to me. I spoke to you yesterday after the shooting. You told me everything was fine." "Everything is not fine." My voice cracked. "I've been lying to you, Mom. Ever since Dominic revealed himself as the chairman of Veil Holdings, he has been avoiding me. I haven't heard from him personally. I haven't seen him.

He hasn't come home. The only news I hear about him is from social media." "How can he treat you this way? After everything you've been through together?" "I don't know, Mom." "Relax." Her voice softened. "Maybe Dominic just doesn't want to let the world know he's married yet. He might have his reasons for keeping things on the low. He loves you so much. He practically used to worship the ground you walked on. Remember? He cooked for you. He cleaned for you. He did everything for you. That kind of love doesn't change overnight." "You're right.

It doesn't." "But I feel this tightness in my chest, Mom. I don't understand what's going on." "That should be the least of your problems. Once people realize the truth, they will stop. You have to find a way to get in contact with Dominic no matter what. You know how he feels about you." "Yes." "Something might be in the way of him coming back home or publicly admitting you're his wife. So do everything you can to meet with him. Once you meet, whatever misunderstandings exist, you can settle them. And then you can proudly show him off to the world." "You're right. You're right." "Okay.

Think of something. Let me know." "Thank you, Mom." I hung up and took a breath. Then another. She was right. Crying didn't solve anything. I needed to act. I found our marriage certificate in the safe. Took a picture. Posted it on social media without a single word. 1/3 +15 Bonus The response was immediate. The trolls who had been tearing me apart went quiet. A few insisted it was fake. But enough people came out to say it was real that the heat eventually died down. I had bought myself time. But time wasn't enough. I needed to see Dominic. Face to face.

And there was only one person who could get me to him. I drove to Helix Research Laboratory at five PM. Except I forgot they had moved locations. I ended up at the old building, locked and empty, feeling like an idiot. I called Kingsley. He answered on the second ring. "You completely forgot about me after I helped you get the job, right?" "Come on. I've been very..." *Just give me the new Helix address." I cut him off. "I need to find Celeste." The drive to the new facility took fifteen minutes. The building was impressive. Modern. Glass and steel.

A far cry from the cramped old space they had before. The receptionist recognized me immediately. "Mrs. Ford! Welcome. Who are you here to see?" "Celeste, and Pat." "Right this way." She led me through the lab. People looked up from their workstations. Some smiled. Some whispered. I ignored all of them. Pat came out of an office and froze when she saw me. She opened her mouth like she wanted to smile, but I didn't give her the chance. "Take me to Celeste." She nodded. "Okay. Come with me." She led me to a glass-walled office at the back. Celeste was inside, typing on a laptop.

She looked up when we walked in. "Sera..." "Don't." I held up my hand. "Don't 'Sera' me like we're friends. Neither of you bothered to call when I was in the hospital. Not one phone call. Not one text." Pat shifted her weight. "We were going to..." "No, you weren't." 2/3 +15 Bonus Celeste set her laptop aside. "Look, Sera. Things have been crazy here. The move, the setup, the..." "I don't care about any of that. I need your help." She blinked. "With what?" "I need you to reach out to Dominic. I need to talk to him." "I don't have a way to reach him.

He's been..." "I know he's been unreachable. But you have a partnership with Veil Holdings. You have contacts. You can find a way." Celeste hesitated. Her eyes flicked to Pat, who gave perfect suggestions. "Okay," Celeste said slowly. "Let me see what I can do." While Celeste was out of the room, Pat tried to make conversation. "So how's your research lab?" Pat asked. "Fine. I have capable hands there. I don't even need to show my face." "You're lucky. Over here, we still have a lot of work. Everyone is so busy. It's exhausting." "And my husband made that possible. Remember?

If I didn't say anything to my husband, he wouldn't have invested in Helix." Pat nodded, "Yeah, you're right. I was even meaning to thank you. It may seem like just a few words to you, but to us, you've practically changed our lives." "Yeah, whatever." Celeste came back. "Okay. I was able to reach out to the CEO's office. He said we can make a call on Helix's official line. Once I call back, they'll put the chairman on. But I have to introduce myself first and explain why I'm calling. Then I'll hand the phone over to you." "Why do you have to introduce yourself?

chapters.title: Chapter 97
chapters.content:
Chapter 97 "Fine. Whatever. Just make the call." Celeste dialed. She put it on speaker. The first ring. The second. There was a click. "Hello." It was Dominic's voice. My heart slammed against my ribs. "Mr. Ford," Celeste said. "I'm sorry to call you out of the blue, using our company line for something a bit personal." "Yeah, I'm really busy. Just get to the point." "Actually, I'm calling because there's someone who wants to speak to you. It's your wife. I'm going to hand the phone over to her." "What wife?" The two words hit me like a slap. "When did I have a wife?" Dominic asked.

"Have I ever told you in person that I am married?" I snatched the phone from Celeste's hand. "Dominic! Dominic, it's me! It's Seraphine! What are you saying?" The call disconnected. I stared at the screen. Redialed. A different voice answered. "Hello? Am I speaking to Mrs. Celeste?" "Give the phone to my husband. I want to speak to Dominic." "Excuse me, who is this?" "This is Mrs. Ford. Give the phone to my husband!" "Listen to me. I don't know who you are or what you want. If you're claiming to be Mrs. Ford, you should have a better way of reaching your husband.

Not through my phone." The call ended. I stood there, phone in my hand, my whole body shaking. "I'm sorry," Celeste whispered. "I'm worried I might have offended him." I dropped the phone on her desk. 1/4 +15 Bonus "You know what? I'll just leave." "Sera, wait." Pat stepped forward. "Is something going on? Whatever it is, you can share it. We can find a way to help." "Mind your own business." I walked out. I made it to my car before the shaking really started. I drove three blocks. Parked on the side of the road. Got out and screamed. The sound tore out of my throat raw and ugly.

People on the sidewalk stared. I didn't care. I couldn't care. When the screaming stopped, I leaned against the car and forced myself to breathe. He denied me. In front of Celeste. In front of Pat. On the phone. He said he didn't have a wife. He said I was no one. But I wasn't going to cry. I wasn't going to break. I needed to see him. Face to face. Let him tell me I wasn't his wife when I was standing right in front of him. But Celeste couldn't help me. She was too scared, too useless, too busy protecting her precious partnership. I needed someone else.

I went home and pulled up the photos from Dominic's reveal party. The night he stood on that stage and announced he was the chairman of Veil Holdings. I studied every face in the background. And then I found him. A man with tattoos. Standing close to Dominic. Leaning in like he was saying something important. I had seen him before. At my press conference. The one where I got shot. He was in the building somewhere, watching. I looked at the photo for a long time. And then I remembered. The club. I had gone there, ages ago, before any of this happened.

I had seen him there, and everyone treated him like royalty. He owned the place. I just needed to remember the name. I paced. I thought. I went through every memory of every club night I'd ever had. And then it hit me. The Den. 2/4 +15 Bonus The club opened at eight PM. I still had hours to kill. I drove to The Den at exactly eight-fifteen. The place was already filling up, bass thumping through the walls, neon lights flickering in the dark. I walked up to the bouncer. "I need to see the owner." "Yeah?

And who's asking?" I pulled out my phone and showed him the picture of the tattooed man standing next to Dominic. "Him. Tell him Seraphine Ford is here. The wife of Dominic Ford." The bouncer's expression shifted. "Wait here." I waited. Twenty minutes later, a man came down the stairs. He was broad-shouldered, clean-shaven, with the kind of face that had seen too much and trusted too little. "What do you want?" "To see your boss." "Who's asking?" "Seraphine Ford. I need your help. I need to reach Dominic Ford." He studied me. His eyes moved over my face, my clothes, my posture.

Taking me apart and putting me back together. "That interview he gave. He said he didn't have a wife." "I know." "So why should I believe you?" pulled out my phone again. Showed him the marriage certificate. "Because I have proof. And because if you help me, I'll make it worth your while." He looked at the certificate. Then at me. Then at the certificate again. "How much?" "Name your price." He thought about it and asked for two hundred grand. I cursed him inwardly, but ended up paying anyway. Finally, he pulled out his phone and dialed. "Yeah," he said into the phone. "I have someone here.

Chapter 98 SERAPHINE The room smelled like expensive whiskey and older secrets. I sat on the edge of a leather chair watching the door, counting the minutes. Thirty passed. Then forty. Then fifty. And now I was sitting in a back room of a club, waiting for a man called Sparrow to decide I was worth his time. The second-in-command who had taken my money kept offering me a glass.

A bed in the corner, a table with two chairs, a wine cabinet. He took a bottle of wine from his cabinet, sat down, opened it, poured two glasses, and pushed one toward me. Why have you been desperately searching for me?" "I need your help." I set the glass down without drinking. "I'm Mrs. Seraphine Dominic Ford. Dominic 1/4 +15 Bonus Ford, the richest billionaire in the country, is my husband. I haven't been able to reach him. I don't know why. He was interviewed and he acted like I'm not his wife. Something is happening. Maybe he can't publicly acknowledge me for a reason," I continued, hearing the desperation bleed into my voice. "But I know how much he loves me.

I just need to meet with him." "And what do I have to do with this?" "I know you're a business partner. Someone acquainted with him. Someone of your caliber can arrange a meeting. I've seen pictures of both of you together. Please help me." He swirled his wine. "If you're truly Mrs. Dominic Ford, you should have another means to reach him. Family. Friends. Something." I bit my lip. Dominic had never talked about his family. Not once in all our years together. And foolishly, I had never asked.

He wasn't the type to volunteer information about his past, and I had been too busy enjoying my life to care. "I don't have anyone else," I admitted. "He never introduced me. He never..." "Then that's your problem, not mine." "Please. I know you can help me." He nodded slowly. "It's true. I can help you. But Dominic and I are not as close as you think. We do business when it benefits us. That doesn't mean I can snap my fingers and arrange meetings with him." "Just this one thing. That's all I'm asking." "Fine." He drank from his glass and set it down. "I can arrange a meeting." "Thank you.

Thank you so much." "Don't thank me yet." His eyes traveled down my body, slow and deliberate. "You need to show sincerity first." "Sincerity?" "Don't play games with me. You're not a child. Nothing goes for nothing." "You want me to pay you?" "Of course. My time is valuable. I had important things to do before you dragged me here. If I'm going to make an arrangement between you and Mr. Dominic Ford, you have to make it worth my while. I'm taking a risk. What if I arrange this meeting and you end up harming him? I lose my business partner." "I won't do that. I'm his wife.

Get me to meet with him, and I'll have him compensate you," I offered. "No. I don't work without payment. I have a reputation. I always deliver. That's why everyone wants to work with me. Pay me first, then the job gets done." 2/4 +15 Bonus "Fine. How much?" "How much do you have?" *Just tell me the amount. I'll find a way." He smiled. It was not a kind smile. He reached into his pocket, pulled out a thick cigar, and bit the end off. He lit it slowly, letting the smoke curl between us, filling the room with something dark and heavy. "You need to hurry up," he pressed.

"I don't have all day." "I'm the one waiting. How much will you charge?" He took a long drag and exhaled. "Look at me. Do I look like I lack money? I don't need money from you. Someone like you can't afford me anyway." "Then what do you want?" "If you insist on paying with money, then send ten billion to my account, and I'll make the arrangement." "Ten billion?" I stared at him. "Just to see my husband?" "We're talking about the richest billionaire in the country. He's worth more than most small countries. Ten billion is a small price for someone who claims to be his wife.

Drop the money tonight, and I'll arrange for you to see him first thing tomorrow morning." "I don't have ten billion." "Exactly what I said. You can't pay me." My heart was pounding. "What else can you take? Other than money?" His lips curved. "Now you're talking." He looked at me the way men look at expensive things they want to break. "You're a very beautiful woman." He licked his lips. "Look at those luxurious melons on your chest. Those smooth wrists. Those curvy hips." I turned my face away. "As long as you please me tonight, I'll make the arrangement." "I'm Mrs. Ford. I told you...

I'm Dominic's wife." "That's not my business. This is a transaction. You scratch my back, I scratch yours." "I can't do something like this. If Dominic finds out..." "Who will tell him?" He cut in. "Will you? Because I'm certainly not a man who kisses and tells." He got to his feet. 3/4 +15 Bonus "The ball is in your court. I've spent too much time here already. It's either you accept my terms or you don't. You're either in or you're out." He began walking toward the door.

If he hadn't abandoned me, if he hadn't denied me, if he hadn't left me with no other options, I wouldn't have had to degrade myself like this. Tomorrow. I'll see him tomorrow. And it will all be worth it. I drove home in a daze. Showered until the water ran cold. Brushed my teeth three times. Ignored the pain in my ass, my scalp, my mouth, my sore pussy. Each time I thought about seeing Dominic tomorrow, my heart raced. I missed him. God, I missed him. I missed the way he held me. The way he touched me.

The way he made love to me, like I was something precious. I missed the way he smelled. The way he laughed. The way he looked at me like I was the only woman in the world. I hadn't realized how much I needed him until he was gone. Tomorrow. Everything changes tomorrow. My alarm went off at five AM. I was out of bed before it finished ringing. I showered again. Did my hair. Put on my best dress, the one Dominic used to love, emerald green that hugged my curves and made my skin glow. Heeled shoes. Red lipstick. I ate breakfast even though I wasn't hungry. Checked my reflection twelve times.

At six-thirty, I grabbed my keys and drove. The club was called The Den. I parked outside at exactly seven. Sparrow wasn't there. I waited. Checked my phone. Checked the entrance. Checked my phone again. Seven-fifteen. Seven-thirty. Eight. Oh God. He tricked me. He lied. He took what he wanted and he lied. I walked up to the entrance, found one of the bouncers, asked where Sparrow was. "He'll show up. Be patient." I paced. I wanted to scream. I wanted to cry. I had let that man do things to me, degrading things, and he had lied. At eight-thirty, a black car pulled into the lot.

Sparrow stepped out, smiling. 1/3 +15 Bonus "You said seven," I snapped. "I did show up, didn't I?" He gestured. "Let's go. We don't have much time." I got into my car. He told me to follow him. I drove behind his car through the morning traffic until we arrived at a restaurant that looked like it belonged in a magazine. The front gate had a sign: Members Only. He gestured to me, and I parked my car on the street and quietly got into his passenger seat. He pulled up to the entrance, rolled down his window, flashed a card. The guard nodded. The gate opened. He parked inside the lot.

The restaurant grounds were quiet. Deserted. No other cars, no staff moving around, nothing. "Are you sure he's here?" I asked. "I know who Dominic Ford is. He probably paid the restaurant to clear the entire area for his meeting. Just be patient. You'll see him soon." My heart hammered. "Don't rush over and ruin the moment. If you disturb his meeting, he might get upset. And that could affect me." "Dominic is my husband. He just has to see me. He won't get upset." I was confident, but my hands were shaking. And then I saw him.

He walked out of the restaurant, his side to me, a phone pressed to his ear. He was wearing a white shirt and dark green trousers, polished shoes that caught the morning light. Everything about him screamed luxury. Power. The man I married. I opened the car door before Sparrow could stop me. I stepped out. Dominic. My Dominic. After all this time. I called his name. He turned. He stood there, phone still at his ear, staring at me like he'd seen a ghost. I ran. I didn't think. I didn't care about the meeting, the arrangement, the propriety. I just ran.
