chapters.title: Chapter 102
chapters.content:
Chapter 102 DOMINIC I sat in my office at Veil Holdings, staring at the same file on my computer for what felt like the tenth time without absorbing a single word. My hands rested on the desk in front of me and I looked down at them, at the veins running across the backs, at the gold band on my finger that I still wore out of habit. I had come to the company for a meeting earlier that morning. That was the plan. Show up, handle what needed to be handled, and leave before anyone could corner me with more questions I did not want to answer.

But after the call from Celeste, after I heard her voice telling me that the time had come for the culmination of our plan, something had shifted in my chest. A tightness I could not name had wrapped itself around my ribs and squeezed. The desire to leave, to retreat to whatever corner of the city I wanted, had evaporated. So I buried myself in work instead, clicking through spreadsheets and reports, trying not to think about what those words meant. Trying not to think about her. My phone buzzed with a text message and I picked it up, squinting at the screen in the dim light of my office.

Celeste. She told me that Seraphine was at her lab, that she was requesting for Celeste to contact me through official means. Celeste had slipped out to let me know. She wanted to know what my situation was. I read the message twice, and then I felt my lips curve into a smile. This was not such a bad idea. If Seraphine wanted to speak to me that badly, I could give her what she wanted. I could give her a taste of what it felt like to reach for something and find nothing but air. I typed back, telling Celeste to go ahead and contact my CEO through the official channels.

I would let my CEO bring the phone to me when the time was right. And since Seraphine wanted to speak to me so desperately, I would speak to her. "All right then," Celeste replied. After the call ended, I immediately called my CEO and told him that Helix Research Laboratory was going to reach out to him any moment now. They were going to say they wanted to speak with the chairman. I told him that as long as the person on the other end was Mrs. Celeste, he should bring his phone over to my office so I could take the call. Then I waited. It did not take long.

My CEO knocked on my door and stepped inside, his phone pressed to his ear. He told me there was a call from Helix Laboratory. I took the phone from him and he slipped out of the room, closing the door behind him. I answered the call. I heard Celeste's voice first, calm and professional, and I knew Seraphine was listening in. I knew she was right there, holding her breath, waiting for me to say something that would prove she still mattered. So when Celeste made mention about my wife, I asked the question I knew 1/2 +15 Bonus would cut deepest. What wife? When did I have a wife?

Have I ever told you in person that I am married?" I heard her then. Seraphine's voice in the background, rising and cracking, growing hysterical in a way that would have stirred something in me once. But that was before. Before I knew the full weight of her betrayals. I scoffed and hung up the call. I handed the phone back to my CEO. I told him he could leave. I told him that if the phone rang again and the person on the other end was Seraphine, he was free to speak to her. He was free to be as rude as he wanted. But he was not to bring the phone to me.

After he left, I sat alone in the silence of my office and let my mind drift back to Celeste. Earlier, when I had heard her voice on the phone, she had sounded like everything was fine. But I knew better. I knew we needed to talk, really talk, and I was dreading it. If everything ended according to the initial plan, we were supposed to go our separate ways. That had been the deal. She did what she needed to do, I did what I needed to do, and once it was all over, we would walk away from each other like none of it had ever happened.

chapters.title: Chapter 103
chapters.content:
Chapter 103 +15 Bonus But everything was happening too fast now. The plan was reaching its conclusion sooner than either of us had expected. And I did not know if I could let her go. I did not know if I had the strength to ask her to stay. What would I even say to her? The divorce with Seraphine had been finalized, but Celeste was still married to Julian. She had done everything for the sake of revenge. What if she was not ready to have anything further to do with me after the dust settled? What if she had already made peace with walking away?

The thought sat in my stomach like lead and I could not shake it loose. I was still lost in that spiral when my phone rang. Sparrow. "What's up?" I answered. "I have good news," he said. "I want to deliver it in person." "Come to my office," I told him. Sparrow had driven me to the company earlier that morning. After I had decided to stay longer, I had sent him off to handle other tasks, telling him I would be safe inside the building. No one could get through the layers of security to reach me here. But now he was back, and the tone of his voice told me whatever he had found was important.

When Sparrow walked into my office, he had his phone in his hand and an expression on his face that I could not quite read. He took the chair across from my desk and scrolled through his screen until he found what he was looking for. Then he turned the display toward me. The footage showed the man who had fired the shot at Seraphine. He was being questioned, his hands bound, his face streaked with sweat and blood. The man had held up at first, insisting he would not talk. But then Sparrow began to cut off the tips of his fingers, starting with the little finger and working his way across.

Each time the man screamed, the sound raw and animal, and by the time Sparrow reached the middle finger, the man could not take the pain anymore. He said he would talk. Sparrow gave him the opportunity, and the man confessed. He said he was sent by the son of Dr. Benjamin Leeds. I sat back in my chair, the name stirring something cold in my chest. Dr. Benjamin. He had been among the people who stabbed my father in the back, who had worked with my father's enemies to try to take over the company. And when I had fought to avenge my father, I had taken Benjamin down myself.

But apparently, he had left behind a son. An illegitimate child I had never known about. A grown man now, with connections and resources and a burning desire to avenge his father. He was the one who had come after me. He was the one who had tried to put a bullet in Seraphine. Sparrow told me he had gathered his men and gone to the address the shooter had provided. By the time they arrived, Benjamin's son was already in a helicopter, fleeing the country. The armed men he had left 1/2 +15 Bonus behind were quickly subdued. Sparrow's team tried to go after him, but they were too late.

He was gone. But Sparrow assured me that he knew which country Benjamin's son had escaped to. He had already informed his contacts there. They were looking for him all over. For now, Benjamin's son was the one on the run, hiding from the same kind of fear he had tried to instill in me. I let out a long breath I had not realized I was holding. The tightness in my chest loosened, just a fraction "The danger at your back is gone for now," Sparrow said. He put his phone away and looked at me. "What should I do with the man who fired the shot? Do you want me to finish him off?" I smiled.

chapters.title: Chapter 104
chapters.content:
+15 Bonus Chapter 104 I shook my head. "All the other men you assigned are still around. You even put someone to protect Celeste, like I asked. You have been by my side for days. I am sure your business is suffering. Go and focus on it." "Maybe tomorrow," he said. "Tonight, I will stay by your side. Just to be safe and make sure nothing happens. I reached out and tapped his shoulder. "That is why you are the best, Sparrow. Reliable to the end After I left the company, I went back to my hotel room.

The suite was large and cold and empty, and I lay on the bed staring at the ceiling, my mind circling back to Celeste. I had made up my mind now. The danger was gone. There was no need for me to hide anymore. I could be out in the open, which meant I could meet with Celeste. I would tell her that she did not have to worry anymore, that everything was finally falling into place. She did not know yet about what had happened, about Benjamin's son, about the danger that had been neutralized.

So if this was what she really wanted, if walking away from me was what she needed to do to find peace, then I would let her go. But I needed to see her first. I needed to look her in the eyes and know for sure. I planned to surprise her. Show up at Helix Research Laboratory or somewhere else she would not expect me to be. I wanted to see the look on her face when she realized I had come for her. I was still lost in thought, the night deepening around me, when my phone rang again. Sparrow. "What is it?" I answered. "I just got an interesting call," he told me.

"My second at The Den just informed me that Seraphine is over there, desperately asking to see me." I raised my brows. "Impressive. She must have connected the dots. Must have found out that you are linked to me somehow. "I figured," Sparrow said. "I wanted to find out if it was okay with you. If you want me to go see her." "Why would I stop you? She is clearly trying to use you to get to me. She has gone all out to try to see me, even going to meet Celeste. So if she is looking for you, she is hoping you will be her way in." "What do you want me to do?

If she asks to see you, how should I handle it?" I thought about it for a moment. The truth was, I did not care much one way or the other. But there was something I needed to give her. Something that would make everything official. And if Seraphine was offering herself up on a silver platter, I could use this. "If she asks you to arrange a meeting," I said, "make the arrangements. The sooner I see her, the sooner I can get it over with." 1/2 "Okay, but if I just do everything for her free of charge, would that not look strange?" +15 Bonus Free? Who said anything about free?

"That is actually perfect," | told him. "I have an idea for a location. | will let you know the details shortly. | need somewhere private. Somewhere no one can get close enough to take a photograph. | do not need the public connecting her to me any further." "Understood," Sparrow replied. The call ended. | set my phone on the nightstand and stared at the ceiling. Well.

In the end, things were going exactly the way Celeste wanted. | would give Seraphine the divorce certificate, she would find out the way Celeste had always intended, and after that Seraphine would have nothing further to do with my life. That part, at least, was clean. The other part was less clean. I checked my phone twice waiting for a call from Celeste that did not come. | did not call her either. | was going to see her tomorrow and | wanted to be in front of her when we had that conversation, not a voice in her ear that she could manage from a distance.

| put the phone face down and went to sleep. | was at Lumiere by eight. It was a private members restaurant that most of the city did not know existed and the ones who did know never discussed. Floor to ceiling windows looking out over a garden that had never once been photographed. | had paid to have the grounds cleared for the morning and the staff had been briefed to stay in the back until | called for them. | had already told Sparrow to make it look like | had a meeting, so that Seraphine would have a reason to wait in the car rather than walking straight up to me.

| did not want a scene inside. | wanted to be able to hand her the certificate and leave. The certificate was in my jacket pocket. | sat at the corner table with a coffee | did not particularly want and waited. Eventually | saw Sparrow's car come through the gate. | gave it a few minutes. Then | stood, slid my phone into my hand as a prop, and walked out of the restaurant. The morning air was cool. | held the phone to my ear and made no call to no one and walked at a deliberate pace across the grounds, keeping my face angled slightly away from where Sparrow's car was parked.

| heard her voice before | turned. My name, called out the way people called things they had been holding in for too long. High and raw and slightly desperate. | turned. Seraphine was running toward me. She closed the distance between us in seconds and threw herself at me before | had fully processed that she was going to do it. Her arms went around my bod: and her face went into my chest and she was crying. Properly crying, her shoulders shaking, her voice muffled against my jacket. : "| missed you," she said. She looked genuinely shocked, which told me some part of her had still been expecting a different reception. "Dominic." Her voice was trembling. "It's me. It's Seraphine. Your wife. chapters.title: Chapter 106
chapters.content:
Chapter 106 She flinched "I gave you divorce papers some time ago, I continued. "You signed them. Right in front of me Whether you read them or not is not my concern. The divorce has been processed and that is your copy "I looked at her steadily "From this point forward, you and I have nothing to do with each other There is no need to grant any more interviews or tell anyone that you know me. And do not appear in front of me again "No" The word came out like something breaking. "No. No, Dominic. I don't agree. I don't agree to this divorce I can't live without you. Please.

Please don't do this to me." She dropped to her knees on the path. Her arms went around my leg. She held on the way people held things they knew were being taken away "You're divorcing me without a single penny," she said against my trousers, her voice cracking. "After all our years together. After everything I went through with you. I was with you when you had nothing. Dominic, you promised me you would treat me like a princess. You promised you would give me the world. And now that you have everything, you are throwing me away? For who? Who is she?

Who is more deserving than the woman who stood by you all those years when you had nothing?" I looked down at her. She kept going. My name over and over. Dominic. Dominic. Dominic. Crying at my feet while Sparrow watched from a car window with the expression of a man who had seen stranger things and not particularly cared about those either. I let her say everything she needed to say. I waited. And when she had run out of words and was simply holding my leg and sobbing, I reached down and carefully removed her hands. She grabbed for me again, but I stepped back.

I turned and walked toward my car. She ran after me. Just as I reached the door she caught me from behind, her arms going around me, her voice in my ear "Please, Dominic. Whatever I have done wrong I am sorry. I will change. I love you. I will do anything Please give me one more chance. I cannot live without you. You have no idea what I have gone through just to see you. My life has been miserable. If you leave me I am going to die." I tried to loosen her fingers from around my body. She tightened her grip. I tried again. She held on harder.

I pulled her hands away with the force the situation required and she went down, landing on the ground with a sharp sound of impact, wincing, tears streaming. 173 +15 Bonus I got in the car and drove. I was through the restaurant gate and onto the road when my phone rang. Celeste. My mood lifted so completely and so immediately that I was mildly embarrassed by it. "Good morning," I said when I answered. "Good morning, Dominic." Her voice was warm and easy, the voice she used when she was not performing for anyone.

"I was just thinking about you." "Were you?" "Do not sound so smug about it." I almost laughed. "I thought about what you said. About it being time." "Yes. I meant it. I am ready." "There is something I did not tell you," I said. "I put two bodyguards on you. I needed to know you were safe." She paused. "You did?" "I was worried. But I also found out something yesterday that works in our favor. Julian has had someone following you. A private investigator. He has eyes on your movements." *Julian had me followed?" Her voice sharpened. "Are you serious?" "Yes. But think about what that means.

You want him to catch us in the act. And he already has eyes on you. All we need to do is set the stage. His man will report back to him and Julian will come running himself. Who knows? He might even bring Seraphine along." There was silence on her end while she worked through it. "We could do this today," I said. "If you are ready." "I thought the security situation was going to take more time." "We will talk about that when we see each other. The situation has changed. I will explain everything in person." "We are really seeing each other today then?" "Yes. I will pick you up.

chapters.title: Chapter 107
chapters.content:
Chapter 107 CELESTE I had to hand it to Seraphine. Watching her unravel after that phone call, the way her voice had climbed and cracked and gone almost hysterical in the background, anyone who did not know better would have thought she was genuinely, desperately in love with her husband. The kind of woman who had been wronged and was fighting to hold her marriage together. It was impressive, really. The performance of it.

But if Seraphine was operating under the impression that a man denying you publicly, and before people considered your friends, meant anything other than he was completely done with you, then she was living in a fool's paradise that I did not have the heart to dismantle for her. Not yet, anyway. I could not keep the straight face for much longer. The moment Seraphine walked out, the awkward silence she left behind pressing against the room, I let out a slow breath and turned toward the window. Pat, predictably, started immediately.

"Celeste." She came to stand beside me, her voice low and careful in the way it got when she was trying to work something out. "What was that about? Why would the CEO of Veil Holdings deny being married to Seraphine? He funded our entire laboratory. He gave us money without blinking. Why would he do that if he was not in good terms with his wife?" I shrugged and kept my voice light. "I have no idea, Pat. That is between them. I am not in the business of getting involved in other people's marriages." "But you were the one who made the call for her.

You must know something." "I made a call because she asked me to. That is all. Whatever is going on between Dominic Ford and Seraphine is their business, not ours. Do not think too much about it, Pat. When Seraphine is ready to talk about whatever is going on, she will come to her two best friends. You know how she is. For now, let us focus on the lab. This phase is fragile and extremely important. We cannot afford to be distracted." Pat considered that for a moment. Then she nodded, more slowly than I would have liked. "You are right.

Actually." Her expression shifted, the worry giving way to something brighter. "Moving on to urgent Helix business, there is someone I want you to meet." She picked up her phone and dialed without explanation. "Dr. Duke" she said when someone answered. "Come to the room now." I furrowed my brows. "Who is Duke?" 1/2 +15 Bonus "You will see," she said, smiling to herself. I watched her with curiosity because Pat was the type who needed to see results before she formed an opinion. So for her to be this eager, this Duke person must have made an impression. A knock came at the door.

Two sharp raps. Then the door opened and a man walked in. I stared. I was not proud of it, but I stared for a full second longer than was appropriate for a professional introduction. He was tall, with broad shoulders that filled his shirt without straining it, brown hair, blue eyes that were unusual enough to be striking, and a face that was handsome in the clean, uncomplicated way that did not require a second look to confirm. He required a second look anyway. Something fluttered in my chest and I did not immediately know what to do with it, which was embarrassing.

chapters.title: Chapter 108
chapters.content:
Chapter 108 My thoughts drifted from the room to Dominic. I remembered the way his arms felt when they wrapped around my waist, solid and secure. The look in his eyes when he wanted me, dark and focused and hungry. The way he smiled when I said something that caught him off guard, that small curve at the corner of his mouth that made him look younger. The taste of him when we kissed. Soft but firm, patient but demanding, like he had all the time in the world but did not want to waste any of it. I was smiling at nothing when Pat's hand appeared in front of my face. "Celeste." She waved.

"Earth to Celeste." I blinked and realized I had been standing there with my eyes fixed on Kingsley Duke while my mind was somewhere else entirely. "Huh?" Pat laughed. "I said I wanted you to meet someone. Where did you just go?" Heat crawled up my neck. I could not remember the last time I had zoned out mid-introduction to think about a man. I was fairly certain it had never happened before in my adult life. "Sorry," I said, composing myself with more effort than it should have required. "Something crossed my mind.

You were saying?" I turned my attention to the man who was still standing there waiting to be acknowledged. Up close he was even more handsome but it did not matter because whatever flutter I had felt was just my brain. playing tricks on me, recognizing Dominic in the shape of a stranger and reacting accordingly. "This is Dr. Kingsley Duke," Pat said, gesturing between us with the barely contained excitement of someone presenting a particularly good acquisition. "An excellent PhD. He has just joined Helix as a senior research associate.

His role covers research reports, papers, and grant proposals, and also coordinating with external researchers, universities, and partner organizations." She paused, clearly building to her point. "Now that Veil Holdings has funded us, other companies and institutions are going to come looking. They will see that Veil Holdings invested and they will want to know why. Having someone of Kingsley's caliber handling our grant proposals at this stage is exactly what we need." I looked at Pat.

She was practically glowing as she spoke and I realized I had never seen her this excited about anyone joining the team. Kingsley must truly be impressive. And with looks like his, I imagined all the female staff would be fighting for his attention. I would be the exception though. You cannot share a bed with a man like Dominic Ford and still feel attracted to someone else. That kind of experience recalibrates your standards permanently. 2 I stepped forward and offered my hand. "Welcome to Helix Laboratory, Dr. Duke.

I hope we can achieve great things together." He took my hand and shook it with a firm but respectful grip. "Thank you, Dr. Celeste. I look forward to contributing." 1/2 +15 Bonus After he left, Pat immediately launched into how he had come recommended, his publication record, his previous institution, his response rate on proposals, the whole file. I stopped her with a hand on her arm. "There is no need," I told her. "I trust your judgment completely. If you think he is right for us, that is enough for me." She looked pleased.

I noted that she also looked slightly more flushed than the conversation warranted. I had planned to go back to the house and collect everything belonging to me, from the guest room. Now that the accommodation at the new Helix was ready, I wanted to move in properly and stop spending another night under the same roof as Elizabeth and Riley if I could help it. But I didn't feel like going back there for now and I had nothing with me, so I went shopping instead.

chapters.title: Chapter 109
chapters.content:
Chapter 109 The whole time I had the persistent, prickling sensation of being watched. I turned around twice in the first store. Once in the second. Each time, no one was looking at me. Just the normal movement of shoppers and staff going about their afternoon. I shook it off and kept going, but the feeling did not fully leave. I had dinner alone at a small place near the lab, something simple that I barely tasted because my mind was elsewhere, and then I went back to Helix and moved into the room.

It was small but thoughtfully built, the kind of space that had been designed by someone who understood that small did not have to mean cramped. The walls were a warm off-white, the floor real hardwood. A compact kitchen along one wall, properly fitted, with a real cooker and a coffee machine that looked like it had been chosen with care. A flat screen mounted opposite the bed, which was a proper double, not a single dressed up with extra pillows. A small table with two chairs.

A balcony just big enough for two people to stand comfortably and look out at whatever the evening was doing to the sky. It would do. It would more than do. I was arranging my things when Pat appeared in the doorway with an expression that was fighting between amusement and concern. "You brought a lot," she observed, looking at the bags lined up along the wall. "I did not want to lack anything while I was here," I told her. She looked at the bags. Then at me. Then at the bags again. "Right," she said, and did not push further, which was one of the reasons I loved Pat.

I waited for Dominic to call. He did not call. I had spoken to him twice already that day and I had been the one to reach out. He knew what was coming. He knew we were at the final stage. And still, nothing. I told myself it did not matter. This was not a relationship. There were no rules about who called whom or how often. We were two people with an arrangement and arrangements did not come with communication expectations. I fell asleep waiting. When I woke up the next morning and checked my phone, there was nothing from Dominic and, surprisingly, nothing from Julian either.

I had spent the night outside the house without a word to my husband and he had not bothered to check. Which told me either his ego was still running the show or something else had his attention. 1/2 +15 Bonus Either way, it was useful information. I started my morning, kept checking my phone between tasks, and eventually could not stand it anymore. Pat caught me looking at my screen for the fourth time in an hour. "Are you expecting a call from someone?" she asked, with the particular tone of a woman who already had a theory. "I am just checking the time," I told her. She did not believe me.

I could see it on her face. But she let it go. I excused myself to the bathroom. I stood in the small tiled space and looked at my phone and had a brief internal argument with myself about whether calling him made me look desperate. I concluded that the question itself was the problem. We were not in a conventional relationship. There was no desperate or not desperate. There was just what I wanted to do. What I wanted to do was hear his voice. I called.

chapters.title: Chapter 110
chapters.content:
Chapter 110 A beat of quiet on his end. He did not say it back. Of course he did not. That was not who we were. That was not what this was. I knew that and the small quiet on the other end of the line was a reminder delivered without malice but landing nonetheless. After the call, I sat on the edge of the bathroom counter and looked at my reflection in the mirror. I had told him it was time. I had meant it when I said it. Her eyes were glassy, her lips trembling, her entire body shaking with the force of the humiliation that had just been dumped on her head like a bucket of ice water, and I knew, I knew with absolute certainty, that she had not seen this coming.

She had walked into Helix thinking she was the predator, thinking she held all the cards, thinking she could destroy me with her righteous fury. She had walked in here ready to watch me burn and instead she was the one standing in the ashes. The staff did not hold back. The whispers started low, a murmur that rippled through the crowd like wind through wheat, but they grew louder and more venomous with every passing second, each voice adding fuel to the fire that was consuming Seraphine's reputation right before our eyes.

"Slut," someone hissed from the left, a woman I recognized as one of the junior researchers, her face twisted with disgust. "She slept with her best friend's husband and then had the audacity to come here and play the victim." "What kind of woman does that?" another voice added, this one male, sharp and incredulous. "Fucking your friend's husband and then showing up at her workplace to accuse her of being a whore? The audacity is astronomical." "Devil," an older technician muttered, shaking his head slowly. "That is what she is. A devil in expensive clothes." "No wonder Mr.

Ford denied knowing her," a voice piped up from somewhere in the back, loud enough for everyone to hear." What husband would want to stay married to a woman who spreads her legs for her best friend's husband in hotel rooms and bars like a common streetwalker?" "I heard she used to sleep with multiple men back in college too," another woman added, her voice dripping with scorn. "Some people never change. You can take the whore out of the streets but you cannot take the streets out of the whore." "Homewrecker," someone else spat. "She probably targeted Mrs.

Celeste's husband from the very beginning. Some women cannot stand to see their friends happy so they have to destroy everything good in their lives." "And she tried to twist it around? Shameless. Absolutely shameless." "Look at her standing there with her hand on her cheek like she is the one who has been wronged. If I were her, I would crawl into a hole and never show my face in public again." "Her reputation is finished. No respectable man will ever want to touch her after this. Everyone in this city is going to know what she did." "She deserves everything coming to her." "Trash.

Absolute trash." The words hit Seraphine like physical blows, each one driving her further into the ground, and I watched as her composure finally cracked, the tears spilling over her eyelids and streaming down her cheeks in thick, mascara stained rivers that lett dark tracks on her skin. Her shoulders shook with silent sobs, her chest heaved, and she looked around the room at the faces that were staring at her with contempt and disgust and hatred, and she saw no sympathy anywhere, no kindness, no mercy. She turned and ran.

Her heels clacked against the floor in a frantic rhythm as she fled through the doors, her hands covering her face, her sobs echoing behind her. The glass doors swung shut behind her and the room fell into a silence that was thick and charged, everyone looking at the spot where she had been standing, the air still vibrating with the energy of the confrontation. I rolled my eyes. The staff began to disperse, turning back to their workstations, pulling out their phones, no doubt preparing to share the Footage they had recorded with the world.

I let them take a few steps before I raised my voice and called them back. "Everyone, wait." +15 Bonus They stopped. They turned. They looked at me with expressions ranging from curiosity to embarrassment, like children who had been caught doing something they should not have been doing. "I noticed all of you took out your phones to record the event earlier," I said, my voice calm and measured, carrying across the room without effort. "And I understand the temptation It is human nature to want to capture drama when it unfolds in front of you.

But I need you to listen to me very carefully because what I am about to say is in your own best interests." Silence. Every eye was on me. "Those videos you recorded," I continued, "they mention Mr. Ford. Dominic Ford. The chairman of Veil Holdings. The man who invested five billion dollars in this laboratory. And they were taken within the premises of Helix. If those videos go viral, if they end up on social media or anywhere else on the internet, Mr. Ford could get very upset.

Chapter 14 I paused, letting the weight of my words sink in, watching the way their expressions shifted as the realization began to dawn. "He could choose to withdraw his funding from Helix," I said. "And when that happens, we all suffer the consequences. This laboratory shuts down. Every single person in this room loses their job. The research we have been working on for years goes down the drain. All because someone wanted to get a few likes and shares on social media." A murmur rippled through the crowd. People exchanged nervous glances.

"But it is not just about Helix," I added, my voice dropping to a more serious tone. "Mr. Ford could come after the individuals who shared those videos. The ones whose phones recorded the footage. He has more money than all of you and some of the best lawyers in the world. None of you would survive a lawsuit where he is the plaintiff. Even if you were the plaintiff, you would still not survive. And the fines the court would impose for sharing defamatory content against a man of his stature? You would be paying them off for the rest of your lives." The room was dead silent.

I could see the color draining from some of their faces, could see the way their hands instinctively moved to their pockets, their phones suddenly feeling like lead weights instead of convenient devices. "I am not threatening you," I said, softening my voice slightly. "I am warning you. As a colleague. As someone who does not want to see any of you ruin your lives over a moment of entertainment. Delete the videos. All of them. And make sure they never see the light of day." For a moment, no one moved. And then, one by one, they pulled out their phones. They scrolled through their galleries.

They pressed delete. Some of them even showed me their screens to prove that the footage was gone. Others just nodded and slipped their phones back into their pockets, murmuring words of thanks as they turned away. "Thank you, Mrs. Fisher," someone said. "You saved us from making a grave mistake." "Thank you for looking out for us." "We would have ruined our lives without knowing it." I smiled and nodded, accepting their gratitude with grace, and then I turned and walked toward my private office.

The door clicked shut behind me and I let out a long, slow breath, the tension of the morning finally beginning to ease from my shoulders. I walked around my desk and was about to lower myself into my chair when I heard the door open behind me. I turned to see who it was but right at that moment, Pat rushed forward and pulled me into a warm, tight hug. Her arms wrapped around my shoulders and she held me like I was something precious, something fragile, something that needed to be protected from the world.

I could feel her shaking, could feel the moisture of her tears soaking into the fabric of my blouse, could hear the shaky, hiccupping breaths she was taking against my neck. "My dear," Pat whispered, her voice thick with emotion. "You have suffered so much. I cannot imagine the pain you must have gone through all this time alone." I smiled against her shoulder, finding her behavior endearing, a little innocent, a little naive, but genuine in a way that touched something deep in my chest.

"Why are you crying?" I asked as we pulled apart, my hands resting on her shoulders, looking at the tears streaming down her cheeks. "I am the one who was supposed to be crying, not you." Pat wiped at her eyes with the back of her hand, laughing and crying at the same time, a sound that was half sob and halt chuckle. "I just feel so sorry for you, Celeste. I can still remember that first day we met Mr. Ford at that bar years ago.

You clearly showed interest in him first but Seraphine swooped in and stole him away like she always did with everything you wanted." I said nothing, just listened, letting her words wash over me. "I should have reprimanded her back then," Pat continued, her voice gaining strength as her anger grew. "We should have stood up against her behavior together. Chapter 147 CELESTE Pat stared at me for what felt like an eternity, her hands still wrapped around mine, hereyes searching my face like she was looking for something she could hold onto, something that would make sense of the words I had just thrown into the air between us. The silence stretched and coiled and I could feel my heartbeat counting the seconds, until finally she pulled her hands away and leaned back in her chair with a long, deliberate exhalation that seemed to carry the weight of everything she was about to say.

"What you are feeling right now is not love," she said, her voice firm, the words landing like stones dropped into still water. I felt my brow furrow, a reflexive denial already forming on my lips. "Why would you say that?" "Think about it logically, Celeste," Pat said, leaning forward again, her elbows resting on her knees, her hands clasped together like she was about to deliver a sermon. "You trusted Julian with everything you had. You built your entire life around that man. You gave him your loyalty, your body, your dreams. And he betrayed you.

He shattered the foundation of everything you believed in. And then Dominic was there. He was the one who told you the truth. He was the one who showed you the evidence. He was the one who held your hand while you watched your world collapse. Of course you feel attached to him. That is not love. That is trauma bonding." I shook my head slowly, the words sitting wrong in my chest, scraping against something tender and raw. "It is more than that, Pat. I know what I feel." "Do you?" Pat asked, her voice gentle but pointed. "You have known Dominic for what, a few weeks? A month at most?

Yes, he is handsome. Yes, he is wealthy. Yes, he has all the qualities that would make any woman weak in the knees. But how well do you actually know him? How much of what you feel is real and how much of it is just the relief of finally having someone on your side after being taken for granted?" I opened my mouth to respond but she held up a hand, stopping me before I could get the words out. "And let us not forget the most important detail," she continued. "It was you who suggested the affair arrangement. You said it yourself.

If you had not mentioned it, Dominic would never have brought it up. Which means that whatever is happening between you two exists because you initiated it. Not because he pursued you. Not because he had feelings for you. But because you needed a tool for your revenge and he agreed to be that tool." The words hit harder than I wanted to admit, each one finding a crack in my armor and slipping through. "I know I am not the best person to give advice on love," Pat said, her voice softening. "My track record with men is a disaster zone and we both know it.

But I do know that it is very easy to confuse infatuation with love, especially when you are coming out of a situation that left you feeling broken and unwanted. Right now, feeling this way for Dominic feels easy because there are no real obstacles He is powerful, he is attentive, he makes you feel seen. But what happens when the novelty wears off? What happens when the reality of who he is, a billionaire with a world of responsibilities, connections, expectations, comes knocking?" I looked down at my hands, at the way they were twisting together in my lap.

"What happens," Pat said, her voice dropping to almost a whisper, "when he decides it is time to settle down with someone of his own choosing? Someone from his world. Someone who fits into the life he has built. Where will that leave you, Celeste? You will be neck deep in emotions you convinced yourself were real and he will walk away without a second thought because to him, this was always just an arrangement." I swallowed hard, the truth of her words settling into my bones like cold water. "I am not saying this to hurt you," Pat added quickly.

"I am saying this because I love you and I do not want to see you broken again. You just escaped one prison. Do not build another one for yourself." 77 +15 Bonus I nodded slowly, the motion feeling mechanical, disconnected from the chaos swirling inside my chest. "I appreciate you looking out for me, Pat. I really do. And maybe you are right. Maybe this is just trauma bonding. Maybe I am confusing gratitude and attraction for something deeper, But I have to tell you, whether what I feel is real or not, the desire I have for that man is unlike anything I have ever experienced.

Chapter 1,8 "What do you suggest I do?" +15 Bonus "End it," Pat said simply. "Officially. Cleanly. The goal of your affair with Dominic has been achieved. Julian and Seraphine have felt the pain you felt. You have asked for a divorce. The revenge arc is complete. If you keep dragging this out, you are only going to confuse yourself further. You need one major conversation with Dominic where you thank him for everything, explain that the arrangement has run its course, and close the door on this chapter of your life. Both of you walk away with clarity. No loose ends.

No what-ifs." I turned the idea over in my mind, testing its weight, feeling the shape of it, and something about the clarity of it appealed to the part of me that was tired of living in uncertainty. "And once you have that closure," Pat continued, "you can move on with your life. Focus on your career. Focus on yourself. Let yourself heal. And all these confusing feelings you have for Dominic will float away with the wind like smoke from a fire that has been properly extinguished." I let out a long breath, the tension in my shoulders easing slightly as the decision crystallized in my mind.

"You are right, Pat. You are absolutely right. It is better to end things decisively now than to drag it out and end up hurt. Instead of sitting here guessing what Dominic is thinking or feeling, I can just talk to him. Make sure both sides understand that everything is over. Save myself from unnecessary heartache." Pat nodded, a small smile spreading across her face. "That is my girl." I reached for my phone, my fingers moving almost of their own accord, pulling up Dominic's contact and pressing the call button before I could talk myself out of it.

The line rang twice before he picked up, his voice coming through the speaker with that familiar warmth that made my stomach tighten. "Celeste," he said, and I could hear the surprise in his voice, the pleasure, the way he said my name like it meant something to him. I did not want to spend too much time on pleasantries, did not want to give myself the chance to get distracted by the sound of his voice or the memories of his hands on my skin. So I kept it brief, professional, to the point. "I wanted to thank you for the bodyguards," I said. "They came in handy today.

More than I expected." "Did something happen?" I could hear the shift in his voice, the protective edge creeping in, and I quickly added, "I will explain everything when I see you. But there is also something I need to tell you in person. Something important." There was a pause on the other end, a beat of silence that seemed to stretch, and then he said, "When?" "Tomorrow evening. Are you free?" "Absolutely," he said without hesitation, the word coming out so quickly that I almost smiled despite myself.

I was about to suggest a private resort I knew, somewhere neutral and quiet where we could talk without distractions, when he spoke again. "Would you come to my place? It would be safer for us to talk there." I hesitated for only a second before agreeing. "That works. I will drive myself." "I can pick you up..." "No," I cut him off, perhaps too quickly. "I need my own transportation." I could not afford the attention his car would bring to Helix, especially after what happened here today. "And it is not a big deal." I added. "I have been to your place before.

More than once." +15 Bonus "Not that place," he said, and there was something different in his voice, something almost careful. "I will send you the address. I felt a flicker of curiosity but I did not press. "Go ahead. Text it to me." "I will. And Celeste?" "Yes?" "I look forward to seeing you." The words sent a ripple through my chest that I forced myself to ignore, my grip tightening on the phone as I said, "Tomorrow evening. I will be there." I hung up before he could say anything else, before the sound of his voice could dig its hooks any deeper into my skin.

Pat was watching me with an expectant expression, her eyebrows raised. "It is done," I said, setting the phone down on my desk. "I am meeting him tomorrow evening at his place. We will talk. We will end things. And then I can move on with my life." Pat nodded, a satisfied smile on her face. "I am proud of you, Celeste. That takes courage." I did not feel courageous. I felt like I was standing at the edge of a cliff, trying to convince myself that jumping was the smart thing to do.

So let us say you give up your career as a model. You start dressing the way this man wants. You become a stay-at-home wife. You cook, you clean, you mop, you do everything to be the best wife you could be. And one day, you find out that your husband has been having an affair. With someone who wears those sexy dresses he asked you to stop wearing. Someone who is a model. And not just that, your husband funded her modeling career with money. Lots of money. While you were forced to give up your career and stay at home. 21 The silence that followed was thick enough to cut with a knife.

Riley's face had gone pale, her hands frozen on the table, her eyes fixed on some point in the middle distance. "What would you do, Riley?" I asked, my voice soft, almost gentle. "Give me your honest answer." She opened her mouth. Closed it. Opened it again. "Why are you quiet?" I asked. "Cat got your tongue? Tell me what you would do if your husband did all of this to you." "I would be very hurt," Riley finally said, her voice barely above a whisper. "I would be very upset." "That is the natural reaction," I said, nodding along. "And then what? You forgive him? You continue in the marriage?

You keep giving up your career? You keep being the good wife at home who covers her whole body while he fucks models behind your back? Is that what you would do?" "No," Riley said, and this time her voice was stronger, firmer, the word cutting through the air like a blade. "No, I would not do that. I would get a divorce." "Really?" I asked, my eyebrows rising in mock surprise. "You would divorce him? But why? What he did does not seem so bad, does it? I mean, he just wanted you to be a good, modest wife while he went out and had fun with women who looked the way you used to look.

Where is the harm in that?" Riley's jaw tightened, her hands clenching into fists on the table. "It is bad. He prevented me from pursuing my career and then he supported someone else to do the same career. He made me feel like I was not good enough while he was out there fucking someone who was exactly what he told me not to be. That is not love. That is control." I leaned back in my chair, letting the silence stretch, letting the weight of her own words settle over her like a shroud.

chapters.title: Chapter 152
chapters.content:
Chapter 152 CELESTE Riley's face crumpled, the fight draining out of her like air from a punctured balloon. She looked down at the table, her shoulders sagging, her hands limp and useless in her lap, and she did not say a word. I took another bite of my pasta, savoring the silence, savoring the taste of victory that was somehow sweeter than the carbonara on my tongue. Riley suddenly shook her head, her hands flying up in front of her like she was warding off my words. "No, no, no, wait.

It is not the same thing." "It is the same thing," I said, setting down my fork and fixing her with a steady look. "Listen to yourself, Riley. Your brother made me stop going to Helix. My life's dream, my life's work. He framed it as love, as concert for me, as wanting me to rest and take it easy. And for the sake of peace in my marriage, I gave it all up. I stopped going to the lab except once in a while. I took my mind off my career entirely and focused my whole attention on him. Look at me. I love looking sexy. I love wearing sexy dresses.

This is how Julian met me, this is how I looked when he fell in love with me, this is what he married. But after the wedding, he wanted me to cover up. He said it was more decent to dress modestly, that a married woman should not be showing off her body to the world. And I did it. I became a stay-at-home wife doing everything for Julian. He did not want children. Even though I did, I agreed. I went on the pill. Whatever Julian did not want, I did not fight him on it.

I gave him everything he asked for without argument." Riley stared at me, her lips pressed together, her eyes shifting uncomfortably. "Even when he stopped touching me," I continued, my voice steady, each word landing like a hammer blow. "He had business trips. He had contracts he was chasing. He needed time. He was always tired. I did not complain. I was still the understanding wife, the patient one, the woman who stood by her man no matter what. But what was he doing behind my back? He was having sex with my best friend. The same person working at Helix Laboratory.

He even opened a bigger laboratory for her. He sponsored her career. Funded her dreams. And she was always dressing in sexy clothes, the kind he told me to stop wearing. Julian never had a problem with that. So tell me, Riley, you said with your own mouth that you would divorce a husband who did those things to you. So why are you trying to convince me to stay with your brother? Why? Simply because he loves me? Is that your definition of love?" Riley shook her head slowly, her voice small when she finally spoke. "No.

INs just that after you left, Julian fainted and he was rushed to the hospital. He has been crying out your name and I feel really, really bad for him." "Of course you do," I said, and my voice came out softer than I expected. "It is natural for you to feel bad for him. He is your brother. You will always take his side. But let me make this very clear to you, Riley. My marriage to Julian is over. Whether he sent you here or you decided to run this errand on your own, you better run back to wherever you came from and tell him that nothing has changed.

You said with your own mouth that you would not stay with a man like Julian. So do not ask that of me." I picked up my fork again and took another bite of my pasta, chewing slowly, letting her sit in the silence. "Now," I said after I had swallowed, "you can see the way I spoke to you. I treated you with respect even though you did not earn it. So respectfully, take yourself away from this table and leave so I can finish my lunch in peace." Riley nodded, a jerky, mechanical motion, and then she stood up, her chair scraping against the floor.

chapters.title: Chapter 153
chapters.content:
Chapter 153 "Wow," I muttered to myself stabbing another forkful of pasta. "You cannot even take it, but you want to advise me? Double standards. You are all the same in that family. You, Julian, and your whore of a mother." The waiter brought my garlic bread and-Late in silence, the food good but the satisfaction of the conversation fading as the reality of what was coming tomorrow settled back into my chest. I finished my meal, paid the bill, but I did not get up.

I just sat there at the corner table, staring at the condensation on my water glass, watching the bubbles rise and pop, feeling the weight of the afternoon press down on me. I did not want to go back to Helix. The environment now reminded me of what Seraphine had done earlier, the way she had stormed into the lab and tried to humiliate me. Yes, I had triumphed. Yes, I had shown the video and turned the tables on her. But Julian was in that video. He was still my husband, or at least he was for now, and everyone at Helix knew it.

I could feel their pitying glances already, the way they looked at me when I walked, the whispers that now followed me down the hallways. It made my stomach turn. But that was not really why I did not want to go back. The heaviness in my chest had nothing to do with Julian or Seraphine or the gossiping staff. It had everything to do with Dominic. Because tomorrow evening, I would have the conversation with him. And after that, it would be truly goodbye. No more excuses. No more reasons to see him.

Just the memory of what we had done together and the hollow space where something might have grown if I had let it. I sat there until I got fed up with my own company, the silence of the restaurant becoming suffocating instead of soothing, and then I paid and walked back to Helix. The walk did nothing to clear my head. If anything, the afternoon sun and the gentle breeze only made me feel more detached from my body, like I was watching myself move through the world from a great distance. When I got back, I found Pat in the main lab and told her I was retiring for the day.

She gave me a knowing look, something sympathetic and understanding in her eyes, but she did not press. She just nodded and said she would handle everything. I went to my room, closed the door, and lay down on the bed fully dressed/ My mind would not shut up. It kept replaying everything, my conversations with Dominic, the way he looked at me, the way his hands felt on my body, the way he said my name like it was something precious. The memories ran through my head like a film reel I could not stop, each one sharper and more vivid than the last.

I kept asking myself the same question over and over. Why did I feel so strongly toward someone I had barely known? We had not known each other intimately for long. But I could not stop thinking about him. Every time I closed my eyes, I saw his face. A knock on my door pulled me out of the spiral. I looked at the clock on my nightstand. Seven in the evening. Earlier than I usually went to bed, but I would have been fine falling asleep right then and there. "Who is it?" I called out. "It is me, Pat." I got up and opened the door.

chapters.title: Chapter 154
chapters.content:
Chapter 154 CELESTE I followed Pat out to the lobby and stopped dead in my tracks. Julian was standing there, surrounded by more bouquets of roses than I had ever seen in one place. Red roses, white roses, pink roses, yellow roses, peach roses, lavender roses, orange roses, bouquets of every color and size arranged around him like he was standing in the middle of a flower shop that had exploded. The scent hit me like a physical force, cloying and sweet and overwhelming, filling every corner of the room.

I counted quickly, my eyes scanning the sea of petals, and I estimated there had to be at least a hundred bouquets, probably more. The staff who were working overnight had come out of their stations to watch, their faces a mixture of curiosity and awkwardness. A few people who had already been given accommodation in the dorms had also wandered out, drawn by the commotion. Julian himself looked terrible. His face was pale, almost gray, dark circles under his eyes, his clothes rumpled like he had slept in them.

He looked like a man who had just walked out of a hospital, which, according to Riley, he had. He walked toward me and then dropped to his knees right there in the middle of the lobby, his knees hitting the floor with a thud that echoed through the silent room. The staff gasped, a collective intake of breath that rippled through the crowd. "Celeste," he said, his voice hoarse and cracked. "I know this is nothing. It is probably nothing to you, but it is just a gesture. I need you to understand how deeply I regret what I have done. How much I still feel for you. Please.

Please give us another chance." I stared at him, this man who had once been the center of my entire world, and I felt nothing but a cold, clean emptiness. He was on his knees, surrounded by flowers, in front of an audience of strangers, begging for forgiveness, and he looked so pathetic that I almost felt sorry for him. "Get up, Julian," I said, my voice flat. "You are embarrassing yourself." "I do not care," he said, and there were tears in his eyes now, spilling down his cheeks. "I do not care who sees me like this. I made a mistake, Celeste.

I gave in to Seraphine's temptation and I was weak. But I love you. I have always loved you. Please. Just give me one chance to make it right." "Stop," I said, and the word cut through his pleading like a blade. "It was not just Seraphine, Julian. Stop using the excuse of being seduced to put all the blame on her. It takes two to tango, and you were more than willing to dance. But like I said this morning, and like I will keep saying until it sinks into your thick skull, we have crossed a line that cannot be uncrossed. We cannot go back.

So this stunt you are pulling now, the flowers, the kneeling, the public display. Do not try it again. The next time, I will have security throw you out. I do not care who you are." I turned around and walked away, my heels clicking against the floor in a steady rhythm that matched the pounding of my heart. Julian called my name behind me, his voice cracking, desperate, pleading, but I did not stop. I kept walking until I reached my room, stepped inside, and locked the door behind me. I leaned against the door, my eyes closed, my breath coming in short, sharp bursts.

The image of Julian on his knees, surrounded by a hundred bouquets, the eyes of the staff fixed on me, the whispers that would follow. It made my blood boil Seraphine, Riley, and now Julian, all of them turning me into a topic of conversation, a piece of gossip for people to chew on instead of doing their work. I spent the rest of the night lying in bed, staring at the ceiling, my mood sour and my mind restless. When I finally fell asleep, it was the kind of sleep that left me more exhausted than when I closed my eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 155
chapters.content:
Chapter 155 I reached for my phone and saw a text message from Dominic. It was an address, a location I did not fully recognize, followed by a brief note: "I have granted you access. Use your fingerprints when you arrive." I stared at the message, my brow furrowing. My fingerprints? How did he get my fingerprints? I had never given him my fingerprints. And why would he go through the trouble of setting that up? The question nagged at me, curiosity flickering through the gloom of my mood, and I felt the corners of my mouth twitch despite myself. "Wow, Dominic," I murmured to the empty room.

"You get more interesting by the day." But the smile did not last. It faded as quickly as it had appeared, replaced by the familiar weight of what I had to do. I got out of bed and went through my morning routine, showering, brushing my teeth, combing my hair. I planned to focus my attention on work until it was time to leave. I did not want to allow any distractions. But when I walked into the main lab, I felt the eyes on me immediately.

The staff who had been there the night before, who had seen Julian on his knees surrounded by a hundred bouquets, who had witnessed the entire spectacle, they were all staring. Some whispered, their voices low enough that I could not make out the words but loud enough that I knew they were talking about me. Pat appeared at my side, her voice low and steady. "You know how the world works. It is normal for people to whisper. Give them a few days and it will all die down." "I know," I said, keeping my eyes fixed on the equipment in front of me. "I know my situation makes for juicy gossip.

I really cannot control what people say. It is just the looks of pity that are getting to me. They are making me upset and embarrassed." "Just forget about it," Pat said. "Focus on your work." But I could not focus. I tried running an experiment and mixed the wrong reagents. I tried recording data and wrote the wrong numbers. I tried following a protocol and skipped three steps. Pat watched me make mistake after mistake until finally she put her hand on my arm and stopped me mid-motion. "Listen to me," she said. "You should go back to your room and rest.

The fact that you are meeting with Dominic later, combined with everything Julian has put you through, has you on edge. You are snapping too easily and getting upset too quickly. Just go back to your room and rest until it is time." I let out a long breath, the tension in my shoulders sagging. "You are right. You are right." I went back to my room, stripped off my lab coat, and lay down on the bed. ordered lunch to be brought to me since I had not eaten all day.

The food came, I ate mechanically, tasting nothing, and then I sat there staring at the clock on my nightstand as the minutes crawled by. Each passing minute made my heart beat faster. This would probably be the most difficult conversation of my life. If I had known it would feel this heavy, I would have just sent a text to Dominic. After all, he already knew the arrangement was coming to an end. We had both known it from the beginning. A simple message would have sufficed. Thank you for everything. This is over. Goodbye. But I knew it would not have been proper.

It would have been a cheap, cowardly way to end something that had meant more to me than I wanted to admit. At three o'clock, I began to get ready. I had agreed to be at Dominic's place at four, and I did not want to be late. I pulled out my makeup bag and stared at it, the tubes and brushes and palettes that I had used to make myself beautiful for him before I put them in my drawer. What was the need? I was not going there to attract him. I was going there to put an end to our affair. There was no reason to look beautiful for that conversation.

chapters.title: Chapter 156
chapters.content:
Chapter 156 I combed my hair, looked at my bare face in the mirror, and nodded at my reflection. "Not bad. I will not really have to spend so much time there anyway. will just go, say a few words, and leave. Knowing Domink, he will not have much to say back. And then I will be gone." I took a deep breath and sat down to wait until it was a few minutes to four, then I got dressed. I did not pick a dress that showed off my figure. I did not pick anything tight or sexy. picked something plain, a simple navy shift dress that covered everything, no cleavage, no curves on display.

There was no need to look attractive for what I was about to do. It was better to look plain, forgettable, like a woman who was not trying to be seen. I sent Pat a text saying I was leaving and gave her a heads up. She replied almost immediately: "There is no need to text me updates since you are coming back directly. I will just get the juice from your mouth when you return." I smiled despite myself, shaking my head at her choice of words, and put my phone in my purse. I walked out of Helix into the late afternoon sun, the air warm and still, the parking lot quiet.

I was walking toward my car, keys in hand, my mind already rehearsing the words I would say to Dominic, when I saw a familiar figure approaching from the far end of the lot. I stopped, squinting against the light, and when the figure got closer, my face broke into a genuine smile. "Felix?" I called out, surprised and pleased. I had not seen my brother in a while. The last time we spoke was when he called to question me about visiting Seraphine at the hospital. I had been so angry that I blocked his number, but I had unblocked him eventually. He had not reached out since then.

I had not even told him the address of Helix's new location, and I had not done any full online marketing yet. How had he found me?" But I was happy to see him. Felix was the only sibling I had in this world. He and my mother were the only blood relatives I held dear. I started walking toward him, my smile widening. As he got closer, I realized something was wrong. His face was red, veins standing out on his forehead, his jaw clenched so tight I could see the muscles jumping beneath his skin.

He was walking, fast, too fast, his strides eating up the distance between us with an aggressive purpose that made my instincts prick up. I opened my mouth to speak, to ask him what was wrong, when he screamed at me. "How dare you, Celeste?" His voice was loud enough to echo across the parking lot, to draw the attention of anyone who might be nearby. "How could you do such a thing? How could you stoop so low and sleep with Seraphine's husband? When did you become so disgusting?" I felt my face harden, the smile evaporating like it had never been there. "Mind your tone, Felix.

Do not talk to me with such disrespect." To my surprise, he just lost it. His arm swung back and his hand connected with my cheek in a slap so hard that my head snapped to the side, my vision blurring, my ears ringing. I stumbled, my hand flying to my face, my eyes wide with shock. I could not believe it. My own brother. The same brother who had held my hand at our father's funeral. The same brother who had walked me down the aisle when I married Julian. The same brother who had never once raised his hand to me in his entire life, had slapped me across the face in the middle of a parking lot.

chapters.title: Chapter 157
chapters.content:
Chapter 157 SERAPHINE The sound of my own heartbeat filled the car as I sped away from Helix, my hands gripping the steering wheel so hard my knuckles had turned white, my vision blurred by more tears I refused to let fall. I had not stopped driving until I pulled into my driveway, killed the engine, and sat there in the silence, my chest heaving, my mind replaying every single second of what had just happened. Celeste had won that round. She had stood there with her calm face and her folded arms and her pitying eyes while I screamed and raged and made a spectacle of myself.

And worst of all, she had shown them the video. She had shown everyone the video of me and Julian, my naked body on that screen, my breasts bouncing, my pussy exposed, my face twisted in pleasure while Julian fucked me. Every person in that lobby had seen it. Pat had seen it. The security guards had seen it. The receptionist had seen it. And Celeste had stood there watching their faces, feeding on their shock, savoring my humiliation like it was a five-course meal. I got out of the car and walked to my front door, my legs heavy, my heart pounding.

The moment I stepped inside, I crumpled to the floor, my knees giving out, my body folding in on itself as the tears I had been holding back finally broke free. I sat there on the cold tile, my back against the door, and I cried until my throat was raw and my eyes were swollen and there was nothing left inside me but a cold, hard rage. I wiped my face with the back of my hand. I took a breath. Then another. And then I called Kingsley Duke. He answered on the second ring, his voice cautious, like he already knew this call was not going to be good. "Hello?" "Come to my house," I said.

"I need to speak to you." "I'm very busy right now. I'm working on a specimen and I cannot just drop everything." "Listen to me." My voice came out low and sharp, a blade wrapped in silk. "Do not push me. If you are not here in thirty minutes, I am going to drive back to Helix and I am going to walk through that building and I am going to tell every single person there that you are my spy. That you are the mole I planted in their laboratory.

That every piece of information I have about Celeste's schedule and Celeste's movements came directly from your mouth." The silence on the other end stretched long and thin, like a wire about to snap. "That will not be necessary," he said finally. "I will be at your place in less than thirty minutes." "Good." I hung up before he could say another word. I got to my feet and began to pace the living room, my heels clicking against the floor, my mind racing through the events of the afternoon. Celeste had known about me and Julian. She had known all along.

She had videos of us together, evidence she had been collecting, building a case against me while I walked around thinking I was the one in control. How long had she known? How long had she been planning this? And how had she gotten her hands on that footage? Dominic. He must have given it to her. He must have been the one who found the evidence and handed it over to Celeste like a gift, like a weapon, like a way for her to destroy me in front of everyone I had ever wanted to impress. That was why he divorced me. That was why he denied me in that interview.

That was why he looked at me like I was nothing Celeste must have found out about the affair first, she must have told Dominic and asked him to find the evidence Then, she seduced him and poisoned his mind against me and turned him into a stranger who did not recognize his own wife. I stopped pacing. My hands were shaking. Pat had been there too. Pat had stood beside Celeste the whole time, watching the video, watching me break down, and she had not said a single word in my defense. She had not told Celeste to stop. She had not tried to calm the situation.

She had just stood there like a loyal little dog, waiting for her master to give her a treat. And then she had slapped me. Pat, a nobody, a loser who +15 Bonus had nothing going for her except a dead-end job at a laboratory that would not amount to anything without my husband's money, had raised her hand and slapped me across the face in front of everyone. I touched my cheek where her palm had landed. The memory of the sting was still fresh. "I will destroy you, Pat," I whispered to the empty room. "I will destroy both of you." I was still pacing when Kingsley arrived.

He walked through the door looking uncomfortable, his hands in his pockets, his eyes darting around the room like he was looking for an escape route. I watched him from across the living room and I admitted to myself that he was handsome, tall and lean with eyes that caught the light, the kind of face that made women look twice. But handsome did not pay the bills. Handsome did not buy you a mansion or a car or the kind of life you saw in magazines. Handsome was useless if the man wearing it was broke.

chapters.title: Chapter 158
chapters.content:
Bonus Still, his presence improved my mood slightly. It was nice to have a beautiful thing in the room, even if that beautiful thing was poor and pathetic and completely af my mercy. "I need you to do something for me," said, getting straight to the point. "What is it?" "Within the next twenty-four hours, I want you to have sex with Pat. And I want you to bring me video footage of it." His face went through a series of changes. Confusion. Disbelief. Horror. His mouth opened and closed like a fish gasping for air. "What? No. No, no, no.

I cannot do something like that." "You agreed to the original plan." "The original plan was to spy on Celeste, befriend Pat and make her like me and report back to you. Not to film myself having sex with someone without their consent. That is completely different." "You sound like you feel sorry for Pat." I tilted my head, studying him. "You feel sorry for that old woman?" "It is not that. It is just that I cannot..." "Listen to me." I stepped closer, my voice dropping to something cold and hard. "I am giving you twenty-four hours. I do not care how you do it.

I do not care if you show your face in the video or not. But no matter what you have to do, you will get me that footage within the next twenty-four hours. Otherwise, I will walk into Helix tomorrow morning and I will tell Celeste and everyone else that you are the spy I planted in their laboratory. You will lose the job you treasure so much. You will lose your reputation. You will lose everything. So what is it going to be?" He stared at me, his jaw tight, his hands curling into fists at his sides.

For a moment I thought he might refuse, might tell me to go to hell, might walk out the door and leave me standing there with nothing. But then his shoulders dropped. His fists uncurled. And he nodded. "Fine. I will do it." "Good." "Is that all?" I walked toward him, closing the distance between us until I was standing right in front of him, close enough to see the pulse beating in his throat, close enough to smell the soap on his skin. I reached up and touched his cheek, my fingers trailing down his jaw, feeling the slight roughness of stubble beneath my fingertips.

"Actually," I said, my voice dropping to something softer, something silkier, "do you need some motivation?" I stood on my tiptoes and pressed my lips to his. He did not respond. His mouth was stiff, and unyielding. But I persisted, my lips moving against his, my tongue tracing the seam of his mouth until finally, reluctantly, he began to respond. Then suddenly, he pulled back. His eyes were dark, his breathing uneven, but his voice was steady when he spoke. "No. I am not interested in any form of motivation. You want me to set up Pat and get the video? I will do it.

Is that all?" I stepped back, hiding my surprise behind a cool smile. "Yes. That will be all for now." He turned and walked out without another word, the door clicking shut behind him. I stood there for a moment, staring at the closed door, feeling an odd mixture of satisfaction and irritation. He had turned me down. Kingsley Duke, a poor nobody who worked for a salary that would not even cover my monthly grocery bill, had turned me down. But it did not matter. He had agreed to do what I asked, and that was all that mattered.

If even I, with all my beauty and my status, could be attracted to Kingsley Duke's handsome face, how much more would a desperate old loser like Pat fall for him? This was going to be easier than I thought. +15 Bonus I went to the kitchen, poured myself a glass of wine, atid took out my phone. I scrolled through my contacts until I found the name I was looking for. Felix. Celeste's brother. I had saved his number years ago, back when I was still at university. I had never called him. Never texted him. Why would I? He was nothing.

chapters.title: Chapter 159
chapters.content:
159 SERAPHINE I waited until evening, watching the clock tick slowly toward the perfect hour. When the sun had set and the city lights were beginning to flicker on, I got dressed, grabbed my keys, and drove to a hotel. A nice place, not too fancy, not too cheap. The kind of place where a woman could check in alone without drawing too much attention. I booked a room on the fifth floor. Paid in cash. Gave a fake name. Then I went upstairs, unlocked the door, and stood by the window, looking out at the city below. I pulled out my phone. Called Felix.

He answered on the third ring, his voice cautious, the way people sound when they do not recognize the number on their screen. "Hello? Who is this?" I took a breath. Let it out in a shaky sigh. Then I let the tears come, the practiced tears I had perfected over years of manipulating men who thought they were too smart to be fooled. "Felix? It is me. I do not know if you remember me. I am Seraphine. Celeste's best friend." There was a pause. Then his voice came back, softer now, a flicker of recognition warming his tone. "Seraphine? Of course I remember you. What is wrong?

Why are you crying?" "Oh, it is nothing. I should not have called. I am sorry to bother you." "No, no, please. Tell me what is going on." "It is just..." I let my voice crack, let the tears thicken my words. "I am in trouble, Felix. I do not know who else to call. You are the only one I could think of." "What kind of trouble? Are you hurt?" "I need help. Please. I am not safe right now. I am going to die if you do not help me." "What? Where are you? Tell me where you are and I will come." I gave him the name of the hotel and the room number. "Please hurry.

I do not have much time." "I will be there as fast as I can. Stay on the phone with me." "No, I cannot. Just come. Please." I hung up before he could argue. I smiled at my reflection in the window. That was almost too easy. Felix had always had a crush on me, a desperate, pathetic crush that he thought he had hidden behind friendly smiles and polite conversations. But I had seen it. I had always seen it. The way his eyes lingered on me a little too long. The way his voice got softer when he spoke to me.

The way he found excuses to be near me, to touch me, to breathe the same air I was breathing. I had never given him the time of day because he was beneath me, a broke loser who could never give me the life I deserved. But now his pathetic little crush was finally going to be useful. I stood by the window, watching the gate of the hotel parking lot. Minutes passed. I checked my phone. Checked the window Checked my reflection in the glass. And then I saw him. A car pulled into the lot, a modest Mercedes. Felix got out, and I felt a small jolt of surprise when I saw him.

He looked better than I remembered. Taller. Broader. His shoulders filled out his shirt in a way that had not been there when we were in university. He had grown into his features, his jaw sharper, his posture more confident. He was not bad-looking, I admitted to myself. Not bad-looking at all. +15 Bonus I turned away from the window and walked to the small table where I had laid out the supplies. A glass of water. And a single pill.

She moved through the lab with purpose, her head held high, her eyes fixed on whatever task was in front of her.

I could not focus at all. I kept turning to look in her direction, my heart pounding, my hands trembling. The guilt was a physical weight in my chest, pressing down on my lungs, making it hard to breathe. Every time she smiled at someone, every time she laughed at a joke, I felt the knife twist deeper. And then my phone rang. I looked at the screen. Seraphine's name flashed at me, bright and insistent, and I felt a wave of hatred so strong that I nearly threw the phone across the room. But I did not.

I got up from my desk, walked to a quiet corner of the building where no one could hear me, and answered the call. "Kingsley," she said, her voice smooth and satisfied, like a cat that had just caught a mouse. "I hope you have what I asked for. Your twenty-four hours are up." "I have it," I said. "Good. I am in the parking lot. Walk toward the end, where the cars will shield you. Come and meet me. Do not keep me waiting. 11 She hung up before I could respond. +15 Bonus I stood there tor a moment, my phone clutched in my land, my heart hammering against my ribs.

chapters.title: Chapter 186
