Chapter 186 She looked at me as I approached, her eyes traveling over my face, my body, like she was assessing a piece of property she had just acquired. "You are really efficient," she said, her voice dripping with mock admiration. "You actually got the video? Hmm. And here I thought Pat was different. So cheap yet acting so righteous. In less than twenty-four hours, you were able to get her into your bed." I did not respond. I could not. My jaw was clenched so tightly that my teeth ached. "I need to see the footage," she said. "I want to know how good it is." I nodded.

I attached the flash drive to my phone, my fingers numb and clumsy. I opened the video file, kept the brightness low, moved over some scenes and pressed play. The screen flickered to life. Pat's face appeared. Her body. And then her moans filled the air between us, those soft, breathless sounds I had drawn from her with my mouth. I stopped the video immediately. Seraphine laughed, a low, delighted sound that made my skin crawl. "Why did you stop the video, Kingsley? Are you so shy? You must have done a very good job if she is moaning so passionately. Good.

Let me have the flash drive." I pulled the flash drive out of my phone and held it out to her. She took it from my fingers, her nails brushing against my skin, and she lifted her hand to tap my cheek, patronizing and smug. "I am so impressed with you, Kingsley. You are a reliable man. You will go places." She turned and began to walk away, her heels clicking against the asphalt, the flash drive clutched in her hand like a trophy. And I watched her go. But my mind was somewhere else. It was back in that hotel room. Back with Pat.

Back to the moment she had told me, "I am willing." Back to the blood on the sheets. Back to her kindness, her trust. She had given me something precious, and I had traded it to a woman who would use it to destroy her. I could not do it. I charged toward Seraphine. She was just opening her bag, just about to drop the flash drive inside, when I reached her. I snatched it out of her hand. She spun around, her eyes wide, her mouth open in shock. "What are you doing?" she demanded. I did not answer.

I threw the flash drive onto the ground, raised my foot, and brought my heel down on it as hard as I could. The plastic cracked beneath my shoe. I stomped on it again, and again, grinding it into the asphalt until it was nothing but splintered pieces. And then I bent down and gathered every single fragment into my hand, every piece of plastic and metal, leaving nothing behind. Seraphine stared at me, her face twisted with rage. "What the hell is wrong with you, Kingsley? What do you think you are doing?" "I will not let myself become this person," I said, my voice trembling but firm.

"This is the only copy I kept. And I have destroyed it. I will not let you use it against Pat." "What the hell is wrong with you?" she repeated, her voice rising, cracking. "You already did what I asked. You already did what I wanted. You brought me the evidence. Why did you have to destroy it? Now I will have to go into Helix and reveal to everyone that you are my spy." I swallowed. My throat was dry. "Fine," I said. "Do whatever you want. But I will not ruin Pat's life. You are a monster" Her face contorted. For a moment, I thought she might strike me.

But she just stood there, her hands clenched into fists, her chest heaving, her eyes blazing with fury. +15 Bonus I turned and walked away. I did not look back. I did not stop until I was inside Helix, the glass doors sliding shut behind me, separating the from her and everything she represented. I went straight to the incinerator room. The door was heavy, metal, cold beneath my fingers. I pushed it open and crossed to the machine in the corner. I stuffed some papers inside, old reports and documents that no one would miss.

Chapter 187 I let out a breath I did not realize I had been holding. The guilt was still there. It would always be there. But I had done the right thing in the end. I had chosen her over myself. Except now I needed that money. I needed that bonus. And I had just destroyed my only leverage with Seraphine. She would tell everyone I was her spy. She would make sure I never worked in this city again. And I had nothing to show for it except a clear conscience and a heart full of shame. I walked back to my desk. Slowly. Each step felt heavier than the last.

I sat down and stared at my computer screen, the cursor blinking at me, waiting for me to do something. I could not stay here. Not after everything. Not with the knowledge that Seraphine could walk in at any morhent and expose me. I opened a new document and typed my resignation letter. It was short. Formal. No explanation. Just the words, "I am writing to formally resign from my position at Helix Research Laboratory, effective immediately." I printed it, signed it, and folded it in half. Celeste was not around.

So I walked to Pat's desk, the letter clutched in my hand, my heart pounding so hard I thought I might pass out. She looked up as I approached, and she smiled. That same warm, open smile she had given me on my first day at Helix. "Hey," she said. "What is up?" I handed her the letter. "This is my resignation letter. I cannot work here anymore." Her smile vanished. "Why? What happened, Kingsley?" I shook my head. "I have no reason. I just... I just." "You just what?" Every head in the lab turned toward us. I could feel their stares, their curiosity, their judgment.

Pat grabbed my hand and pulled me away, through the lab and into her private office. She closed the door behind us and turned to face me, her arms crossed, her eyes searching my face. "Where is this coming from?" she asked, her voice soft but firm. "Is it because of what happened earlier? Listen to me, Kingsley. You do not need to feel pressured, okay? I am not asking you to take responsibility or date me or anything. I did it because I wanted to help you out of the situation. It means nothing, okay? I do not have any expectations of you." "I know," I said.

"I know you do not." But I could not bear it. I looked at Pat, at the concern in her eyes, the kindness, the trust she still had in me despite everything I had done. And I made a decision. "Listen to me, Pat," I said, my voice low and urgent. "You are a very nice person. You are kind. And you deserve better. I am sorry. I am really, truly sorry. Please forgive me, if it is possible." "Kingsley, what are you talking about?" "Also, I want you to watch your back. Seraphine is out to get you.

Chapter 188 DOMINIC I had been pacing the length of my living room for what felt like hours, my feet pressing into the cold floor, my mind a tangled mess of thoughts I could not seem to untangle. Ever since Celeste had left after that night Julian and Seraphine saw what we had been doing, I had been unable to sit still. I wanted to open my heart to her. I wanted to tell her that she had become more to me than I had ever expected, more than I had ever allowed myself to want. But she was still married to Juhan.

Every time I thought about professing my love to her, while she was still legally bound to someone who did not deserve to breathe the same air as her, I felt sick. How could I do that to her? How could I put her in a position where she would feel pressured to give me an answer before she was ready? I thought about different ideas, different ways to bring her closer, to create an opportunity where I could show her what she meant to me without forcing the words out before their time.

And finally, after pacing for so long that my feet had gone numb, I settled on something so pathetic I almost laughed at myself. I decided I would call her and tell her I was sick. That I had no one to take care of me. That I needed her. It was low, even for me, a man who had built an empire on calculated moves and strategic deceptions. But I did not think I had any other choice. I was desperate, and desperation made fools of even the sharpest men.

But before I could pick up my phone and dial her number, before I could put my ridiculous plan into motion, my phone rang in my hand and her name appeared on the screen. Celeste. I stared at it for a moment, my heart lurching in my chest, and then I answered. She told me she wanted to see me. She said it would be the next day, in the evening. I almost bit through my lip because I already had plans, important plans that I could not simply cancel without consequence.

My grandmother was finally arriving after years of being away, years I had kept her hidden in a different city with a different family, years of pretending she did not exist so that no one could use her against me. Now that my identity was out in the open, now that everything was balanced and the threats had been neutralized, it was time for her to return. And around the same time Celeste said she would be coming, I was supposed to pick my grandmother up from the airport and bring her home. But I did not hesitate. I could not let this opportunity slip through my fingers.

I did not know when I would get another chance to have Celeste in my space, in my home, alone with me. So I accepted immediately, my voice calm and steady even as my mind raced to rearrange everything I had planned. I called my driver, I made arrangements for my grandmother to be taken to a different mansion tomorrow. I prepared maids and a chet and everything she could possibly need. I told myself it was only for one night, that I would see her the following day and give her a reason, that she would understand. Then I began to think about how I would handle Celeste when she arrived.

The best plan, I decided, was to seduce her. It felt oddly uncomfortable, the idea of asking her outright about her feelings, of laying my heart bare before her when she was still wearing another man's name. But what if I showed her instead of telling her? I knew she was attracted to me. I could see it in the way her pupils dilated when she looked at me, in the way her breath caught when I touched her, in the way her body responded to mine even when her mind was still trying to resist. But she was a strong-willed woman and that could not be enough.

So I put effort into my appearance, more effort than I had put into anything in years. I spent time in front of the mirror, making sure every detail was perfect, every strand of hair in place, every muscle defined under the careful drape of my clothes, all the while, looking casual so she would not be suspicious. No. No, no, no, I could not let this happen. Not now, not after she had finally said the words I had been dreaming of hearing. "Celeste," I called out, my voice rough She turned and looked at me, her face carefully blank. "I was not planning on staying long anyway. So good night." Good night? The universe had handed me her confession on a silver platter and my grandmother had snatched it away before I could even savor it. I rushed toward her, not caring that I was still wearing nothing but a towel, not caring that my grandmother and Imelda were watching me with wide eyes. I stopped Celeste by the door, my hand closing around hers, and I said, "Please, don't leave, Celeste. Please stay." She shook her head, her eyes avoiding mine. "I cannot, Dominic. You have important guests. And besides, it is getting really +15 Bonus late.

I do not want to move at night." "Then please stay the night," I told her. She let out a laugh that was more disbelief than amusement. "Stay the night? Can you listen to yourself? Your grandmother and your fiancée are already here and you are asking me to stay the night." "Please, Celeste. Stay the night." I was begging now, I could hear it in my own voice, and I did not care. "I need you. I really need you." She stared at me for a long moment, her eyes searching mine. She looked down at my hand holding hers, then back toward my grandmother, then back at me. And finally, she nodded. "Fine.

All of a sudden your driver told me that he was taking us to a different address. If I had not taken note of this address when we spoke, you would have tricked me." "Granny, what are you saying?" "I would have still come tomorrow to see you, okay? You both cannot stay here tonight." "No, I just came. This is my grandson's house. I am not leaving." She crossed her arms, her chin lifting in that stubborn gesture I remembered from my childhood. "And we are very hungry. So you need to find something for us to eat." "Granny, you know I hate cooking," I said. "There is no way I can go into the kitchen to make food for both of you." "You hate cooking but you cooked for this girl?" "This is different. I planned for it, it didn't happen unexpectedly. Besides, Imelda is here.

If you guys are hungry, Imelda can cook for both of you." "But I don't know how to cook," Imelda complained, her voice small and whiny. "I've never cooked before." I turned my attention back to Celeste, who had barely touched her food. She was pushing it around her plate with her fork, her eyes distant, her movements mechanical. "Go on, Celeste. Eat. The moment Celeste disappeared, Imelda slid over to the table and opened the pots that Celeste had not bothered to touch. She began scooping food onto a plate for herself, and when she took her first bite, her eyes widened. "Wow, Granny, Dominic's cooking is so delicious. You have to taste this. Seriously." My grandmother smiled and went to sit beside her, reaching for a plate.

She turned to look at me, her expression shifting from pleasure to disappointment. "You ruined my plans today, Granny," I said, my voice flat. "And you know how upset I get when my plans are ruined." "Dominic, I am really disappointed in you," she replied, her voice heavy with reproach. "Do you remember the conversation we had months ago? You said yes to this alliance. If you had not agreed, I would not have brought Imelda all the way here. Back home, she is treated like a princess. Do you know how good her family has been to me? Felix is cheating on me. I am two months pregnam I could not shake the image of Sierra's tear-streaked face, the way her hands had trembled as she spoke, the desperation in her voice when she talked about the child growing inside her. My brother had done this.

My brother had abandoned his pregnant fiancée on the side of the road to go and fuck Seraphine, the same woman who had been spreading her legs for all the men in the world. Sierra was carrying my niece or nephew, and Felix was too busy chasing after a snake to care. I had always wanted children, had always dreamed of the day I would hold my own baby in my arms, but Julian had convinced me to wait, to push that joy further and further away until it became a distant hope I no longer reached for.

But now there was about to be a child in the family, even if it was not directly from me, and I would be damned if I let Seraphine destroy that child's future before it even had a chance to be born. The promise I had made to Sierra echoed in my mind. I give you my word. I will get that woman out of Felix's life. Just be patient and give me some time. I had said those words with conviction, but as I drove through the familiar streets of my childhood neighborhood, I realized I had no idea how I was going to keep that promise.

There were lines I did not want to cross, things I was not willing to do, but Seraphine had gone too far. I pulled into my mother's driveway and parked, taking a moment to compose myself before I stepped out of the car. My mother came out of the house before I even reached the front door, her arms open wide, and she pulled me into a hug that smelled like home and safety and the kind of love that never asked questions. "I was about to call you to ask what was going on," my mother said, holding me at arm's length to look at my face.

"You said you would be here in a few minutes and that was hours ago." "I am sorry, Mom," I said, following her into the house. I had initially called her after I left Dominic's house, telling her I would come see her soon, but the conversation with Pat and then the stop at Sierra's apartment had taken much longer than I expected. "I got held up." "Don't worry about it, darling. Come, sit down." We settled into the living room, the familiar furniture and the smell of my mother's cooking wrapping around me like a blanket.

She sat across from me, her eyes searching my face, and I could see the worry lines etched into her forehead. "So, have you had breakfast yet?" she asked. "I have not, but I will have something later." "Why? I already prepared something for you." "Mom, I came so we could talk..." "I will be right back," she said, already on her feet and heading toward the kitchen before I could protest. I sat there, listening to the sounds of pots and pans clattering, and I knew better than to argue with my mother when she had decided to feed me.

She came back a few minutes later with a plate of steaming food, the aroma making my stomach growl despite my nerves. "Come on, have breakfast," she said, setting the plate in front of me. "Mom, you are going to make me feel guilty. How can you cook for me? I should be the one doing this." My mother chuckled, the sound warm and familiar. "Celeste, no matter how much you grow up, you will always be my little +15 Bonus Princess. Besides, you have always loved my cooking to death.

Do you remember when you were about to get married and you were so sad because you knew you would no longer have access to my food like always? I told you that you could always come over and eat whenever you wanted, but you did not really do that." "I am sorry, Mom. There was just so much going on. I should have spent more time with you. I should have come home more often." She just smiled at me. I smiled back and picked up my fork, taking a bite of the food. The flavors exploded on my tongue and I let out a soft moan of appreciation. "I have missed this so much.

chapters.title: Chapter 203
chapters.content:
Chapter 203 My Mom just watched me with a satisfied smile as I ate, and for a few minutes, flet myself forget about all the chaos that had become my life I just ate my mother's food and pretended I was a little girl again, safe and untroubled. When I was done, I cleared and washed the dishes, my mother hovering nearby like she was afraid I would disappear if she looked away. We went back to the living room and sat down, and I knew the time for pleasantries was over. "Alright, so tell me," my mother said. "What is going on?" "Let me show you something first," I said.

I pulled out my phone and found the videos of Seraphine and Julian in bed together. I handed the phone to my mother and watched her face as she watched the footage, her expression shifting from curiosity to disgust to something close to horror. "Why do you have videos like this in your phone?" she asked, handing the phone back to me like it was contaminated. "Mom, the main issue here is that Seraphine was having an affair with Julian." My mom was quiet for a moment, her lips pressed into a thin line. "You do not seem surprised, Mom." I told her. She let out a long breath.

"Your brother Felix called me earlier. Do you know what he told me? He said you've been having an affair with Seraphine's husband. He said you would try to turn things around and claim that Seraphine is the one having an affair with your husband, and asked me to be wary because it would all be lies you made up to cover your tracks." "That is ridiculous," I said, my voice sharp. "Mom, Felix has completely lost his mind. You know he slapped me yesterday because Seraphine told him lies about me?" "What?" "Felix raised his hand to me. Right outside my new Lab.

He believed Seraphine's lies without even asking me for my side of the story. Look at my face, Mom. If you look closely, you can still see the marks from his slap." My mom's face went pale, then red, her hands clenching into fists in her lap. She was breathing hard, her chest rising and falling with barely contained fury. "Calm down, Mom. Let me tell you everything from the beginning." I told her the whole story. I told her about Julian and Seraphine's affair, about the videos Dominic had shown me, about the agreement Dominic and I had made to get revenge on both of them.

My mother listened without interrupting, her eyes fixed on my face, her expression shifting through a dozen emotions I could not name. When I was done, she got up and began to pace, her footsteps heavy against the floor. "I cannot believe this," she said, her voice tight. "In all of this, what upsets me the most is Felix. He is supposed to protect you He is your older brother.

How could he listen to Seraphine and come to your workplace and lay his hands on you?" I wanted to tell her about Sierra's pregnancy, about Felix abandoning his fiancée to go and sleep with Seraphine, but I decided against it. My mother was already upset enough, and I did not want to add more fuel to the fire Not yet. "So you can see, Mom..." "Slow down," my mother said, stopping her pacing to look at me. "But seriously, Celeste? Sleeping with Dominic? I mean, I understand what Seraphine and Julian did was wrong.

If you do not want to be with Julian anymore, I would understand that completely. No woman should tolerate such disrespect. But two wrongs can never make a right, Celeste Sleeping with Seraphine's husband because she slept with yours, that is not the kind of thing people like us do. We are bigger than that. You are bigger than that. Do not do such things." "Mom, this is not about revenge on Julian and Seraphine anymore." +15 Bonus "What are you talking about?" I reached out and took my mother's hands, looking her straight in the eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 204
chapters.content:
Chapter 204 CELESTE I got to my feet, my heart hammering against my ribs. "Felix, what are you doing here?" "I came to see Mom. And I heard everything. So you came here to tell Mom lies and make yourself look innocent?" He was still speaking when he charged toward me, his hands reaching for my throat. He slammed me against the wall, his fingers wrapping around my neck, squeezing so hard that could feel my windpipe closing, my breath coming in short, desperate gasps. "Felix, let her go!" my mother screamed, hitting him on the back with her fists. "Let her go right now!" "No, Mom. I knew it.

I said it. Celeste was sleeping with Seraphine's husband. Now she has admitted it. She wants to be with him because of his money. She is nothing but a gold-digging whore..." I did not let him finish. I brought my knee up as hard as I could, connecting with his balls with every ounce of strength I had left. His grip on my throat loosened immediately and he crumpled to the ground, his hands cupping himself as he groaned in pain. I doubled over, gasping for air, my mother's hands on my back, steadying me.

When I finally caught my breath, I straightened up and glared down at Felix, who was still writhing on the floor. "Mom, everything I have told you is the truth," I said, my voice hoarse but steady. "I want to be with Dominic and he wants to be with me too. No one is going to stop me." Felix got to his feet, his face purple with rage, and he pointed a shaking finger at me. "You..." But I had already reached into my bag. I pulled out the pepper spray I always carried and aimed it at his face, pressing the button and watching the cloud of vapor hit him square in the eyes.

He screamed, stumbling backward, clawing at his face as the burning sensation spread across his skin. My Mom stood frozen, tears in her eyes as she watched her children tear each other apart. "Look at you," I said, my voice dripping with contempt. "You are nothing but a disgrace. You are upset with me, telling me that I had sex with Seraphine's husband? So you do believe Seraphine is a married woman, and yet you went and had sex with her anyway?" "What are you talking about?" my mother asked, her voice barely a whisper. "Mom, Felix is nothing but a two-faced hypocrite.

Guess where he was two nights ago. He was having sex with Seraphine. He abandoned Sierra on the road, on their way to pick out wedding rings, to go and run to Seraphine. He spent the whole night with her. And now he is standing here acting high and mighty, trying to please his lover so he can keep having sex with her. He is nothing but Seraphine's puppet." Felix shook his head, still blinking away the effects of the pepper spray. "No, Mom. It is not true. It is all Celeste's fault. If she had not tried to kill Seraphine... If she had not drugged her..." I let out a sharp laugh.

"Can you listen to yourself? You sound like an idiot. I tried to kill Seraphine? I drugged her? And out of all the people in the world, she thought of calling you? You, who have not had contact with her in years? Your stupid little brain did not tell you that she was using you? Mom, do you know that Felix has a child on the way? Sierra is pregnant with his baby. But he did not even think twice about the woman he was going to marry in a few months. He went out and had sex with Seraphine.

chapters.title: Chapter 205
chapters.content:
Chapter 205 "Where is the proof?" Momasked, her voice cold. "Where is the proof that Celeste drugged her? Seraphine told you that and you just believed it?" "Mom, the most important thing here is that Seraphine and Dominic are no longer married," I said, drawing my mother's attention back to me. "Do you know why? Because Dominic divorced her cheating ass. Mom, I was on my own the day Dominic called me and told me about Julian's affair with Seraphine. I went to the location and I saw them with my own two eyes, right there, outdoors, fucking each other." 1 I turned to Felix.

"How do you think I got all the evidence I have? Dominic gave it to me. He already served Seraphine divorce papers and they are already divorced. There is nothing between them anymore. So if I want to be with Dominic, I am doing nothing wrong. Afterall, Julian and I are in the process of getting a divorce, Since Julian and Seraphine want to be together so badly, let them have their way. Dominic and I couldn't care less about them. But you, Felix? You are an idiot. A puppet being used by Seraphine like a toy." "Enough with the lies," Felix yelled, his voice cracking.

"Seraphine already told me you would say all of these lies. When you and Seraphine first met Dominic years ago, you were interested in him. But because you thought he was poor, you ignored him and you ended up setting him up with Seraphine. Then Julian came along and you quickly married him because he was a millionaire. Now the moment you found out Dominic is a billionaire, you left Julian and ran to Dominic. You are creating all of these stories because there is no end to your greed, Celeste.

You just want to be at the top, to be married to the richest man and enjoy all his wealth." I stared at him, and despite everything, I felt a smile spread across my face. "At the very least, according to your theory, I am using my brains. But what are you doing with yours? Seraphine called you and claimed that I drugged her. And just like that, you believed her without a second thought. That is the first sign to convince you that you are a fool.

The second sign is that you were with your fiancée on the way to get rings for your wedding and you kicked her out of your car, knowing she is pregnant, to go and spend the night with Seraphine. Have you even called Sierra since then? Do you even know how she is feeling? Do you even care about the baby on the way? No. You are the most stupid man I have ever seen." "Shut up! Enough, Celeste! Do not make me more upset than I already am. This act you are putting on will only work on Mom, not me. You think I'm speaking without proof? I took Seraphine to the hospital for crying out loud.

I saw her test results. She almost died because of you. Or are you going to say she did that to herself? Because Seraphine already predicted that you would say that. Let me tell you, I've already figured out the kind of person you are Celeste." "Fine," I said, my voice flat. "Then let us not drag this any further. Felix, you make me sick. I am disgusted that I am related to a fool like you." "Celeste!" His words carried a warning tone. "You are pushing me to the..." "Listen to me, Felix, and listen well." I cut him off.

"From today, you and I share no relationship anymore Whatever bond we have as brother and sister, I am severing it today. You have no right to interfere in my affairs or my life anymore. If you as much as come an inch close to me or try to lay your hands on me again, you will end up in jail or the ICU. I assure you, Felix. Last time you hit me, I let it go for Mom's sake. But now I have severed all ties between us. If you dare come close to me again, you will be sorry. And yes, I have Dominic Ford behind me.

chapters.title: Chapter 206
chapters.content:
c Chapter 206 I turned to my mother, my voice softening. "Mom, I am very sorry. I genuinely planned for this moment to be pleasant, but there is a stranger here and don't feel comfortable saying what I want to say. But Mom, you have to trust me, okay? Twill not do anything against my conscience, and I have not done anything wrong. The ones who have offended me are the ones who should be worrying. I only refuse to sit down and take whatever they throw at me. Since they want to play a game with my life, I will show them that I can play it even better.

Mom, I know you are hurt that I have severed ties with this fool. But he had it coming. For a long time I have overlooked a lot of things, especially his stupid obsession with Seraphine. And now, after finding out what he did to Sierra, knowing she is pregnant with his child, I feel sick to my stomach. I cannot acknowledge that I am related to him. I will call you and find time for us to talk properly." "But Celeste, this Dominic..." "Do not worry, Mom. I will tell you more about him at the proper time.

And do not worry, I will bring him to see you eventually." My mother looked troubled, her eyes flickering between me and Felix, but I pulled her into my arms and whispered into her ear. "Dominic already confessed to me, Mom. He said he is in love with me and I feel the same way about him. You should be happy for us." When I pulled away, my mother let out a long sigh. "So you are telling me that you are happy?" "Mom, this is the happiest I have been in my entire life." "Alright then," she said, her voice soft. "As long as you are happy, I am happy.

I will see you around." I turned and looked at Felix, who was standing there staring at me with pure hatred in his eyes. I stared back at him with nothing but contempt, and then I turned, unlocked the door, and stepped out into the fresh air. "Goodbye, Mom. I will call you." I got into my car and started the engine, my hands still trembling from the adrenaline. I pulled away from the curb and began to drive, my mind racing through everything that had just happened. And then a thought struck me. Where were my bodyguards?

Dominic had assigned them to follow me everywhere, but I had not seen them today. If Felix had locked the door, they could have easily kicked it down if they had been there. But they had not come. Which meant they were not with me. I reached for my phone, intending to call Dominic and ask him if he had called the bodyguards back, but before I could unlock the screen, an arm shot out from the back seat and locked around my throat, yanking me hard against the headrest.

I clawed at the arm digging into my windpipe, my nails tearing into skin, the car swerving across the lane as I fought to keep one hand on the wheel while the other hand scratched and grabbed and searched for anything to hurt whoever had me. Whoever it was said nothing. No threats, no demands, just cold, practiced silence, the kind that told me this was not the first time they had done this. I slammed my foot down on the brake and threw my elbow back with everything I had, felt it connect with something solid, but the arm around my throat only tightened harder.

chapters.title: Chapter 207
chapters.content:
Chapter 207 CELESTE The first thing I registered was the ache in my shoulders, a dull throbbing that traveled up my neck and settled behind my eyes. The second thing was the rough texture of rope biting into my wrists, the kind of friction that promised bruises before I even opened my eyes to confirm my situation. I forced my lids apart and the world swam into focus. A ceiling I did not recognize. Walls painted a pale yellow that felt deliberately cheerful in a way that made my stomach turn.

was sitting on a wooden chair, my arms pulled behind my back, the rope wrapped around my wrists so tight that my fingers had started to tingle. Kidnapped. The word landed in my chest like a stone dropped into still water, sending ripples of cold dread through every part of me. Seraphine. That was the first name that surfaced, the most obvious conclusion. Who else would want me tied to a chair in a Who else stranger's house? Who else had the combination of spite and boldness to pull something like this off? Julian had been begging for my forgiveness. He would not dare. But Seraphine?

She had already tried to destroy me once. This was just the sequel. I tested the rope again, wincing as it bit into my skin. My fingers were already going numb. I needed to think. I needed to get out of here before whoever did this came back. And then I remembered the bracelet. The silver cuff Dominic had slid onto my wrist three days ago, his fingers lingering against my pulse point as he fastened it." Keep this on," he had said. "Always." I had assumed it was a gift, a piece of jewelry chosen for its delicate shimmer.

But when I had examined it later, I had found the tiny catch, the hidden blade no longer than my thumbnail but sharp enough to slice through most things. I twisted my arm, feeling for the clasp. My fingers brushed against it and I almost sobbed with relief. I adjusted my angle, pressing the hidden blade against the rope, and began to saw. The motion was awkward, my wrists bound too close together for proper leverage, but I kept at it, feeling the fibers give way millimeter by millimeter. The door swung open. Light flooded the room, a harsh overhead bulb that made me squint.

A figure stepped through and I blinked repeatedly, trying to adjust, trying to make sense of the silhouette moving toward me. My eyes cleared. I stared. Of all the faces I had expected to see, hers was not on the list. Not even close. "Seriously?" The word came out as a scoff, disbelief bleeding into my voice. "You? Elizabeth?" Julian's mother stood before me, her arms crossed over her chest, a smile playing at the corners of her lips that made my skin crawl.

She was dressed casually, a simple blouse and slacks, as if kidnapping your daughter-in-law was just another errand her daily to-do list. "Yes, it's me, Celeste." She stepped closer, her heels clicking against the wooden floor. "What? You did not expect that I was going to kidnap you, did you?" Before I could answer, another figure appeared in the doorway. My breath caught. Riley. She stepped into the room slowly, her eyes wide, her face pale. She looked from me to her mother and back again, confusion written across her features in bold strokes.

+15 Bonus "Mam, what are you doing?" Riley's voice was sharp, unsteady. "You said you wanted to show me something. You kidnapped Celeste? Why would you do this?" Elizabeth turned to face Trek daughter, her expression softening into something that was supposed to look reasonable and only succeeded in looking unhinged. "Listen to me, Riley. Your brother will not give up on Celeste until I show him what she really is.

Until I show him how disgusting she can get." "What are you going to do?" Riley asked, and I could hear the war in her voice, the part of her that wanted to walk out and the part that was too afraid to defy her mother. Elizabeth reached into her bag and pulled out a small transparent nylon pouch filled with white pills. She held it up like a trophy, letting the light catch the plastic. "Here. There are so many pills in here. I am just going to feed them to her, and then, since she is a whore who loves being with men so much, I will arrange the men in the other room for her.

I just need to let them out and give her the opportunity to have fun with them. I will record all of it and send it to Julian. Once he sees this, he will let her go as quickly as possible. So, what do you think of my plan?" I let out a low chuckle, the sound surprising even me. My eyes darted around the room, cataloging every detail. My handbag was slumped against the wall near the far end of the room, close to the window. If I could get to it... "Really?" I said, my voice dripping with disdain.

chapters.title: Chapter 208
chapters.content:
Chapter 208 "Watch your mouth," she missed. "I will not tolerate any disrespect from you." "Disrespect?" I laughed, turning my head back to meet her eyes. "Since when did telling the truth become disrespect?" "Stop it, Celeste," Riley said, taking a step forward. "You stop it, Riley." I fixed my gaze on her, holding it. "Oh, don't tell me you're not aware your mother is a whore." Riley's face flushed crimson. Her hands curled into fists at her sides. "You think I am joking?" I continued, the words pouring out of me now, hot and fast and unstoppable. "Go ahead, Riley.

Ask your mother who the real father of Julian is. Go on. Ask her." Riley turned to stare at her mother. The silence stretched, thick and uncomfortable. "You are talking rubbish," Elizabeth raged, but her voice had lost its edge. "Rubbish!" I smiled, slow and deliberate. "I did my research on you, Elizabeth. I know your favorite bar. I know you used to be a prostitute. Everyone knows it. Everyone also knows you were obsessed with a man called Bull. Your current husband walked into the bar one day and you figured out he was loaded, so you started throwing yourself at him.

Not knowing any better, he thought you were a decent woman and started something with you. You got pregnant for Bull, but pinned it on him. The poor millionaire married you. You should have stopped there, Elizabeth, but no. Your shame was not enough. You even got pregnant with another man's baby, not even Bull's, and gave birth to Riley." Riley's face had gone white. She shook her head slowly, backing away from her mother. "No. No, this cannot be true." "But it is true, Riley." I kept my voice steady, kept my eyes locked on hers.

"When I first met Julian and your mother started making life difficult for me, I figured there had to be something about this woman. I mean, a normal, right-thinking person cannot be so vicious for no reason. So I decided to look into her background. Trust me, I was not expecting what I found out. Even after being married to your father all these years, your mother has still been fucking around.

Keeping so many men by her side." "What do you know?" Elizabeth screamed, her composure finally cracking "If my husband was not so infertile, I would not have had to have children from other men." I chuckled. "Riley, you see. You and Julian share the same mother, but two different fathers. Elizabeth is nothing but a whore who cannot do without men. So if anyone needs those men she just spoke about, it is her." "Shut up," Elizabeth snarled. She pulled out her phone and thrust it into Riley's hands. "Go on. Once I give her the drug, I want you to take a video of her.

I am going to record everything she will do with those men." Riley stared at the phone in her hands like it was a live grenade. "No." She shook her head. "Mom, this is not right. We cannot do this." "Really?" Elizabeth's voice dropped, becoming silky and dangerous. "Celeste already knows my secret. She knows that Fisher is not really your father. If we let her go now, she will go to him. She will tell him the truth. And he will disinherit you and Julian Is that what you want?" Riley shifted her weight from one foot to the other. She looked at me, then at her mother, then back at the phone.

"If we get this video and put it out there," Elizabeth continued, pressing her advantage, "even if she goes to him and tries to tell him anything, he will not listen to her. He will think she is just a whore trying to come between his family. And even Julian would be too disgusted to have anything to do with her. This is how we get rid of Celeste for good." +15 Bonus Riley let out a long breath. Her shoulders sagged. "Okay, fine," she said, her voice hollow. "Let us do it quickly and leave. I do not feel comfortable here." She raised the phone, pointing the camera at me.

"Really, Riley?" I asked, and I could hear the exhaustion creeping into my voice. "You are a woman, just like me. You came to me earlier to talk to me, to play mediator, and now you are going to do this? You are going to allow your sick mother to turn you into this kind of person?" "Shut up, Celeste." Riley's voice cracked. "I gave you a chance. I came to speak to you, but you insulted me. I tried to convince you because I wanted Julian to be happy. But since you do not care about my brother, I will not care about you. Mom, go on.

chapters.title: Chapter 209
chapters.content:
Chapter 209 DOMINIC After I left Celeste, I climbed into the back of my car and let my driver pull us out into traffic, heading toward the office, and for the first time in longer than I could remember, I felt something close to peace settle over me. I turned out that when a man finally found the one, his heart simply knew it, no hesitation, no second-guessing, just a bone-deep certainty that made everything else in the world fall into its proper place. I wanted to spend the rest of my life with her. I wanted to protect her from anything and everything that dared come near her.

I had never felt anything like this before. Not once, not with Seraphine, not with anyone. This was the kind of happiness that settled into your bones and made itself at home, the kind that made you think about white dresses and small hands and the sound of children's laughter bouncing off walls you had built for the people you loved. I let myself imagine it. A little girl with Celeste's eyes and Celeste's smile, her hair in pigtails as she ran through the penthouse, her voice bright when she called my name.

A boy, stubborn like me and kind like her, learning to ride a bike while I stood behind him, my hands ready to catch him if he fell. The thought was so vivid my chest tightened, a grin spreading across my face before I could stop it. If only I had married Celeste first. If only I had not wasted those years with Seraphine. We might already have a family by now. Then the smile faded. I thought of the mark on Celeste's face. A handprint, unmistakable even from across the room, the kind of mark that didn't come from an accident. She had lied to me about it. Brushed it off like it was nothing.

Which meant she was protecting someone, and the only question that mattered was who. I pulled out my phone and called her bodyguards. "Where is Celeste right now?" I asked the moment the call connected. "At Helix, sir," came the reply. "She's inside working." Good. She was safe. "I need both of you at my office. Now." They arrived within the hour, and I had them shown straight into my office, gesturing for them to sit across from my desk. 1 hadn't questioned their competence before today.

They were among the best men I had, trained for exactly this kind of work, and I had never once had cause to doubt them. But the mark on Celeste's face wouldn't leave me alone, and I needed to know exactly what had happened while I hadn't been watching. "Tell me everything," I said. "Every single detail, starting from the moment. I put you on her." They walked me through it, methodical and thorough, and for the first few minutes I found myself almost smiling, genuinely impressed by how closely they'd tracked her movements, how quickly they'd responded to every shift in her schedule.

Then they reached the part about the man who had slapped her, and something in my chest went cold and then immediately hot, rage rising so fast I had to press my palms flat against the desk to keep from standing. "She told us to stand down," one of them said. "Said the man was her brother. We backed off because she gave the order directly. "And there was a woman with him," the other added. "She stayed off to the side the whole time. Looked pleased when he went after her." Pleased.

I turned that word over in my mind, already narrowing down the list of people cruel enough, desperate enough, to stand back and enjoy watching Celeste get hurt. There was only one name that fit. I pulled up a photograph on my phone and turned the screen toward them. "This woman?" Both men nodded without hesitation. I set the phone down slowly, my jaw tight enough to ache. Every instinct in me wanted to drive straight to wherever Celeste's +15 Bonus brother was and make him regret the day he learned how to raise his hand against a woman. But Celeste had stopped my men from touching him.

She had hidden the truth from me entirely, which meant, whatever her reasons, she was still protecting him. If I went after her brother now, she might see it as me overriding her, undermining a decision she'd made for reasons of her own, and the last thing wanted was for her to be upset with me. So I set that anger aside, for now, and made a different call instead. I had someone pull together a full report on everything Seraphine had been doing over the past several days.

It took twenty minutes to land in my inbox, and by the time I finished reading it, the rage I'd set aside had come roaring back twice as strong. She had used Celeste's own brother as a weapon against her. Manipulated him, turned him against his sister, all so she could watch someone else do her dirty work for her. She had made her choice. She'd had every opportunity to quietly let this go, and instead she'd chosen to escalate. 1 reached for my phone to make the call when one of the bodyguards suddenly straightened in his chair. "Sir," he said, already pulling up something on his own phone.

chapters.title: Chapter 210
chapters.content:
Chapter 210 "Seraphine has become a problem," I told him. "What do you need me to do?" Sparrow asked, his voice already shifting into the flat, businesslike register he used when he was about to enjoy his work. "I want her so busy she doesn't have a spare second to remember Celeste's name." "Anything specific in mind," he asked, "or should I use my discretion?" I thought about it for a moment. Chapter 219 CELESTE My hand was on the car door handle, the cool metal pressing into my palin, when the thought hit me like a slap across the face. Dominic was in danger and here I was, about to drive away alone. I turned around and ran back into the house, my heels slapping against the concrete, my breath coming in short sharp bursts. The sounds of moaning and flesh slapping against flesh were still drifting through the house as I made my way to the sex room, calling out for the bodyguards as loudly as I could manage. "Come out, both of you! Right now!

We need to leave!" The bodyguards emerged from the room, their expressions shifting from professional composure to alett concern when they saw the look on my face. One of them was still holding his phone, the video still recording, and I pointed at it. "Turn that off and keep the footage. We need to go. Dominic is in danger." "What kind of danger, ma'am?" "I do not know exactly but he asked me for help. That is all I need to know. We have to get to his house right now." They did not ask any more questions.

They moved past me, their footsteps heavy and urgent, and I followed them out of the house. There were four cars parked outside. The bodyguards got into one of them and I got into my own car, pressing the ignition, the engine roaring to life. I drove like I had never driven before. The streets blurred past me, buildings and trees and traffic lights merging into a smear of color as I pushed the accelerator harder, weaving between cars, ignoring the honks and the angry gestures from other drivers.

My heart was pounding so hard I could feel it in my throat, in my temples, in the tips of my fingers where they gripped the steering wheel. Dominic did not sound okay. For him to call me and say those words, for him to actually ask for help from me, meant his situation was far beyond anything I could imagine. The drive took ten minutes that felt like ten hours. When I pulled up to Dominic's house, my stomach dropped. There were about a dozen men standing at the entrance, all of them dressed in black suits, their postures rigid, their faces blank.

They were blocking the door like human barricades, their mission clear. No one was getting inside. I parked my car haphazardly on the curb and jumped out, my hand already reaching into my bag for my stun gun. The bodyguards pulled up behind me, their doors opening in unison, and they flanked me as I marched toward the house. The men at the door saw us approaching and a ripple of laughter passed through their ranks. One of them, a large man with a thick neck and a shaved head, stepped forward, his arms crossed over his chest.

"And where do you think you are going, little lady?" "I am going into that house. You are going to step aside." He laughed, a deep rumbling sound that came from his belly. "Is that so? And what are you going to do it I do not?" I did not answer with words. I charged at him, my stun gun raised, and he was still laughing when the prongs connected with his chest and fifty thousand volts sent him crashing to the ground. The laughter died instantly. The other men turned toward me, their faces hardening, but before they could make a move, my bodyguards were already on them.

The fight was brutal and efficient. My bodyguards moved like machines, their fists and feet finding their targets with surgical precision. I used the stun gun on two more men who tried to break away from the fight, sending them twitching to the ground, and then I turned my attention to the door. The door was locked but luckily, Dominic had set my fingerprint into the lock days ago. I pressed my thumb against the scanner and the mechanism clicked open. I pushed through the door and stepped inside.

Chapter 225 PAT I sat at my desk long after everyone else had gone home, staring at a spreadsheet I had not actually read in twenty minutes, my mind stuck on the same question circling over and over like water going down a drain. Why had Kingsley left like that? He had seemed happy here, genuinely happy, the way people are when they have found something they did not expect to find. He had not even collected his final paycheck, and people who quit jobs in a hurry usually still want the money owed to them. He had not.

I picked up the resignation letter from where I had set it down, his signature at the bottom in that neat, deliberate handwriting I had memorized over the past few days, and I read his name like it might give me answers if I stared at it long enough. Was it me? Was it because we had slept together? Had there been someone else in his life this whole time, some girlfriend or fiancée I knew nothing about, and the guilt had caught up to him and chased hip out the door? But that did not sit right either, because if there was guilt to assign, it was not mine to carry.

He was the one who had called me. He was the one who had asked for my help. He had been inside me, his mouth on my skin, his fingers in my hair, his cock buried so deep I had felt him in my throat, and I had not asked him for a single promise afterward. I had not asked him to take responsibility for me, had not asked for a ring or a title or a conversation about where this was going. I was a grown woman. I knew how to have a moment without turning it into a referendum on my worth.

Still, if I was honest with myself, some small stubborn part of me had hoped it might turn into something more, and that hope was exactly what made his silence sting. I thought back further, trying to find the thread I was missing, and landed on something he had said right before he disappeared. Watch your back. Seraphine is out to get you. I had not thought much of it at the time. Now it sat in my chest like a stone. How would Kingsley know anything about Seraphine, let alone know her well enough to warn me about her specifically? Was that why he had left?

Did his disappearance have something to do with her? My phone buzzed against the desk. Seraphine's name lit up the screen. Speak of the devil, I thought, and I let it ring out. If Celeste had still been in the office, I would have shown her the screen, laughed about it, made some joke about summoning demons just by thinking about them. But Celeste had left to visit Dominic hours ago, and Kingsley's warning was still rattling around my skull, so instead of answering, I set the phone face down and went back to pretending to work. A minute later it buzzed again. A text this time.

I picked it up and read it, and the bottom dropped out of my stomach. Meet me in the Helix parking lot in ten minutes, or everyone on the internet, gets to find out exactly how cheaply you opened your legs for Kingsley Duke. It was seven at night. The lab had closed hours ago. I should have already been curled up on my couch with a glass of wine and a book, trying to forget the way his hands had felt on my waist. But I had stayed. I had stayed because I could not stop thinking about him, about the way he had left. And now Seraphine was waiting in the parking lot, talking about him?
