I would lose everything." "That is not my problem. Figure it out. And your second task is this.

I want video and audio of Celeste admitting, out loud, in her own words, that she slept with Dominic Ford while she was still married to Julian, and that the only reason he invested five billion dollars into Helix is because of her relationship with him." "How would I even get her to say something like that? It's not possible." Seraphine shrugged, the picture of indifference. "That is your problem to solve, not mine. You have until one p.m. tomorrow. It by then the news of Helix burning down does not reach me, and if I do not have that confession in hand, your sex video goes viral.

Every platform. Every site. Your mother. Your colleagues. Everyone will see just how cheaply you open your legs." She turned and walked back to her car without looking back at me, her heels clicking against the asphalt, her red dress swaying with each step. She opened the door, slid inside, and started the engine without a single glance at the woman she had lett kneeling on the ground. I stayed there long after her taillights disappeared around the corner. The gravel dug into my knees. The night air chilled my burning cheeks. And I cried.

I cried until my throat was raw and my eyes were empty, until there were no tears lett, until I was just a hollow shell sitting in an empty parking lot with nothing but the taste of betrayal in my mouth. Kingsley. The man I had given my virginity to. He had been her pawn the entire time. Every touch, every kiss, every moment of tenderness had been a performance for a hidden camera somewhere I had not known to look. He had recorded me. He had captured the sounds I made, the way my body responded to him, the trust I had placed in his hands.

chapters.title: Chapter 228
chapters.content:
Chapter 228 I cursed him in my mind, a litany of hatred that burned through the grief. I cursed myself too, for my naivety, for my stupidity, for believing that a man like Kingsley Duke could ever want someone like me. I was thirty years old. I had waited my entire life for something special. And I had given it to a camera hidden behind a curtain. I do not remember taking myself home that night. I do not remember climbing the stairs to my apartment or unlocking the door or collapsing onto my bed.

I do not remember the hours I spent staring at the ceiling, my face wet with tears, my mind replaying every moment of that hotel room on an endless loop. But I remember the morning. I remember the pale light filtering through my curtains, the ache in my jaw where I had slapped myself, the cold resolve settling into my chest like a stone. I sat up and looked at myself in the mirror across the room. My cheeks were red, swollen, marked with the outline of my own fingers. My eyes were puffy, my hair a disaster, my skin sallow from a night of no sleep. I looked like a woman who had been broken.

But I did not feel broken. I felt something else, something harder, something that had crystallized in the dark hours of the night while the world slept. And I was not going to let Seraphine win. I took a shower and let the hot water beat against my bruised face until I could feel the blood moving beneath my skin again. I put on clean clothes. I applied concealer to my cheeks until the red was barely visible, until I looked like myself again, like a woman who had not spent the night crying. When I arrived at Helix that morning, I pretended like everything was fine.

Celeste didn't realize anything. She had no idea what I was carrying. And she had no idea that Seraphine had spent the night plotting her destruction. And I could not tell her. Not yet. Not until I had done what I needed to do. I went through the motions of the morning like a robot. I smiled when Celeste made a joke. We talked about Dominic and I joked too. I nodded when she talked about the new equipment she wanted to order. And all the while, I was watching, waiting, planning. When Celeste excused herself to use the restroom, she left her phone on the desk.

I watched her walk away, her footsteps fading down the corridor, and I counted to ten before I moved. My hand was steady as I picked up her phone. I knew her password. I had known it for years, back from when she used to hand me her phone across the lab to answer calls while her hands were busy with samples. The screen unlocked smoothly, and I navigated to her video folder, my heart pounding so loud I was sure someone would hear it. The videos were there. Seraphine's videos. The ones Celeste had shown everyone at the lab that day, the ones that had changed everything.

I found them, selected them, and copied every one of them onto my own phone. Then I erased my tracks carefully, deleting the transfer log, making sure nothing was out of place. And then I set Celeste's phone back on her desk exactly where she had left it. Later, I walked to my office and closed the door. My hands were shaking as I sat down at my computer, but I forced them to still.

chapters.title: Chapter 229
chapters.content:
Chapter 229 The moment it went live, something in my chest loosened for the first time since the parking lot. I watched the notifications roll in, first a trickle then a flood shares and comments and retweets spreading across platforms faster than I could track. The view count climbed: a thousand, ten thousand, fifty thousand, a hundred thousand. The comments were brutal, people calling her every name in the book, dissecting her body and her technique and her morals, making memes and jokes, crucifying her in the court of public opinion.

And I watched it all from behind my anonymous screen, my face expressionless, my hands steady. This was war, and I had just fired the first shot. I would never burn Helix down. I would never betray Celeste, not for Seraphine, not for anyone. But Seraphine had set me up and now wanted to release a sex video of me. Fine. Let her. It would not carry the same weight as hers, because whatever else people wanted to say about me, I had not slept with a married man. I certainly had not slept with my own best friend's husband.

If Seraphine wanted to drag me through the mud, she was going to be lying right there in it beside me. One o'clock came and went. I sat at my desk, my phone face-up beside me, waiting for the notification that would change everything, the notification that Seraphine had fulfilled her promise and my video was out in the world for everyone to see. But it did not come. I refreshed my email. Nothing. I checked every social media platform, searched for my name, searched for Kingsley's name, searched for any mention of a video involving us. Nothing. The hours crawled by. Two o'clock. Three o'clock.

Four o'clock. I paced my office. I drank water I did not taste. I stared at the ceiling and tried to breathe. What was she waiting for? Why had she not released the video? Was she saving it for a more dramatic moment? Was she planning something bigger? By evening, I had convinced myself she was toying with me, that she wanted me to suffer, to spend every moment waiting for the axe to fall, jumping at every notification, terrified of what was coming. And it was working. I was a wreck, barely holding myself together, my mind spinning through every possible scenario. Then, my phone rang.

chapters.title: Chapter 230
chapters.content:
Chapter 230 CELESTE I paced the length of Dominic's hospital room, my thumb hovering over Pat's contact, the call already disconnected, the silence on her end still ringing in my ears. She had not said a single word after my question. Just breathing, wet and uneven, and then a sound I rarely heard from her, a sob that seemed to claw its way out of her throat like it hurt to come up. And then nothing. I had stood there listening to dead air for ten seconds before I realized she was not going to answer me. "I do not understand," I said, more to myself than to Dominic.

"She released Seraphine's videos, and now she is crying on the phone like a baby." Dominic shifted in the hospital bed, the IV line tugging against his arm. "Maybe you should call her back." "I don't think she is in the right mood to speak over the phone." "Then maybe you should go to her." I stopped pacing and looked at him. He was sitting up now, the color slowly returning to his face, his eyes clearer than they had been a while ago when I found him delirious and burning with fever. "I cannot leave you here alone," I said. "Not after what happened. Your grandmother is out there.

Imelda is out there. For all I know, there is another photographer hiding in the janitor's closet." He chuckled. "I can take care of myself, Celeste." "You could not take care of yourself a while ago. You were hallucinating and asking me to sit on your face in the back of a moving car." A grin spread across his face, slow and crooked. "That part I remember clearly and I stand by every word of it." I tried to glare at him but the laugh escaped before I could stop it a sharp burst of sound that cut through the tension in my chest. "You are impossible." "I am serious. Go to Pat. She needs you.

I will be discharged in a few hours and I will come pick you up myself." "The doctors said you need at least a day of rest." "The doctors also said I should avoid stressful situations and I am about to hear my grandmother's voice on the phone any minute now. That ship has sailed." He reached for my hand and I let him take it, his fingers warm and steady against mine. "Go. I will be fine." I squeezed his hand once and let go. "Call me if anything happens. Anything at all." "I will.

But first I need to know something." "What?" He leaned back against the pillow, studying me with those sharp eyes that missed nothing. "How did you know it was Pat?" I sat down on the edge of the bed, the mattress dipping under my weight. "When I left your house this morning and went backo Helix, I noticed she was acting differently. She tried to hide it. She smiled at me the way she always smiles, asked me about my night, made the usual small talk about lab schedules and supply orders. But her eyes were wrong.

They were putty She had been crying and she had done a terrible job of covering it up." "Maybe she was just tired." "She did not call me last night, Dominic. Not once. And Pat knows I was not planning to spend the night with you. She knew I was just going to come see you and go back. For her to go an entire night without calling me, without sending a single text to ask if I was okay, that is not like her at all. Something had to have kept her occupied and I doubted it was good news." He nodded slowly.

chapters.title: Chapter 231
chapters.content:
Chapter 231 Dominic's eyebrows rose. "Staring at your phone?" "Every time I set it down, I caught her looking at it. Not glancing. Not checking the tinte Looking. Like she was trying to figure out the combination to a safe. I did not know what she wanted with it but I decided to give her the opportunity to take whatever she needed." "You deliberately left your phone with her." "I pretended to go to the restroom. I left it on her table, face up, unlocked. And I watched secretly as she picked it up and started scrolling through it." "That is a gamble," he said.

"She could have been checking your messages." "Pat would never do that. I knew whatever she was looking for, she had a reason for it. I just did not know the reason was Seraphine's videos." "And you did not confront her about it?" "I was going to. I planned to ask her about it when I came back to Helix after visiting my mother. I never suspected she would take the videos. Pat has always been disgusted by Seraphine's actions. She thought Seraphine was vile for sleeping with Julian.

I did not think she would touch those videos, let alone release them to the entire internet." I stood up, smoothing down my dress. I leaned down and kissed him, my lips brushing against his forehead, his cheek, the corner of his mouth. He caught my chin with his fingers and pulled me into a proper kiss, soft and slow, his tongue tracing the seam of my lips before he let me go. "Be careful," he said. I nodded, grabbed my bag and walked out of the hospital room, my mind already racing ahead to Helix, to Pat, to the conversation I knew I needed to have.

I spent every second of the drive running through scenarios in my head, trying to figure out what could have pushed Pat to this point, what Seraphine could have said or done to turn the gentlest person I knew into a weapon aimed at someone else. Helix was still humming with activity when I arrived, and the moment I stepped through the glass doors, I felt the shift in the air. Conversations stopped mid-sentence. Eyes tracked my movements. People whispered behind their hands and looked away when I caught them staring. I ignored all of it and headed straight for Pat's office.

The door was closed. I knocked once, twice, and when there was no answer, I pushed it open anyway. Pat was sitting at her desk, her face buried in her hands, her shoulders shaking with silent sobs. The computer screen in front of her was dark. A crumpled tissue lay on the floor beside her chair. Her hair, usually pinned back in a neat bun, had come loose in places, strands of it sticking to her damp cheeks. "Pat." She looked up and the sight of her face hit me like a punch to the chest. Her eyes were swollen, red rimmed, the skin around them raw from crying. Her nose was running.

Her lips were chapped and bitten. She looked like she had been drowning for hours and had only now broken the surface. "Celeste, I am so sorry." Her voice came out in a croak, barely recognizable. "I did not mean to do it. I did not mean to take your phone. I did not mean to..." I crossed the room in four steps and pulled her into my arms. She stiffened for a moment, her body rigid, and then she collapsed against me, her fingers gripping the back of my dress, her +15 Bonus face pressing into my shoulder, and she cried. Not the polite quiet crying of someone trying to hold it together.

chapters.title: Chapter 232
chapters.content:
Chapter 232 "Start from the beginning, said. "Tell me everything." She took a shaky breath and therrit all came out. Seraphine's text. The parking lot. The demand to meet. Kingsley's betrayal. The video of her that Seraphine had. The blackmail. The slaps she had to give herself, ten of them, kneeling on the concrete while Seraphine watched. By the time she finished, my jaw was clenched so tight could feel the ache spreading into my temples. "She threatened to release a sex video of you and Kingsley?" Pat nodded, fresh tears spilling down her cheeks. "She said she had it.

She said Kingsley recorded it for her. She said he was working for her the whole time and that is why he resigned, because his job was done." "And you believed her?" "She knew details about us, Celeste. Things no one else knew. The hotel we went to. The time.... How would she know all of that if Kingsley had not told her?" I leaned back against the couch, my mind turning the problem over like a Rubik's cube. "Did you actually see the video? Did she show it to you?" Pat's mouth opened and closed. "No. She did not.

But, she wouldn't lie about something like that." "Seraphine came to my house and slept with my husband while we were still best friends. Do you think lying about a video would cost her a single night of sleep?" "She would not lie about something like that." "She would lie about anything if it got her what she wanted. You said it yourself. She has always resented the fact that you were close to me. What if she does not have a video at all? What if she was just using the threat of one to control you?" Pat shook her head, her hands trembling in her lap. "But Kingsley warned me about her.

He said, 'Watch your back. Seraphine is out to get you.' And then he disappeared. Why would he warn me if he was not working for her? Why would he tell me to watch my back if he was not in her circle?" I stared at her, the question hanging in the air between us. "What if Kingsley was not working for Seraphine? What if he found out she was planning something and tried to warn you before she got to him?" "Then why did he resign? Why did he leave without saying goodbye?" "I do not know. But I am going to find out." Pat looked at me, her eyes wide and desperate.

"How?" I stood up, pulling my phone out of my bag. "I have a contact. Someone who helped me dig up information before about Julian's mother. If there is anything to find about Kingsley Duke, he will find it." "You do not have to do this for me. Not after what I did." I stopped at the door and turned back to look at her. "Pat, you released Seraphine's videos. You did it to protect yourself That does not make you a bad person. It makes you a scared one.

And I am not going to abandon you because you were scared." She started crying again, but this time there was something different in the sound, a loosening, a release. "Stay here," I said. "I will be back." I walked out of her office and through the corridors of Helix, past the whispering employees and the curious stares, past the lab technicians who pretended to be busy when I caught their eyes. I knew what they were thinking. I knew they believed I had released the videos myself, that I had finally snapped and decided to burn Seraphine's reputation to the ground.

Let them think +15 Bonus it If it came down to protecting Pat from legal trouble, I would stand up in front of a judge and say I did it myself. Outside the building, I putted out my phone and scrolled through my contacts until I found the name I was looking for. A man I had not spoken to in months, a hacker with a taste for expensive whiskey and a moral code that bent depending on who was paying. He had helped me dig up Elizabeth's background when I first started suspecting Julian's mother was not so simple. He had delivered everything I needed within twenty-four hours.

chapters.title: Chapter 233
chapters.content:
Chapter 233 I called. He picked up on the third ring. "I need your help," I said. "Celeste Fisher. It has been a while. I heard you have been busy. Something about a billionaire and a very public divorce." "I need information on someone. Fast." "I am listening." I sent him Kingsley's full name, a copy of his passport photograph, and the last known address I had on file. "I want to know everything.

Where he grew up, who his parents are, what he has been doing for the past six months, and why he resigned from his job at Helix without collecting his final paycheck." "You think he is in trouble?" "I think someone is using him to get to me. And I want to know why." The line went quiet for a moment. Then: "Give me thirty minutes." "Thirty minutes?" "I like you, Celeste. You pay on time and you do not ask stupid questions. You get the express rate." "Send me the bill." I hung up and stood there in the parking lot, the air cool against my skin, my phone warm in my hand. Thirty minutes.

I could wait thirty minutes. I walked to a small bench near the entrance of the parking lot and sat down, my eyes fixed on the sky, my mind drifting through the events of today. The kidnapping. The rescue. Dominic in that hospital bed. Pat on her knees in a parking lot, slapping her own face while Seraphine watched. Thirty minutes passed. Then forty. Then my phone buzzed with a notification. A file. Large. Packed with information. I opened it and started reading. The first thing I learned was that Kingsley Duke had not always been broke.

His father, Arthur Duke, had been a billionaire, the kind of man who owned hotels and shopping malls and half a dozen companies that operated across three continents. He had been married to Kingsley's mother, Evelyn, for thirty years. They had been happy, by all accounts. Wealthy, respected, with a son who worshipped the ground his father walked on. And then Arthur Duke made the mistake that cost him everything. He took a mistress. I scrolled further, my eyes moving faster as the details piled on.

The mistress had been beautiful, ambitious, and patient She had spent two years working her way into Arthur's life, into his confidence, into his bed, and when she had gathered enough information, she had betrayed him. With the help of Arthur's own brother, Kingsley's uncle, she had siphoned the family's wealth, emptied the accounts, and transferred all the properties. Arthur Duke had a cardiac arrest three days after discovering he was broke. He died on the operating table. Evelyn Duke, Kingsley's mother, had been admitted to the hospital soon after.

The stress, the grief, the collapse of everything she had built her life around. She had been there for years now, critically ill, her body failing piece by piece, kept alive by machines and the prayers of a son who could not afford either. +15 Bonus the file included a medical report. The diagnosis was severe cardiomyopathy, a heart condition that had deteriorated to the point where only a transplant could save her. The surgery would cost two million dollars. Kingsley did not have two million dollars. He did not have two thousand dollars.

He was surviving on odd jobs and handouts, sleeping in his car some nights, skipping meals so he could afford his mother's medication. I set the phone down in my lap and stared at the sky again. Had Kingsley worked for Seraphine because he was desperate? Because his mother was dying, because he would have done anything, anything at all, to save the only family he had left? But the file also showed something else. Something that made my chest tighten with a complicated feeling I could not name. No money had been deposited for Evelyn's surgery.

Ruby's writing style is bold and irresistible-perfect for those who crave intense, addictive love stories.

chapters.title: Chapter 234
chapters.content:
Chapter 234 I could walk away. I could go back inside, tell Pat that Kingsley was a desperate man who had made a terrible choice, and let the chips fall where they may. None of this was my responsibility. I had my own problems, my own war with Seraphine, my own marriage to untangle. But I thought about Evelyn Duke, lying in a hospital bed, her heart failing, her son begging for a miracle that was not coming. I thought about what it felt like to watch someone you loved slip away while you stood there helpless. I stood up, got into my car, and drove to the hospital address listed in the file.

I walked through the front doors and asked for Evelyn Duke's room. The nurse at the counter gave me a curious look but pointed me down the hall. Evelyn was in a small room at the end of the corridor, a private room that must have cost Kingsley every spare penny he had. She was asleep when I walked in, her face slack, her skin pale and waxy, her body lost in the hospital gown that hung loose on her diminished frame. Tubes and wires connected her to machines that beeped and hummed in the quiet of the room.

Her hair, once probably a rich dark brown like her son's, had gone thin and gray, pulled back from a face that looked older than her years. I stood at the foot of her bed and watched her breathe. She did not know I was there. She did not know that her son had almost destroyed himself trying to save her. I pulled out my phone and called the hospital's billing department. "My name is Celeste Fisher," I said, keeping my voice low. "I want to pay for Evelyn Duke's surgery. In full." There was a pause on the other end.

"Ma'am, the cost of the procedure is two million dollars." "I am aware." "Plus post-operative care and rehabilitation. That brings the total to approximately two point three million." "Send me the invoice. I will have the funds transferred within the hour." Another pause, longer this time. "Ma'am, are you a relative of the patient?" "No. But she needs the surgery and I can pay for it. That is all you need to know." I hung up before she could ask any more questions. A few minutes later, I made the payment.

I walked out of Evelyn's room and through the hospital corridors, past the nurses and the patients and the vending machines that hummed in the corners. I made it to the front entrance, pushed open the glass doors, and stepped out into the evening air. My phone buzzed. Pat. I was about to answer when I heard footsteps behind me, fast and heavy, someone running. I turned. Kingsley was there, his chest heaving, his face shining with sweat, his eyes wild and desperate. He looked like he had been running for miles, his shirt untucked, his hair disheveled, his hands shaking at his sides.

Ruby's writing style is bold and irresistible-perfect for those who crave intense, addictive love stories.

chapters.title: Chapter 235
chapters.content:
Chapter 235 CELESTE I stood there watching Kingsley Duke kneel on the concrete like a man who had finally reached the end of a very long rope, and I felt something twist in my chest that I did not have a name for. "I do not need you on your knees," I said, my voice coming out flatter than I intended. "Get up." He did not move. His hands were pressed flat against the ground, his shoulders still shaking. "I have been searching for a way to save her for months. I have begged. I have borrowed. I have done things I am not proud of.

And then you walk in, and you fix everything in the time it takes to make a phone call. I do not understand." "I said get up." He pushed himself to his feet slowly, his legs unsteady, his eyes still wet. He was taller than I remembered, broader, but right now he looked small, folded in on himself like a man who had forgotten how to stand straight. "I just arrived at the hospital," he said, wiping his face with the back of his hand. "I was coming to check on my mother when the nurse stopped me and said someone had just paid the full amount for her surgery.

She showed me the name on the receipt. Celeste Fisher. I ran after you immediately. I did not even know what I was going to say. I just knew I had to catch you before you disappeared." "I did not do it for you," I said, and I watched his face tighten as though the words had struck him physically. "I did it for your mother. She is lying in that bed because her husband could not keep his dick in his pants and his mistress decided to ruin his entire family. She did not deserve to die for a sin she did not commit.

That is the only reason." He nodded slowly, his jaw working, his hands clenching and unclenching at his sides. "Still. You did not have to do it. You could have walked away. You could have let me drown. I would have deserved it. After everything I did to Pat, I would have deserved to watch my mother die alone in that hospital bed." "So, you gave Pat's sex video to Seraphine, right?" I asked, my voice coming out harder than I intended. He shook his head, his eyes widening, his voice cracking on the single syllable. "No.

My conscience could never allow me to do something so horrible." I studied his face, looking for the tell, the flicker of dishonesty that would confirm what Pat had said. But all I saw was the truth. "Then what happened? Explain it to me. From the beginning." He took a shaky breath, his hands trembling at his sides, his eyes fixed on the ground as though he could not bring himself to look at me while he spoke. "I was desperate for a job. Any job. My father's name used to open doors. After he died, and the news broke that we had lost everything, those same doors slammed shut in my face.

I was sleeping in my car, skipping meals so l could afford my mother's medication. I had nothing left." "So what happened?" "Someone told me Seraphine Ford was a philanthropist, that she helped people in difficult situations. I went to her office and asked for a job. I told her about my mother, about the surgery, about everything. She listened to me with this expression on her face, this calm, patient expression that made me think she actually cared." He let out a bitter laugh. "And then she said no. Flat out. No openings.

She could not help everyone who walked through her doors with a sob story. Later, she reached out and told me she could get me a position at Helix instead. I thought she was doing me a genuine kindness. Eventually, I found out what her ultimate goal was. "What did she want?" "She told me to sleep with Pat, record it, and bring the footage to her. If I refused, she said she'd walk straight into Helix and expose me as her spy in front of everyone." +15 Bonus "And you did what she wanted." "I did it, and I hate myself for it.

"He opened his eyes and looked at me, his gaze steady despite the tears still clinging to his lashes. "And then I deleted it I deleted the file and all its backups, and told Seraphine to go to hell. Afterward, I went to Pat and told her to watch her back. I could not explain what I had done. But I could warn her. So I did. And then I resigned. I've spent the whole of today knocking on doors, sending applications, begging for a chance. Friends I have known my entire life have turned their backs on me. People I helped when they were down have pretended they do not remember my name.

I have been rejected from positions I am overqualified for, jobs that pay less than minimum wage, positions that require no experience at all." "I want to ask you something," I said after staring at him for a while. "Anything." "If I gave you the chance to get everything back, everything your father lost, everything your uncle stole froin your family, would you take it?" He stared at me, his mouth slightly open, his eyes searching mine for the punchline that did not come. "What did you just say?" "I know someone. Someone who can help you recover what was taken from your family.

chapters.title: Chapter 236
chapters.content:
Chapter 236 "You are serious." "I do not say things I do not mean +15 Bonus He took a step toward me, his voice dropping to something barely above a whisper. "Why are you doing this? I lied. I manipulated someone you care about. I recorded her without her knowledge or consent. I am the villain in this story. Why would you help the villain?" "Consider it payment," I said, "for not giving Seraphine Pat's video." He shook his head, his jaw tightening. "I cannot accept that. I cannot take payment for doing the right thing. I broke Pat's trust.

I am the one who needs to make amends, not you." "Fine. Consider it a loan. When you get your fortune back, you can pay me the full amount plus interest. And you will make things right with Pat so she can get the closure she deserves and move on with her life." He was quiet for a long moment, his eyes fixed on the ground, his breathing slow and measured. When he looked up, there was something new in his expression, something that looked almost like hope. "Deal." "Good. Do not make me regret this." "You will not.

I swear to you, you will not regret this." I pulled out my phone, dialed Dominic's number, and pressed the phone to my ear, watching Kingsley watch me with an expression I could not read. I pulled out my phone and called Dominic. "Hey," he answered, and I could hear the smile in his voice even through exhaustion. "Everything okay?" "Everything's fine. I need a favor, actually. I want to set up a meeting with Sparrow." "Sparrow? What for?" "Nothing you need to worry about. You're the one who told me what he's capable of in the first place.

I just need to make use of it now." "All right." I heard him shift, papers rustling somewhere in the background. "Let me make a call. Give me a few minutes and I'll send you the location. He'll be expecting you." "Thank you." "I'm about to be discharged, so I'll head home and we can talk properly when you're done." There was a pause. "Be careful, Celeste." "Always." I turned to Kingsley, who was watching me with a mixture of curiosity and apprehension. "Who is Sparrow?" "Someone who is going to help you get your life back." Twenty minutes later, I had an address, and I drove Kingsley.

The bar was tucked away in a part of the city I had never visited, a narrow storefront with no sign and a door that looked like it had been kicked in more than once. I pulled up to the curb and killed the engine. I got out of the car. Kingsley followed. We walked to the door and I pushed it open without knocking. +15 Bonus The inside was nothing like what I expected. The walls were lined with dark wood, the kind that had been polished by decades of use. A long bar stretched across the back wall, stocked with bottles I recognized and bottles I did not.

The lighting was low, amber and warm, and the air smelled of whiskey and leather and something faintly floral I could not place. Sparrow was sitting at a table in the corner, a glass of something dark in his hand, his legs crossed, his expression unreadable. He rose the moment he saw me, greeting me with a level of respect that told me exactly how highly Dominic had spoken of me to him. "Celeste." His voice was low, smooth, the kind of voice that belonged in a recording booth or a confession booth. a He gestured to the chairs across from him and I sat down.

"You will answer my questions first, Scarlett. Tell me who sent you, and what you want, and I might let you live." I let out a shaky breath, letting my shoulders slump in defeat. +15 Bonus "His name is Julian Fisher," I said, letting fresh tears spill down my cheeks. "He captured me and my friends. We fell into his trap and now we owe him a hundred million dollars.

Not having the money to pay him, he locked us all up and said if I slept with Dominic Ford and recorded it, he would clear all our debt and let us go." I paused, letting my voice crack. "My sister Tasha is one of the girls in his custody. I had no choice but to do what Julian wanted. I had to do it to protect her." He was quiet for a long moment, studying my face, and I let him look because I knew my expression was perfect, my tears real enough to pass any test. "I see," he said finally, and he put the gun away entirely.

I had to fight to keep my face arranged into fear and gratitude instead of the laugh threatening to climb up my throat. Julian genuinely believed he was the one running this. The architect. The mastermind pulling strings from the shadows. In reality he was nothing more than an instrument, dancing exactly to the tune I'd composed. I had targeted him because I knew Julian was having sex with Dominic Ford's wife and Dominic Ford was having sex with Julian's wife in return, a beautiful symmetry of betrayal.

I had believed Julian would eventually make it easy for me to get close to Dominic Ford, and once I was close to Dominic Ford, having an audience with Sparrow would be possible. Tonight I had walked in expecting Dominic Ford. If it had been him waiting in that booth, I would have played an entirely different hand. But it was Sparrow instead. And the instant I'd looked into his face and recognized him, I'd understood that every plan, every calculated move, every sacrifice, had delivered me exactly where I needed to be.

And with a man like Sparrow, I already knew the fastest route to an audience was the oldest one there is. Sparrow, by every reputation I'd gathered, wasn't a man who went a single day without a woman in his bed, and beautiful women always sat at the very top of his preferences. Fortunately for me, I had enough beauty to spare for twenty women and still have some left over. And honestly, sharing Sparrow's bed had been no loss at all. Quite the opposite.

I watched him process everything I'd told him, even knowing, with total certainty, that he'd likely known most of it before I ever walked into that booth. Still, I let myself collapse to the floor, sinking onto my knees, fresh tears sliding down my cheeks. "Whoever you are," I said, "please. Save my sister. Save my friends. Get us away from that monster. In return, I will do anything you ask." His lips curved into something almost gentle. "My name is Sparrow." Hearing him finally offer it to me himself, plainly, without games, I let out a breath of genuine relief. This was really happening.

chapters.title: Chapter 246
chapters.content:
Chapter 246 SERAPHINE Let me tell you something about standing in a parking lot after watching your last shred of leverage get destroyed, it makes you want to break something expensive. Kingsley had destroyed the only copy of Pat's sex video, the one piece of ammunition I had that could actually hurt Celeste, and destroy Pat. He had crushed it in front of me like it was nothing more than a crumpled piece of paper.

I stood there with my hands balled into fists, my nails biting into my palms, the evening aír doing nothing to cool the rage simmering under my skin, and I thought about all the ways I was going to make Kingsley regret the day he decided to cross me His time would come. Everyone who had wronged me would get what was coming to them. I just had to be patient. I just had to be smarter.

I was still standing there, frozen in place by my own fury, when I spotted Felix weaving between the parked cars with that look on his face, the one that said he had been searching for me and was about to make it my problem. "There you are!" he called out as he jogged over, slightly out of breath. "Where did you go? I finished with Celeste, came back to the car, and you were gone. I've been looking everywhere." "I needed some air," I said. "Just went for a little walk. I'm tired, Felix. I feel exhausted.

I want to go home and sleep." "Okay, let me take you home." I wanted to tell him I would rather walk across broken glass than spend another minute in his company, but I had learned long ago that men like Felix responded best to weakness. They wanted to be needed. They wanted to be heroes. So I let him lead me to his car, let him open the passenger door for me, let him drive me through the city streets while I stared out the window and counted down the minutes until I could be alone. When we pulled up to my house, I turned to him and said, "Thank you for everything, Felix. Really.

You have been so kind to me. I think I can manage from here." "You don't look so good, Seraphine." "I'm fine. Just tired. A good night's sleep will fix everything." "I don't think I should leave you alone like this." "Felix, really, I will be okay." "I'm not leaving you alone. Not in this state. What if something happens? What if you need someone? I'll stay Just for a little while. Until you feel better." I looked at him, this fool who thought he was protecting me, and I considered my options.

I could argue with him, waste more energy I did not have, or I could let him in and deal with him the way I dealt with people who overstayed their welcome I torced a small, grateful smile onto my face and said, "Fine. But only for a little while." He followed me inside like a lost puppy, and I hated the way his presence filled my space, the way he made himselt comfortable on my couch, the way he looked at me with those eyes full of love I had not asked for.

I sat down across from him and said, "Felix, I want you to know how much I appreciate everything you have done for me You have been there for me when I needed someone the most. I do not know what I would have done without you." "Of course, Seraphine. I told you I would be here for you." "I want to show my appreciation. Let me get you something to drink." I stood up before he could respond, walked into the kitchen, opened the cabinet and pulled out a glass. I found the bottle of sleeping pills I hid in my kitchen, and emptied the entire contents into the bottom of the glass.

I poured the juice over the pills and watched them dissolve, swirling the liquid until it looked innocent, until it looked like nothing more than a kind gesture +15 Bonus from a grateful woman. I walked back into the living room and handed him the glass with both hands, a little bow of gratitude that made me want to laugh at my own performance. "Here," I said. "Drink. You must be thirsty." He smiled at me, that earnest, trusting smile that made me wonder how someone could be so stupid, and he took the glass from my hands.

chapters.title: Chapter 247
chapters.content:
Chapter 247 "I hope it helps you relax, said, and I meant it more than he would ever know. He finished the rest of the juice and set the glass down on the coffee table, leaning back against the couch with a satisfied sigh. I watched him, counting the seconds, waiting for the chemicals to do their work.

His eyelids began to droop within minutes, his head nodding forward as the drugs pulled him onder, and within ten minutes he was completely unconscious, his moutli hanging open, a soft snore rattling out of his throat I stood up and looked down at him, this obstacle I had temporarily removed from my path, and I said aloud to no one in particular, "Finally. Some freedom from this idiot." The night was still young, and I had work to do. 1 I drove back to Helix with my hands steady on the wheel and my mind running through the plan I had pieced together in the car.

Kingsley had destroyed the video, yes, but Pat did not know that. Pat had slapped me, humiliated me, treated me like I was nothing, and I was not about to let that go unanswered. I parked in the lot across from the Helix building, pulled out my phone, and called Pat. It rang and rang and went to voicemail. I called again. Same result. I smiled, put the phone away, and sent her a text message instead. I leaned against my car and waited, counting the seconds in my head, watching the entrance to the building like a hawk.

She came rushing out, her face pale, her eyes wide with panic, exactly the way I knew she would. She spotted me and hurried over, her hands shaking at her sides. Once I was done with Pat, I left. The drive home was a blur of streetlights and satisfaction. I had Pat exactly where I wanted her. She would do whatever I asked now. She would burn down Helix. She would destroy Celeste's dream with her own two hands. And when she did, I would be there to watch it all burn.

Felix was still unconscious on my couch when I walked in, still snoring, still taking up space in my living room like he had any right to be there. I looked at him and felt a wave of irritation so intense I almost kicked him. But I stopped myself. I was not done with him yet. He still had a use. I went to bed that night with a smile on my face, dreaming of fire and ashes and the look on Celeste's face when everything she loved turned to dust. Morning came slowly, the sunlight creeping through my curtains like an unwelcome guest.

I checked my phone immediately, scrolling through the news, refreshing every page, waiting for the headline that would tell me Helix Laboratories had burned to the ground overnight. But there was nothing. Pat had not done it yet. She was delaying. I told myself to be patient, that she would come through, that she was probably just waiting for the right moment. She had until noon, I decided. If Helix was not ashes by noon, I would have to apply more pressure. Felix woke up at fifteen minutes past eleven, groaning and rubbing his head like he had the mother of all hangovers.

I had been ready for this moment. I had my phone in my hand, a fake text message already prepared, and I had been sitting, waiting for him to open his eyes. "What happened?" he asked, his voice thick with sleep. "I feel like I was hit by a truck." "You fell asleep," I said, and then I let the tears come. A single tear sliding down my cheek, my lower lip trembling, my voice breaking just enough to sound genuine. "Felix, I am so scared." He sat up immediately, his fatigue forgotten, his instincts kicking in. "What is wrong?

chapters.title: Chapter 248
chapters.content:
Chapter 248 "Do not worry," he said. "Celeste is my sister. I will deal with her. I give you my word." "Please help me, Felix. She is going to destroy me." "I will handle it." He was out the door in under a minute, his footsteps echoing down the hallway as he rushed off to confront his sister on my behalf. I watched him go, and when the door clicked shut behind him, I let out a long breath and said to the empty room, "Oh my God, it is almost too easy." I went back to my phone, refreshing, waiting, counting down the minutes until noon.

fell asleep with my phone in my hand, the screen still glowing, the news still empty of the headline I wanted. The ringing pulled me out of a dream I could not remember. My phone was buzzing against my palm, the screen showing my mother's name, and I answered with a groggy, "Hello?" "What have you done?" My mother's voice was a scream, high and shrill, cutting through the fog in my head like a blade. "What have you done, Seraphine? Your video! It is everywhere! Everyone has seen it! You have been ruined!" "What are you talking about?" "Your sex video! The one with that man!

It is all over the internet! Someone has ruined you, and I know it is that good for nothing Celeste! What were you doing? Why did you not take care of it? How could you let this happen?" I ended the call without saying another word and opened my browser, my hands shaking so badly I could barely type. And there they were. My videos. The ones Celeste had. They were everywhere. Every platform, every site, every feed. People were sharing it, commenting on it, tearing me apart in the comments section. Whore. Slut. Disgrace.

The words blurred together as I scrolled, my vision swimming, my stomach churning. I knew it was Celeste. She was the only one who had access to this footage. She had used Dominic's money and influence to make sure the videos stayed at the top of every search, to make sure I could not escape it. I started making calls. Desperate calls. People I knew who worked in digital media, people who owed me favors, people who could help me bury the video before it ruined me completely. But every call ended the same way. Someone had paid to keep it trending. Someone had made sure it could not be removed.

No amount of money I could offer would undo what had already been done. I threw my phone across the room and screamed, the sound tearing out of my throat raw and primal and full of everything I had been holding in. Celeste had done this. Celeste had taken everything from me. My husband, my reputation, my future. And now she had taken the last thing I had left. My phone did not stop buzzing. Calls came in one after another. People from my lab. People I had not spoken to in years. Journalists. Strangers.

I watched the notifications pile up until I could not take it anymore and I turned the phone off, silencing the world, and I slid down the wall until I was sitting on the floor with my knees pulled up to my chest and my face buried in my arms. I do not know how long I sat there crying. Minutes. Hours. Time had lost all meaning. All I knew was the ache in my chest and the wetness on my cheeks and the overwhelming certainty that my life was over. And then I heard footsteps. I looked up, my eyes swollen, my vision blurry, and I tried to see who was there.

chapters.title: Chapter 249
chapters.content:
Chapter 249 +15 Bonus SERAPHINE I woke up with a headache that felt like someone had driven a spike through my skull. My eyes opened to an unfamiliar ceiling, high and vaulted, with a chandelier that probably cost more than my entire house. I was lying on a sofa so soft I could have sunk into it and disappeared, and the room around me was enormous, decorated in shades of cream and gold, with paintings on the walls that looked like originals! I sat up slowly, my hand going to my throbbing head, and that was when I saw him.

He was tall and broad-shouldered, dressed in a suit that fit him like it had been sewn onto his body, with dark hair slicked back and eyes that were sharp and assessing and undeniably amused. He walked into the room with the confidence of a man who owned everything he could see, including me. "You are awake," he said, his voice deep and smooth, the kind of voice that could talk you into anything. "What is going on here?" I asked. "Who are you? Why was I brought here?" "I apologize if my men handled you roughly.

That was not my instruction." I stared at him, trying to place where I had seen him before. There was something familiar about him, something nagging at the back of my mind that I could not quite grasp. He smiled, showing perfect teeth. "I am Emerson Gath. You have probably heard of me. I am the only heir of Senator Gath." My breath caught in my throat. Senator Gath. One of the most powerful men in the country. And this was his son. The heir to an empire of influence and money and connections that dwarfed even Dominic's. I swallowed and asked, "Why did you have me kidnapped?

What do you want from me?" "I want you." I stared at him, certain I had misheard. "What?" "Ever since I saw your viral video, I have not been able to get you out of my head." I could not believe what I was hearing. The entire world was calling me a whore, sharing my most intimate moments without my consent, tearing me apart piece by piece, and this man was standing here telling me he could not get me out of his head? "Listen," he said, walking closer. "I may have had you brought here, but I am not going to force you to do anything. I like my women very, very willing.

I also like my women spirited, with a lot of fire in their bodies. And after watching your videos, I have fallen so hard for you. That fire you have, that energy, it is something I am eager to experience firsthand. But I will give you time to think about this. I know it must be a shock." "Why would you want me? Everyone else is calling me names and you are telling me you want me?" "Because I see what others do not. And if you agree to be my woman, I promise I will remove every trace of that video from social media. Completely.

As though it never existed." I stared at him, my mind racing, trying to find the trap. There was always a trap with men like this. Dominic had taught me that Men with money and power did not give things away for free. They collected. They owned. They used. "In the meantime," he said, reaching into his pocket and pulling out a card, "you can leave it you want. The door is not locked. Here is my card. I already have your number. Save mine. If you agree to my proposal, let me know immediately" I took the card, my fingers brushing against his, and I nodded.

He smiled, warm and confident, and he turned and walked away, leaving me alone in that ridiculous mansion with a card in my hand and a future I had not expected waiting for me to decide. I walked outside in a daze, and a man in a driver's uniform approached me and said, "I am the driver of Senator Gath's son. I have been instructed to take you home." +15 Bonus I nodded and got into the back of the car, a sleek black Rolls Royce that smelled like leather and money, and I pulled out my phone as the driver pulled away from the mansion.

I searched for Senator Gath, for Emerson Gath, scrolling through articles and photos and biographies, and my eyes widened with every piece of information I absorbed. They were wealthy, almost as wealthy as Dominic. Dominic was still number one, but the Gaths were right behind him. And they had something Dominic did not have. Power. Political influence. Connections that reached into every corner of the country. But I had to be careful. Rich people were dangerous. Dominic had taught me that too. When something was too good to be true, it usually was.

chapters.title: Chapter 250
chapters.content:
Chapter 250 I waited until the Rolls Royce disappeared around the corner, and then I walked toward my house, and as I got closer, I started screaming. "What are you doing here? Your sister has already ruined me! She has destroyed me completely! Have you seen the videos? She used my face to make fake videos! Everyone thinks it is me! She made good on her threats! She threatened me this morning and now she has done it! Just leave me alone! Your sister has ruined my life!" - "Seraphine, please," Felix said, his face full of guilt, his hands reaching for me. "Please do not cry.

I will take care of everything. I promise I will make sure everything is fine." "No! I do not want to live anymore! Just leave me alone!" I ran into the house, and he followed me, and I did not stop running until I reached my storage closet and pulled out a rope. I grabbed a stool and climbed onto it, my hands shaking as I tried to tie the rope to the ceiling, as I tried to loop it around my neck. But Felix was there in seconds, pulling me down, his arms wrapped around my waist, his voice desperate in my ear. "What are you doing? How can you want to end your life?

Do not do this to yourself, Seraphine! You still have so much to live for! I collapsed onto the floor, sobbing, my whole body shaking, and I said, "I have nothing left to live for! Your sister took my husband! She ruined my reputation! She destroyed me! I cannot even show my face in public anymore!" "You have me," he said, pulling me into his arms. "You have me, Seraphine." What do I do with a loser like you? I thought as I cried into his shoulder, my tears soaking his shirt.

But I kept up the performance, kept my body shaking, kept my voice broken, until he finally said, "I promise you, I will get justice for you." "Just leave," I said. "I want to be alone. I cannot look at you, Felix. You have the same face as Celeste. Every time I look at you, I see her, and the pain gets worse." "But I cannot leave you like this. How can I leave you in this condition?" "I will be fine. I promise I will not harm myself.

But please, just let me be alone." He stood up, his face hard with resolve, and he said, "I will not spare Celeste." And then he turned and walked out, the door clicking shut behind him. I waited until I heard his car start and drive away. Then I stood up, brushed the dust off my clothes, and said to myself, "Wow. That was quite a performance, Seraphine. I hope he does not come back." I was walking toward my bedroom to take a shower when my phone buzzed with a text message. I opened it, and my eyes went wide. A credit alert. Five billion dollars.

Sitting in my account like it was the most natural thing in the world. A text message followed: This is just a little incentive while I wait for you to make up your mind. I wanted you to know that I can do anything for you. Also, I have gotten rid of your viral videos as a sign of good faith. They are completely off social media. That way you can know how serious I am about you. I screamed, a sound of pure disbelief and joy, and I scrambled to check online, scrolling frantically through every platform, every search result, every feed. Nothing. The videos were gone. Wiped clean.

As though they had never existed. "I cannot believe this," I whispered to myself. "This is real. This is actually real." I checked my bank account. Five billion dollars. Five billion. Celeste had slept with Dominic, degraded herself, destroyed my marriage, all for five billion dollars. And I had gotten the same amount for nothing. Just for the chance that I might say yes to Emerson Gath. I pulled out his card, my hands trembling with excitement, and I dialed his number. He answered on the second ring. +15 Bonus "My answer is yes," I said. "Yes, I agree. I accept.

I am going to be your woman." "Good," he said, and I could hear the smile in his voice. "Get ready. I will send my driver to pick you up tonight. We have a lot to talk about." "I am looking forward to it." The call ended, and I stood there in my living room staring at my phone, at my bank account, at the empty news feeds that no longer held my shame. I had lost Dominic Ford and thought my life was over. But here I was, rising from the ashes like I was born to do it. I am going to rise so much higher than anyone ever expected me to. My enemies will never see me coming.

chapters.title: Chapter 251
chapters.content:
Chapter 251 SERAPHINE The dress I chose was blood red, a slip of silk that barely qualified as clothing, cut so low at the front that the curve of my breasts looked like an invitation and split so high at the thigh that walking became a promise. I stood in front of the mirror and tumed slowly, watching the fabric catch the light, watching the way it clung to every dip and swell of my body like it had been painted on. My hair fell in dark waves past my shoulders, loose and deliberate, and I had lined my eyes with enough kohl to make my gaze look dangerous. Red lips.

Gold heels that strapped around my ankles. A thin chain around my waist that jingled softly when I moved. I looked expensive. I looked like a woman who had just been given five billion dollars and wanted the world to know she was worth every penny. The driver arrived exactly on time, the black car with tinted windows pulled up to my gate and waited without honking. I grabbed a small clutch, checked my reflection one last time, and walked out the door with my head high. The driver opened the back door for me and I slid in.

He said nothing as he pulled away from the curb, and I said nothing either, because my heart was too busy hammering against my ribs to form coherent words. Everything still felt like a dream. But the money in my account reminded me it was reality. I pulled out my phone for the tenth time since leaving the house and opened my banking app. I stared at the numbers, the nine zeros lined up in neat rows, and a smile spread across my face so wide my cheeks ached. Five billion dollars. Sitting in my account. Mine.

I had done nothing for it except exist, except catch the attention of a man who had seen my most humiliating moment and decided he wanted me. I laughed softly, shaking my head, and tucked the phone back into my clutch. Life was strange. Life was cruel and unfair and then, without warning, it handed you a gift so absurd you could only laugh. I looked out the window as the city rolled past, the streetlights blurring into streaks of gold and white, and I wondered what Emerson Gath truly wanted from me.

Men like him did not give five billion dollars to women they had just met unless they wanted something specific. But I had already decided I did not care. Whatever he wanted, I would give it. Whatever price he asked, I would pay. Because I had seen what the bottom looked like, had been scraped against it until I bled, and I was never going back there again. The car turned into a private driveway lined with tall hedges, the gates swinging open automatically as we approached.

The main building rose three stories high, its facade a blend of modern glass and classical stone, and the lights inside glowed warm and golden, inviting and intimidating all at once. The driver parked at the entrance and came around to open my door. I stepped out, smoothed my dress, and followed him inside. I kept my expression neutral as I walked, but inside I was cataloging everything, calculating the cost of every piece of furniture, every art fixture, every crystal drop on the chandeliers. This was old money. Political money.

The kind of wealth that did not need to announce itself because everyone already knew it was there. I was escorted to a study at the end of a long hallway. The doors were heavy wood, carved with patterns I did not recognize, and when they swung open, I stepped into a room that smelled of leather and aged whiskey and something else, something sharp and masculine that made the hairs on my arm stand up. The study was vast. Bookshelves lined every wall, their spines a rainbow of rich colors, and a massive oak desk sat at the center of the room like a throne.

chapters.title: Chapter 252
chapters.content:
Chapter 252 Emerson was there, standing by the fireplace with a glass in his hand. He looked exactly as I remembered, tall and broad- shouldered, his suit charcoal gray and perfectly tailored, his dark hair swept back from a face that belonged on magazine covers, He smiled when he saw me, a slow curve of his lips that did not quite reach his eyes, and he crossed the room with easy strides to take my hand. He lifted my hand to his lips and pressed a kiss to my knuckles, his eyes holding mine the entire time. Up close, he was even more striking.

Strong jaw, sharp cheekbones, a nose that looked like it had been broken once and healed slightly crooked, giving his face character it would not have otherwise had. "Seraphine," he said, his voice low and warm. "You look more breathtaking than you did a few hours ago." "Thank you," I said, and I let my own smile show as I said words I didn't get the chance to say before. "You have a beautiful home." "It's just a house. It's the people inside that make it a home." I almost laughed at that, at how perfectly practiced the line was, how smoothly it rolled off his tongue.

But I kept my composure, kept my smile soft and my eyes bright. Then I noticed the other man. He had been standing in the shadows by the far bookshelf, half hidden by the angle of the light, and when he stepped forward, I felt my breath catch in my throat. He was tall, just as tall as Emerson, with a leaner build and lighter hair, a golden blond that caught the firelight and turned it into something almost ethereal.

His eyes were a pale gray, the color of storm clouds, and his suit was navy blue, perfectly fitted, and when he smiled, it was slower than Emerson's, more deliberate, like he was savoring a secret he had not yet shared. He walked toward me with the same easy confidence, took my hand, and pressed his lips to my knuckles in the same gesture. But his kiss lingered a fraction of a second longer, and when he looked up at me, there was something in his eyes that made my stomach tighten. "Emerson has told me so much about you," the man said.

"Has he now?" "All good things, I assure you." Emerson stepped closer, his hand settling on the small of my back, a light possessive pressure that told me everything I needed to know about how this night was going to go. "Seraphine, this is Shane. My best friend. We've known each other since we were boys, and there is no one in this world I trust more." "It's a pleasure to meet you, Shane," I said. "The pleasure is all mine." There was a beat of silence, the kind that felt weighted, and then Emerson spoke again, his voice casual, like he was discussing the weather.

"Shane and I share everything, Seraphine. We always have. Businesses, investments, secrets. And now, Shane has expressed an interest in you as well." I kept my smile steady, kept my breathing even, but inside, something clicked into place. Of course. Of course there was a catch. Five billion dollars did not fall into your lap without bigger strings attached, and now I was seeing exactly what those strings looked like. "She would belong to both of us," Emerson continued, his tone still light, still conversational. "If you agree, of course." I looked at him, then at Shane, then back at him.
