| reached up and wiped them away with my thumb, and the gesture was so familiar, so maternal, that it made my heart ache. "Growing up, | had to watch Lynette waste away. She loved you so much, Tasha. She wanted nothing more than to be with you, to hold you, to have you back. So | focused on my studies. | took my lessons. | learned how to fight, learned how to hack, learned how to survive so | could find you by any means possible. Before | could find you, Lynette passed away. But on her dying bed, she made me promise to look for you.

And I have spent every day since then trying to keep that promise.

chapters.title: Chapter 299
chapters.content:
Chapter 299 When | eventually found you, you were already under Big Bryan's control. And | am no match for Big Bryan. | may have a few skills, but he is way out of my league. Sparrow is the only one who can stop him. Sparrow is way stronger than Big Bryan, he has more reach, more influence, and he has a personal vendetta against him. Big Bryan did something horrible to Sparrow years ago, something he has never forgiven.

So | knew that no matter what, Sparrow would not be able to turn down a chance for revenge." Tasha was quiet for a long moment, her eyes searching my face like she was looking for the lie, the catch, the angle. | let her look. | had nothing left to hide. "So you are saying you met with Sparrow, you took all the risk, you slept with him, just to help me and the other girls?" "Yes.

"And you did not want Julian to sleep with me last night because it would be too painful for me to still go ahead and sleep with Sparrow today." "That is exactly right." "But it still sounds strange to me." She shook her head, her voice trembling. "Even though | am your blood, you barely know me. | am nobody. | am just a girl who grew up in the wrong house with the wrong people. | am nothing." "You are not nothing." | gripped her hands so hard my knuckles went white. "You are the only family | have left in this world.

Everything | did, every man | slept with, every lie | told, every line | crossed, | did it for you. | joined the Phantom Circle for you. | got close to Damon for you. | convinced him to convince Big Bryan to let us come to this city for you. | let Julian catch us, | let him lock us up, | let him think he owned me, all because | knew that eventually, somehow, it would lead me to Sparrow. And it did. It led me right to him." Tasha stared at me, and | watched the understanding dawn in her eyes like a slow sunrise. "Big Bryan may have acted as though he liked you.

| saw how friendly he was with you. But he was a horrible man, Tasha. He slept with all the girls who worked for him, except the ones he called the caged birds. You were a caged bird. He left you untouched because you fell under a different category. The caged birds are sold off at auctions to rich, horrible men, and these men turn them into sex slaves. Eventually, these men get bored, and many of the girls do not survive. That was what was waiting for you.

Bryan would have made sure of it." She shuddered, and | pulled her into my arms without thinking, holding her tight the way Lynette used to hold me when | was small and afraid. "You also have something in your body," | said against her hair. "Something called Hemovax. Every three months, Big Bryan arranged for you girls to get check- ups, right?" She nodded against my shoulder. "Those were not check-ups. You were being poisoned. Every three months, you had to get another dosage. If you failed to do it, you would die. Jasmine, Maya, you... all three of you.

| never got those drugs because | joined voluntarily. But you have just one month left. If in one month you do not get the antidote, all of you are going to die. Everything | am doing now is to prevent that from happening." Tasha pulled back and looked at me, her eyes red- rimmed and swollen but clearer than | had ever seen them. "Okay. So now you have gotten me out. But what about Maya and Jasmine?" "1 will go back for them. | give you my word. We do not need to put up with Julian anymore. | was only bearing with him for the time being.

And as for Sparrow..." | hesitated, because this was the part | had been dreading, the part that made me want to punch a hole through the nearest wall "| know he is not going to be easy. He is a wild man. Very wild in bed. And | know you are innocent. | know this will be hard for you. But just try to play along, okay? All you need to do is go on your knees, unzip his pants, take out his cock, and start sucking it. | never bothered to teach you this before because | never planned for you to do it. So | know it will be hard.

chapters.title: Chapter 300
chapters.content:
Chapter 300 But just bear with it, okay? The sex will likely be rough, and it will hurt. | wish there was a way | could prevent this, but it is out of my hands. Nothing is more important than you being alive right now, and Sparrow is our only solution." Tasha was quiet for a long time after | finished. The clock above the concierge desk ticked away the seconds, and | could feel the deadline approaching like a physical weight pressing down on my chest. "So, in the end, you became a whore for me. You let men use your body for me. You risked your life over and over for me.

Because of a promise you made to a mother | never knew." Her lips were trembling. "Lynette loved you so much, Tasha. If she were here right now, she would tell you herself. She would hold you and never let you go." Tasha closed her eyes, and when she opened them again, there was something new in her expression, something that looked almost like peace. "The woman | grew up with, | knew she was my stepmother. There was no way she could be my real mother. She was horrible to me. | was a maid in that house, slaving every day for her and her children.

And then one day, Big Bryan showed up and took me away. | did not know what he wanted from me. | even thought that life with him was better because at least | got to eat well." She laughed, a small bitter sound. "But thanks to you, | now understand how much danger | was in. And you made it possible so | would not go through it. You are so good to me, Scarlett." "Itis fine." | wiped at her tears again, careful not to smudge what was left of her makeup. "Come on, do not ruin your face, Natasha. | will do anything for you. That goes without question. | love you so much.

| am your only blood family left, the only one | know of, and | will always have your back. | want you to remember that." She nodded, and we looked at each other for along moment, and then we made up our minds and stood up together, hand in hand, and walked toward the elevator that would take us up to Sparrow. The penthouse was exactly as | remembered it from the night before, vast, glittering, obscenely luxurious in a way that made you feel both awed and slightly nauseous.

Sparrow welcomed us at the door with that same sharp, assessing gaze, and when his eyes settled on Tasha, | saw something flicker in them that made my stomach tighten. Interest. Genuine interest. | had dressed her too well. "You wait here," he told me a few minutes later, and then to Tasha: "You come with me." And then they were gone, the bedroom door closing behind them with a soft click that sounded to my ears like a gunshot. | paced the living room like a caged animal, my mind racing through every possible scenario. What if he hurt her too much? What if she froze and couldn't move an inch?

| had read Sparrow's file, or what little of it existed...the man did not sleep with the same woman twice, preferred a different bed partner every night, and had a reputation for being brutal even by the standards of men who made their living through brutality. If he hurt Tasha too badly, if he broke her the way he must have broken so many others, | would never forgive myself. | would spend the rest of my life finding a way to make him pay, even if it killed me. The minutes crawled past like hours. | checked the time. | checked it again.

| considered pressing my ear to the door, decided against it, considered it again, and was halfway to the door when | heard Sparrow's voice, loud and furious, cutting through the penthouse like a blade. "Scarlett!" | rushed into the room before my brain had time to catch up with my feet, and the first thing | saw was Tasha scrambling past me, half-dressed, her face flushed red, her eyes wet with tears. She fled through the door without a backward glance, and | felt a complex rush of emotions, terror that Sparrow was angry, relief that Tasha was unhurt, confusion about what had gone wrong.

chapters.title: Chapter 301
chapters.content:
Chapter 301 And then Sparrow was in front of me, his hand closing around my throat, pushing me against the wall. When | found out why he was upset, the relief that flooded through me was so intense it almost made my knees buckle. He had not hurt her. He had rejected her. She was safe. She was safe, and | could have wept with the sheer magnitude of my gratitude. In the end, Sparrow took me instead, used me the way | offered myself to be used, broke his own rule of not having the same woman he'd already had, and the deal was still intact. We were still going to survive this.

When he offered me the marriage deal afterward, | was completely shocked. | let the silence stretch between us while | did the arithmetic in my head. A year of my life. A year of playing the part, of smiling for the cameras, of spreading my legs whenever he wanted. In exchange for everything; Big Bryan destroyed, the girls saved, enough money to disappear forever. It was the best deal | had ever been offered. But | passed it off to Tasha. It was a perfect arrangement. As Sparrow's wife, even for just a year, Tasha would be untouchable. No one would dare hurt her.

No one would dare come near her. She would be protected in a way | could never protect her, shielded by Sparrow's reputation and his resources and his terrifying reach. And once the year was over, | could take her far away, somewhere no one knew our names, and we could start over. A hundred million dollars from Julian, sitting in accounts | had quietly diverted, would be more than enough to give her the life she deserved. | could not believe how lucky | had gotten. When Sparrow dismissed me, telling me to bring Maya and Jasmine that very night, | quickly slipped out of the penthouse.

Tasha was staying behind, so Sparrow knew | wasnt messing around. But | did not take the front exit. Julian's men were still waiting outside the hotel, parked in the loading zone, and if they saw me leaving alone, there would be questions | could not answer. So | found the service elevator, slipped past the kitchen staff who were too busy to notice one more person in the chaos, and exited through the back of the hotel into an alley that smelled of garbage and frying oil.

| hailed a cab and gave the driver the address of Julian's apartment, and as the city lights blurred past the window, | let myself feel something | had not felt in years. Real, genuine, terrifying hope. We were going to survive this. Tasha was going to be safe. Maya and Jasmine were going to get the antidote. Big Bryan was going to be destroyed. And then we were going to disappear, all of us, and build new lives somewhere far away from men like Julian and monsters like Big Bryan. But first, | had something important to take care of.

chapters.title: Chapter 302
chapters.content:
Chapter 302 SCARLETT | had been mapping a building in my head, every time Julian's men escorted me back. | knew where the cameras were positioned and where their blind spots began, knew the rotation of the night shift guards and which ones smoked at two in the morning. Julian thought he was keeping me prisoner, but the truth was simpler and considerably more insulting to his ego: | had been casing his operation from the inside, and he had been too busy staring at my tits to notice.

The cab dropped me two blocks from the building, far enough that none of Julian's men would see me approaching, close enough that | could cover the distance on foot without arriving looking like | had just run a marathon. | paid the driver in cash, slipped out of the back seat, and began walking with the unhurried stride of a woman who had every right to be on this particular street at this particular hour.

The evening air was cool against my bare arms, still carrying the faint chemical sweetness of the hotel shampoo Sparrow kept in his penthouse bathroom, and | wondered briefly whether the universe had a sense of humor broad enough to appreciate a woman who went directly from one man's bed to another man's apartment to commit what was probably going to be several felonies before sunrise. My heels made soft clicking sounds on the pavement, the only noise in a street that was otherwise holding its breath.

| had changed out of the dress I'd worn to Sparrow's and into something darker, something that wouldn't catch the light if | had to move quickly through poorly lit corridors. Black jeans, black shirt, my hair pulled back tight against my skull so no one could grab itin a fight. | looked like a cat burglar's understudy, which was not far from the truth, except that | was not stealing anything. Tonight, | was taking back what was already mine.

The service entrance was exactly where | had noted it on my mental blueprint: a nondescript gray door tucked into an alcove between two dumpsters that smelled like they had not been emptied since the previous administration. No camera on this side, because Julian's security team had apparently never met a woman who wasn't afraid of garbage, and the lock was the same cheap deadbolt they had been using since | first arrived, the kind you could pop with a credit card if you knew what you were doing. | knew what | was doing.

The door swung open with a soft click, and | slipped inside, my eyes adjusting to the dim fluorescent lighting of the service corridor while my ears paid attention to the soft shuffle of a guard's footsteps not too far away. | had spent years learning how to move in spaces where | was not supposed to be. And I'd learned this: invisibility was not about hiding. It was about being so unremarkable that no one bothered to remember you were there.

| applied the principle now, moving through the service corridor with the quiet confidence of someone who belonged exactly where she was, my footsteps light and even, my breathing slow and controlled. The first guard was Stationed at the junction where the service corridor met the main hallway, a large man with a neck thicker than my thigh and the kind of dead-eyed stare that suggested he had been standing in the same spot for so long his brain had entered a low-power conservation mode. He did not hear me coming.

| had learned the death strike from a former special forces operative who ran a self-defense class out of a strip mall dojo in the bad part of town, the kind of place where the mats smelled like feet and the instructor's knuckles were permanently swollen from demonstrating techniques on volunteers who had not volunteered quickly enough The strike itself was simple: a precise blow to the brachial plexus, the bundle of nerves that ran along the side of the neck, delivered with enough force to disrupt the nerve signals traveling between the brain and the rest of the body.

It did not kill, despite what the name suggested. It simply turned off the target's consciousness like flipping a light switch, and when it was done correctly, which it almost always was when | did it, the target collapsed in a heap with no more sound than a sack of potatoes hitting the floor.

chapters.title: Chapter 303
chapters.content:
Chapter 303 The first guard made exactly that sound. | caught him before his head could strike the concrete, lowered him gently to the ground, and dragged his considerable bulk behind a stack of empty pallets that someone had left in the corridor. One down. Five to go. The second guard who was patrolling the entrance was even easier than the first because he had his back to me and his earbuds in, listening to something with enough bass that | could feel the vibrations through the air before | was close enough to strike. | almost felt bad for him.

The death strike dropped him mid-step, and | dragged his body into the shadow, arranging his limbs so he would not be immediately visible to anyone. His music was still playing, a tinny pulse of electronic noise that faded as | moved away. Three and four were together, which was a complication | had anticipated but still dreaded. They were probably two men who had been working together long enough that they had developed the kind of silent communication that made them more dangerous as a pair than they would have been individually.

| watched them from the shadows for a full two minutes, cataloguing their positions, their body language, the frequency with which they glanced in my direction, and when | had enough data to work with, | made my decision. | walked out with my shoulders back and my chin up, the posture of a woman who had every right to be there, and the momentary flicker of recognition on their faces, the split second of hesitation that came from seeing a familiar figure, was all the time | needed. The first one went down before he could open his mouth to ask what | was doing outside the apartment alone.

The second one reached for his weapon, his hand closing around the grip with the practiced efficiency of someone who had drilled the motion a thousand times, but | was already inside his guard, my palm driving upward into the soft flesh beneath his chin, and his eyes rolled back in his head before his finger ever found the trigger. | dragged their bodies into a supply closet and locked the door behind me, my heart hammering against my ribs in a rhythm that was equal parts exhilaration and terror. Four down. Two to go.

The last two were stationed at the apartment door itself, which meant there was no way to approach them without being seen. | had known this from the beginning. The entrance leading to Julian's apartment door was long and straight and brightly lit, a shooting gallery for anyone stupid enough to try a frontal assault, and the two men guarding the door were the best Julian had, the ones he trusted to protect him while he slept.

They saw me the moment | turned the corner, and their reaction was immediate: a tightening of postures, a shifting of weight, a barely perceptible movement of hands toward holsters that told me everything | needed to know about their training and their instincts. "Evening, gentlemen." | kept walking toward them, my stride unhurried, my smile easy, the smile of a woman who seemed to be their boss's favorite toy, and had never once given them a reason to consider her a threat.

"Julian asked me to come back alone and pick up something." The one on the left, a wiry man with a face like a hatchet and the kind of eyes that had seen too much to believe anything at face value, narrowed his gaze at me. "We haven't received any instructions." "Because I'm the instructions, genius." | was close enough now to see the individual pores on his nose, close enough to smell the coffee on his breath and the gun oil on his hands. "Do you want to call Julian at this hour and tell him you're questioning his orders?

Because | would love to be here when you have that conversation, but | have things to do, so let's speed this along." The one on the right, younger and dumber and clearly not entirely comfortable with the idea of pointing a weapon at a woman he had seen in significantly less clothing, shifted his weight from one foot to the other. " It's fine. You can go in."

chapters.title: Chapter 304
chapters.content:
Chapter 304 I sighed, the long-suffering sigh of a woman who had been sent on an errand by a man who did not appreciate her hard work. Hatchet-face was not buying it, | could see the skepticism hardening behind his eyes, but Baby-face was already relaxing, his hand typing in the code and unlocking the door, and that was all the opening | needed. | struck Hatchet-face first because he was the threat, my hand moving in the same precise arc that had dropped four other men tonight, and he went down with a grunt of surprise that died in his throat before it could become a warning.

Baby-face had time to register what was happening, time to reach for his weapon and begin the process of reacting, but his body was slower than his brain, and by the time his fingers found the grip of his gun, | had already pivoted and struck him in the exact same spot, watching his eyes go wide with disbelief before they rolled back and his body crumpled to the floor. Six guards down. But | didn't want any of the men to die.

So they could easily be found, | went through the trouble of retrieving all the other four unconscious men, one after the other, and leaving them just right outside the door. It took nearly ten minutes of dragging dead weight, and by the time | finished, sweat clung to the back of my dress. I had actually memorized the access code a while ago, watching Julian's fingers dance across the keypad with the casual arrogance of a man who had never considered that the woman standing behind him might be paying attention. But | couldn't take any chances.

What if the password was changed after | left with Tasha? That was why | had the men unlock the door before | took them out. Now, | pushed the door open and stepped inside. The apartment was quiet, lit only by the pale amber glow of the city filtering through the floor-to-ceiling windows. Julian was on the couch, exactly where | had expected him to be, his head tilted back against the cushions, his mouth slightly open, an empty whiskey glass on the coffee table in front of him and the faint sour smell of alcohol hanging in the air around him like a ghost. He was asleep.

Actually, genuinely asleep. | stood over him for a moment, watching the steady rise and fall of his chest. | left him snoring on the couch and made my way to the bedroom where Maya and Jasmine were, my footsteps silent, my heart rate finally beginning to slow from its combat pace to something approaching normal. The bedroom door was unlocked, Julian had never bothered to lock it, because where were they going to go, and when | pushed it open, | found both of them awake and waiting, their faces illuminated by the thin strip of light from the hallway.

Maya was sitting on the edge of the bed with her knees drawn up to her chest, her hair falling around her face in tangled waves. Jasmine was standing by the window with her arms crossed over her chest, her expression guarded and suspicious in equal measure, the expression of a woman who had learned the hard way that hope was just another word for disappointment. "Get ready," | whispered, keeping my voice low enough that it would not carry down the hallway to where Julian was sleeping. "We're leaving. Right now.

Both of you." Maya's eyes went wide, and | could see the war playing out behind them: hope fighting against fear, relief struggling against the learned helplessness that had been drilled into her since the day Big Bryan's men dragged her into the Phantom Circle. "How? The guards..." "The guards are sleeping. All six of them. They're going to stay that way for a while, but we need to move. Jasmine did not ask questions.

She was already pulling on her shoes, her movements quick and efficient, the movements of someone who had been waiting for exactly this moment and was not going to waste a single second of it on unnecessary conversation. Maya followed a beat later, her hands shaking so badly she could barely tie her laces, and | had to resist the urge to do it for her, to treat her like the child she sometimes seemed to be even though she was only a year younger than all of us.

chapters.title: Chapter 305
chapters.content:
Chapter 305 | left them to finish getting ready and crept back to the living room, positioning myself behind the door where | could see Julian on the couch through the narrow gap between the hinges and the frame. He was still asleep, still snoring, still completely unaware that his carefully constructed prison had just been broken open by a woman he had dismissed as nothing more than a talented whore. The irony was so rich | could practically taste it, and | allowed myself a small smile in the darkness before the sound of a phone ringing cut through the silence like a blade. Julian's phone.

On the coffee table. Vibrating against the wood with the insistent urgency of someone who was not going to stop calling until they got an answer. | watched him stir, watched his hand fumble across the table in search of the phone, watched his eyes blink open and then narrow as he registered the name on the screen. The call was important. | could tell from the way his posture changed, the way his shoulders tightened and his jaw locked, that whatever news was coming through that call was not going to be good.

"What happened?" His voice was rough with sleep, the words slurring together at the edges. | could not hear the other side of the conversation, but I could read the responses in Julian's face the way | had learned to read every man who had ever tried to own me. Confusion first, the brow furrowing, the lips pressing together. Then disbelief, his free hand coming up to rub at his temple like he was trying to physically massage the information into his brain. Then anger, the jaw clenching, the knuckles going white around the phone, the whole body tensing like a spring being compressed.

Julian's response hit the air like gunshots, and | felt my own eyebrows rise in surprise. Celeste had filed for divorce. Celeste, Julian's wife, the woman he had been obsessing over since the day | met him, was finally cutting the cord. | would have applauded if | had not been busy hiding behind a door and trying not to breathe too loudly. "There has to be something we can do." Julian's voice was climbing now, the controlled fury giving way to something closer to panic. "A delay.

A counter-filing Something." | watched him listen to whatever his lawyer was saying, watched the color drain from his face, watched his free hand curl into a fist at his side. "No," he said, and the word came out louder than he probably intended, echoing off the walls of the empty apartment. "No, this cannot happen now. | need more time. | need time to show Celeste what kind of man Dominic really is. Once she sees the videos, once she understands that he is no better than me, she will reconsider. She has to reconsider." | almost laughed out loud.

He was still clinging to the Dominic Ford plan, still convinced that the footage | was supposedly retrieving right now was going to be his salvation, still completely unaware that Dominic Ford did not exist in my agenda. The call ended, and Julian sat there on the couch for a long moment, his phone clutched in his hand, his chest heaving with the effort of processing everything that had just been dumped on him. Then he pushed himself to his feet and headed for the door, moving with the jerky, uncoordinated stride of a man who was fully panicked, and | knew that this was my moment.

| slipped out from behind the door and followed him, my footsteps silent, my body moving with the fluid, predatory grace that had been drilled into me through years of training and necessity. He reached the door and pulled it open, and | saw him stop, saw his shoulders go rigid, saw the exact moment when his brain registered that the guards who were supposed to be guarding the house were currently unconscious on the floor.

He stepped back into the apartment and slammed the door, his hands fumbling for the deadbolt, and then he turned to run for the room at the end of the hallway, and | struck him. The blow landed exactly where | intended it to land, the same spot on the neck that had dropped six other men tonight, delivered with the same precision and the same force. Julian went down like a building imploding, his legs folding beneath him, his body hitting the floor with a dull thud that | felt through the soles of my shoes.

He landed on his back, his eyes open and staring at the ceiling, his mouth forming a word that never made it past his lips.

chapters.title: Chapter 306
chapters.content:
Chapter 306 "Scarlett?" My name. The last thing he said before the darkness took him. | stood over his unconscious body and felt something that was halfway between satisfaction and disgust. For some reason, this victory tasted surprisingly similar to ash. | could kill him. The thought surfaced in my mind with the clarity of a bell ringing in still air, and | did not push it away.

| had never directly committed murder before, had always found a way to accomplish my goals without crossing that particular line, but standing over Julian Fisher's prone body with the knowledge of everything he had done to Maya and Jasmine and me and probably dozens of other women | did not even know about, | felt the urge rise up in my chest like a physical thing, hot and sharp and almost impossible to resist. He had forced himself on Jasmine yesterday.

Not just used her, not just taken what he wanted in the way that men like him always did, but actually, deliberately raped her out of jealousy and possessiveness and the kind of twisted entitlement that made my stomach turn. | lifted my leg and brought my foot down on his chest, hard, the impact jarring through my ankle and up into my hip. He did not move. He did not flinch. He just lay there, unconscious and helpless, and | realized with a strange mixture of relief and shame that | could not do it. | could not kill a man in cold blood, no matter how much he deserved it. | was not a murderer.

| was a survivor, and sometimes those two things looked the same, but they were not, and the distinction mattered more than | had ever allowed myself to admit. | turned my back on Julian Fisher and walked back to the bedroom where Maya and Jasmine were waiting, their faces pale with fear and anticipation, their bags clutched against their chests like shields. "Come on," | said, my voice steady despite the trembling in my hands.

"Let's go." We moved through the apartment in silence, stepping over Julian's unconscious body on our way to the door, and neither of them asked what had happened to him. Perhaps they could see the answer in my face. Perhaps they simply did not want to know. We slipped out, past the guards | had left crumpled on the floor.

| could feel the adrenaline beginning to fade, replaced by a bone-deep exhaustion that | had been holding at bay through sheer force of will, and by the time we emerged into the alley behind the building, my legs were shaking and my hands were numb and | was fairly certain that if | stopped moving for more than thirty seconds, | would collapse and not get up again for a week.

We walked two blocks before | felt safe enough to hail a cab, and when one finally pulled up to the curb, a dented yellow sedan with a driver who looked like he had seen enough strange things in his career that three women emerging from an alley at this hour did not even register on his list of concerns, | herded Maya and Jasmine into the back seat and gave him the address of the Beaumont Hotel. The cab pulled away from the curb, and we sat in silence for the first several blocks, the city lights sliding past the windows in long amber streaks.

Maya was staring out the window with the glassy-eyed expression of someone who had not yet processed that she was free. Jasmine was staring at me. "Why did you do that to me?" The question came out flat and hard, the voice of a woman who had been holding it in for hours and was finally giving it permission to escape. | turned to face her, and the look in her eyes was not anger exactly. It was something more complicated, something that had been simmering beneath the surface since the moment | told her to stuff her underwear with tampons and pretend to be menstruating.

"| couldn't speak before because we were in the house," Jasmine continued, her voice low and controlled. "But | know that everything you did was to protect Tasha. Isn't it?" The cab driver glanced at us in the rearview mirror and then very deliberately returned his attention to the road. He had almost certainly heard stranger conversations in his cab, and he had almost certainly learned that the safest response was to pretend he had not heard anything at all.

chapters.title: Chapter 307
chapters.content:
Chapter 307 "Tasha has always been your favorite, right? I've seen it. All three of us are your friends. You met all of us at Big Bryan's. But you always treated Tasha differently, and | never complained about it, but now | need to know why. You used my name. You told Julian to take me instead of her. You wanted Julian to have sex with me so that Tasha would not have to. Isn't that exactly what happened?" "No." The word came out faster than | intended, sharper. "No, it is not the way you are thinking. Listen to me, Jasmine. Tasha is still a virgin." "And I'm not.

So Julian gets to rape me because I've already been used. Is that the logic?" "The man Sparrow, the one | told you about, the one who can get rid of the poison in your body, he agreed to help us. But he asked for Tasha specifically. If Julian had been with Tasha last night, she would have been too sore today to go be with Sparrow. And Sparrow is rough, Jasmine. Sparrow is much rougher than Julian, and if Tasha had shown up already used and already sore, he might have rejected her. He might have rejected all of us.

| was trying to look at the bigger picture." Jasmine stared at me for a long moment, her dark eyes unreadable in the shifting light of the passing streetlamps. "And if Julian had killed me? If he had decided | wasn't worth the trouble and put a bullet in my head, what would the bigger picture have looked like then?" "He was never going to kill you. Julian does not kill his toys. He breaks them, but he does not throw them away. "| reached out and took her hand, and she let me, which was more than | deserved. "| am sorry.

| did not want Julian to do that to you, and | did not want to sacrifice you. But this was the only solution. The poison in your body, the Hemovax, you do not have much time left. If in one month you do not get the antidote, you are going to die. Maya is going to die. Tasha is going to die. Everything | am doing now is to prevent that from happening." Maya spoke for the first time since we had left the apartment, her voice small and trembling but steadier they are going to pay.

Chapter 310 "Dominic Ford," | said, shaking my head slowly from side to side, "you were supposed to leave for work an hour ago. Your driver has been waiting outside since seven. "For you, Celeste, | am willing to be late to work for the rest of my life. Let the board of directors fire me. Let the shareholders revolt. Let the stock price plummet. None of it matters. This, right here, matters.

Watching you put on your lipstick matters more than every business meeting | have ever attended." "That is absurd." "That is love." "That is financial irresponsibility, is what that is." He laughed then, a genuine laugh that transformed his entire face, and for a moment | forgot that there was a driver waiting outside, forgot that Helix had samples that needed processing, forgot that | was still technically married to a man whose face | never wanted to see again, forgot everything except the sound of Dominic Ford laughing in the morning light that streamed through the floor-to-ceiling windows and painted golden rectangles across the dark hardwood floor.

"| want to tell you something." His voice had shifted, the playfulness receding slightly, replaced by something more earnest, something that made his eyes look deeper and more serious than they had been a moment ago. Just the truth, laid bare between us like an offering. "For giving me a chance. For choosing me, Celeste.

In the end, you chose me, and | don't think | will ever stop being grateful for that." | reached up and cupped his face in both my hands, feeling the slight roughness of his jaw beneath my palms, the warmth of his skin, the steady pulse of his heartbeat that | could feel through my fingertips. "It was not as though there was a better option than you." His brows drew together, a crease forming between them.

"If someone better ever came along, does that mean you would leave me?" "What kind of question is that?" "A serious one." "Dominic." | pressed my palms more firmly against his cheeks, tilting his face down so that his eyes met mine directly, so that there could be no mistaking what | was about to say. "How could that ever happen? In my eyes, you are the best man who has ever walked into my life. No one else could ever be better than you, because there is no measurement, no scale, no universe in which anyone else compares. My eyes will only ever look at you.

Do you understand what | am telling you? Choosing you was not settling. Choosing you was not the safe option or the convenient option or the option that made the most sense on paper. Choosing you was the first time in my life | ever felt like | had actually won something. Like | had finally, against all odds, hit the jackpot.

And Dominic, money has absolutely nothing to do with what | just said." He pulled me into his arms before | could draw another breath, wrapping himself around me with a ferocity that knocked the air from my lungs, his face buried in the curve of my neck, his hands pressed flat against my back, and | felt the words before | heard them, felt them vibrate through his chest and into mine.

"| love this woman to the sky and beyond." | closed my eyes and let myself sink into him, breathing in the scent of his cologne, something warm and woody with an undercurrent of spice that reminded me of cedar and sandalwood and the faint, intoxicating trace of something | could never quite identify but always, always associated with him. He laid her gently across the back seat and got behind the wheel, and | climbed in beside her, holding her bloody hand between both of mine, telling her over and over that she would be fine, everything would be fine, even though | was not sure she could hear me. The guilt made it hard to breathe. If anything happened to Pat, | would never forgive myself.

Dominic drove to the best hospital in the city, and he had already made calls along the way, because when we pulled up, the staff and doctors were waiting outside with a rolling bed. They took Pat from the car, placed her on it, and wheeled her straight through the doors. We followed, but a nurse stopped us in the corridor and asked us to wait outside so the doctors would not be distracted. | held it together for about three seconds before | broke down, the tears coming hard and fast, my voice cracking as | repeated that it was all my fault, all my fault.

Dominic pulled me into his arms and held me tightly until | finally went quiet. We waited a long time before the doctor came out. My head whipped up the second | saw him, and the word tore out of me. "Pat..." "She will be fine," he cut in, and | sagged with relief so sudden it left me lightheaded. "We found traces of misoprostol in her system," the doctor continued, his voice calm and clinical. "She experienced substantial blood loss, severe pain, and dehydration.

Her blood pressure was very low when she was brought in, but the good news is that she will be fine in no time." | nodded, relief washing through me, but something in the back of my mind snagged on the word. Misoprostol. | knew that name, but | could not place it. The doctor turned to leave, and | called after him. "Hold on, doctor. What exactly did you say caused my friend's condition?" "Medication abortion." My eyes went wide, and the world tilted. Pat was pregnant?

chapters.title: Chapter 342
chapters.content:
Chapter 342 PAT The hours had ticked by when | finally looked up from my desk, and | had spent the whole day buried in work | no longer remembered starting. My shoulders ached, my eyes burned, but the exhaustion in my body was nothing next to the exhaustion in my chest, because the truth was that | had not been able to get past what happened, not really, and pretending otherwise was getting harder with every passing hour. | could not forgive myself. That was the plain and ugly center of it.

| was the older friend, the sensible one, the voice of reason who was supposed to hold the line while everyone else lost their minds. And what had | done the moment Kingsley Duke turned those eyes on me? | had folded like a teenager who had never once been told that beautiful men lie. How had | become this stupid? I used to be proud of my instincts. Every man | had ever dated eventually packed his bags and told me, with varying degrees of politeness, that | was too smart for him. | noticed things.

| caught the small cracks ina story the way other people caught a crooked picture frame, and | could not keep my mouth shut about them. Seraphine had warned me once, in that syrupy voice she used when she was being unhelpful, that a woman who acted like she knew too much was a turnoff, that men wanted to feel clever, not corrected. | had tried. | really had. But my nature always leaked out, usually in the middle of a perfectly nice dinner, and the man across the table would get that faraway look that meant he was already planning his exit.

Then Celeste almost stopped coming to Helix, and Seraphine drifted in now and then but barely lifted a finger, and | poured every last drop of myself into keeping the lab breathing. That was where my late twenties went. That was where my early thirties started. There was no time for men, no time for anything but Helix, and | crossed thirty without ever noticing the milestone until it was already behind me. Maybe that was it.

Maybe the loneliness had finally caught up with me, and the first time a handsome man looked at me like | was the only woman in the room, | had thrown my brain out the window and followed my body straight off the ledge. Even thinking about it made my face burn. | had given myself to him. Just like that. | had not verified a single one of the holes in the story he fed me, and there had been holes, real ones, wide enough to drive a truck through if | had only been paying attention. But | had not been paying attention. | had been too busy melting.

Celeste had told me he deleted the video, that it never reached Seraphine. | believed her, and | was grateful, but the relief did not wash away the shame. | had been an experiment. A transaction between him and Sera. The fact that he had a change of heart at the end did not make me feel one degree less cheap. It had been eleven days since | gave myself to him, and the sting of his betrayal was as fresh as the morning it happened. | had gotten very good at pretending over the past week and a half.

Celeste had been wonderful, more wonderful than | deserved, but only | knew how hard it was to stop hating myself long enough to smile. When Celeste moved in with Dominic more than a week ago, | assumed | would barely see her. | assumed wrong. She came early every morning and stayed until close. Some days she had lunch with Dominic, and some days she had lunch with me, and those lunches had slowly become the closest | had been to her in years. She opened up to me now in a way she never used to, and somewhere along the line | had become the person she trusted with the messy parts.

| tried to give her the same in return. big sale: 100 bonus free fou you

chapters.title: Chapter 343
chapters.content:
Chapter 343 She was glowing, honestly glowing, the way a woman glows when she is happy and well loved, and | was genuinely glad for her. | had convinced myself | was putting the Kingsley mess behind me, one day at a time. Today had shown me what a lie that was. Celeste had told me this morning that she would not be in. Her mother was not feeling well, and she wanted to spend the day with her. The lab was full, packed with the new scientists Celeste had brought in to lighten my load and speed up the research, but without her in the building | felt like a stranger in my own home.

| had retreated to my office, closed the door, and let the memories pour in, one after another, until | could barely breathe. | wanted to talk to someone. Celeste was the only person | trusted now, and she already had enough on her plate without me dragging my mess into her mother's sickroom. Then | felt it. A sudden, startling warmth between my legs, my panties wet against my skin, and | went still at my desk. | walked quickly to my accommodation, locked the bathroom door behind me, and checked. There it was, faint and pink, staining the cotton. Not the usual color of my period.

And | was not due for three more days. | stared at the stain for a long moment. My cycle had always been punctual to the point of being boring. It arrived all at once on the first day, stayed for three, then packed up and left. This was not that. This was a spotting | could not explain. Maybe it was different this time. Stress did strange things to a body. | shook it off, wiped, changed into fresh panties, and washed the stained pair in the sink until the water ran clear. Then | straightened my skirt, squared my shoulders, and walked back toward my office.

When | reached the door, my heart stopped. Kingsley Duke was standing beside it. He looked nothing like the man | had met. Nothing. The news five days ago had announced that the heir of the Duke family had recovered their stolen fortune, and Celeste had told me Sparrow would help him, and she had been right. Kingsley stood there now in clothes that probably cost more than my annual salary, carrying himself with the easy authority of a man who had been born into a boardroom, and he was even more handsome than | remembered, which felt deeply and personally unfair. | swallowed.

The pain in my chest was sharper than | expected, sharper than | wanted it to be. "What can | do for you, Mr. Duke?" He turned, and the relief on his face was so plain it almost made me angry. Down the corridor, a cluster of staff huddled together, staring at him with open admiration and whispering behind their hands. They had been crazy about him when he did not have a penny to his name, and | had been no different back then. God only knew how much crazier they were now that he was a big shot.

"1 need to talk to you, Pat." His voice was soft, and it sounded sincere, and | could not have cared less. " Please. Just give me some of your time." | walked past him, pushed open my door, and stepped inside. He followed, close enough that | caught his cologne, and | hated that | noticed it. Inside my office, | leaned back against my desk and folded my arms. "Say whatever you want to say." My chin lifted, and | let the words fall with all the warmth of a slammed door." And then get out." To my shock, Kingsley went down on his knees.

He remained on his knees, and for a long while he did not look at me at all. He kept his gaze fixed on the floor between us, and when he finally spoke, his voice came out low and rough, the voice of a man who had rehearsed this speech a hundred times in his own head and still could not make it sound the way he wanted.

chapters.title: Chapter 344
chapters.content:
Chapter 344 "| feel gravely ashamed kneeling here looking at you." He lifted his eyes then, and they were red at the rims, wet in the way a man's eyes go wet when he is fighting very hard not to cry. "But | had to face what | did. Saying sorry is not enough to beg for your forgiveness, Pat. | know that. | only hope you will give me the chance to make amends. But | will start with this." He swallowed hard. "l am very sorry." | folded my arms tighter and let the silence stretch until it sat between us like a third person in the room.

"You want my forgiveness?" He nodded, and for one wild moment | almost laughed at the absurdity of the whole scene. There he was, the heir of the Duke family, dressed in expensive clothes, kneeling on the floor of my office like a man begging a judge for mercy. The joke, of course, was on me, because some tired and stupid part of me wanted to believe him. | had carried this shame for eleven days. | had replayed my own foolishness every night until it felt like a stone lodged permanently behind my ribs. Maybe forgiveness was the only way to set the stone down.

Maybe it was the one thing | needed to do for myself, not for him. "| forgive you." The words came out flatter than | intended. "There is no need for you to kneel. Get up and leave." He stared at me as though | had struck him. Then he rose slowly to his feet and took a step toward me, but | shot my hand out between us. "Do not come any closer." "Pat, please." His voice cracked in the middle of my name. "Just give me a chance to court you properly." "Court me? Why?" "Because | want us to start over." "There is nothing between us to start over from." | kept my hand raised.

"| felt sorry for you back then, and | thought | was helping you, that's why | did what | did without realizing that the whole time, you were busy stabbing me in the back." "| deeply regret that." "And | have already forgiven you. | only said it so there would be no illusions about what we were to each other before. Which was nothing." "Please." He edged another inch forward, and | saw his hands trembling at his sides. "Give me a chance." "Why?" | let the word hang in the air. "Are you in love with me?" He swallowed, and the truth of it moved across his face before his mouth opened.

"| am not sure what | feel for you. "Then | am sure for you." | uncrossed my arms and pointed at the door. "You still feel guilty because you believe sorry is not enough. That is all this is. If you need complete absolution, go find a priest. They will not ask you to leave." Something flickered across his eyes, hurt or surprise, | could not tell which. "Then at least let us be friends. I just want to be close to you, Patricia." "| can never be friends with a man | have slept with." | let out a long breath. "You are wasting both our time. | am sure you have things to do, Mr.

Duke, just as | have things to do. Leave, or | will call security." He stared at me for along, quiet moment, and for one second | thought he might argue. Then he turned and walked out of my office without another word, and the door clicked shut behind him. The breath that left me came in one long rush, and | realized my hands were shaking. | pressed them flat against my desk and waited for my heart to slow. It refused to slow for a very long time. The rest of the day passed in a blur | could not account for.

| stayed locked in my office, staring at the same spreadsheet until the numbers stopped meaning anything. | did not cry. | had cried enough over the past eleven days to last me a lifetime. But | could not make myself work either, so | simply sat there while the afternoon light crawled across the wall and faded into evening. + big sale: 100 bonus free fou you

chapters.title: Chapter 345
chapters.content:
Chapter 345 When Helix closed for the day and the building fell quiet, | slipped out of my office and walked to my accommodation with my head down, the way a woman walks when she is hoping to be invisible. The shower was hot enough to sting, and | stood under it for a long time, letting the water beat against the back of my neck. When | reached for fresh panties, | noticed the pair | had changed into that afternoon. More spotting. Faint, pink, still nothing like the color my period should be. | told myself it was stress.

| ate a few snacks straight from the box, climbed into bed, and decided | would tell Celeste everything in the morning, the visit from Kingsley and the strange spotting and all of it. She would know what to make of it. She always did. | fell asleep almost the moment my head touched the pillow. And then | dreamed. | was in an operating theatre, all white light and green scrubs and the cold smell of antiseptic. | could not move, could not feel anything below my chest, yet somehow | knew a caesarean was being performed on me.

| watched it happen from somewhere above my own body, detached and floating, as the surgeons worked. And then, before my eyes, they lifted a baby boy out of me, wet and small and furious, and his cry pierced my ears like a blade. | woke with a gasp, sitting bolt upright in the dark. My nightgown was soaked through with sweat and my hands were freezing cold. | pressed one palm to my chest and waited for my breathing to slow. | had never dreamed anything like it in my life. Never.

It had to be some stray memory, something | had watched or read about a woman giving birth through a C-section, regurgitated by an exhausted brain. | tried to lie back down, but the moment my head touched the pillow, a nagging feeling crept in, the cold little prickle of a woman forgetting something important. My mind drifted back to Kingsley, to the way he had looked kneeling on my office floor, and then something clicked. "No." | got up with a start, and the word echoed off the walls of the small room. My heart began to pound so hard I could feel it in my throat.

Because | had not been sexually active before, | had stopped paying attention to my cycle. | never worried about the morning-after pill, because there had been no one to need it for. The only reason | still noted when my period would arrive was so it would not take me by surprise and stain my clothes in public. That was it. That was the entire extent of my diligence. And Kingsley had not used a condom. | grabbed my phone and opened my menstrual calendar with shaking fingers, scrolling back to that afternoon | had given myself to him. Eleven days ago.

| stared at the date, then at the little ovulation marker beside it, and my stomach dropped clean through the floor. Unsafe. | had slept with him during my unsafe period, one day before my ovulation day. "No. No. No. This cannot be." If that faint pink spotting in my panties was implantation bleeding, | was going to lose my mind. Why were my own things always different? Why did nothing in my life ever go the way it was supposed to? Other women made one stupid mistake and walked away with nothing but a story.

| made one stupid mistake, and apparently my body had decided to turn it into a full-blown crisis. | checked the time. It was past three in the morning. | needed a pregnancy test, and | needed it now. | threw on clothes and walked across the dark compound to the Helix lab, my footsteps echoing off the empty corridors. | searched the lab thoroughly, and relief flooded through me when | realized | could run the test myself with a simple finger prick. Then | stopped halfway. If implantation had only just happened, a finger prick would not be enough.

My HCG levels would still be low, and | could not afford a false negative. | needed to draw actual blood, a proper sample, for a quantitative B-hCG test.

chapters.title: Chapter 346
chapters.content:
Chapter 346 Drawing my own blood was risky. It was also the only option, because | refused to let anyone else in that lab do it. | was not about to make myself the subject of gossip before the sun had even come up. | tied the tourniquet around my arm and sat there sweating, my hands shaking so badly | could barely hold the needle still. | tried three times to get it into the vein, and each time | missed, until finally | gave up and dropped the needle onto the counter with a clatter. Drawing your own blood with a needle was hard enough on a good day.

Doing it when your hands would not stop trembling was impossible. So | decided to wait until daybreak and go to a lab far from the city, somewhere no one would recognize me. | walked back to my accommodation, freshened up, and changed into clean clothes. | could not bring myself to get back into bed. | just sat on the edge of it and checked my phone every few minutes, watching the clock crawl toward dawn.

At the first light of day, | left Helix and flagged down a cab, and | gave the driver the address of a Lab on the outskirts of the city, a small place | had found in an online search at four in the morning. The Lab was still locked when | arrived, so | stood outside in the cool grey light and waited, hugging my arms against my chest. A few minutes later, a woman in a white coat unlocked the door, and | went inside, had my blood drawn, and sat in the waiting room with my heart lodged in my throat.

One hour later, | stood outside that clinic staring at the test results in my hand as though they belonged to someone else. But the text on the paper was as real as the paper itself. Name: Patricia Spears Age: 30 Pregnancy: Positive. | was almost four weeks pregnant. Like a fool, | had gotten pregnant for Kingsley Duke. | sat down on a low wall at the corner of the clinic, in the shade of a struggling tree, and | stayed there for two hours thinking. About everything.

About the life growing inside me, and the man who did not love me, and the long, lonely stretch of years that had carried me to this exact spot. By the time | stood up, my mind was made. | was going to get rid of the baby. | would never use a child to make aman stay with me. | would never start a family with a man who did not love me, and | would never raise a child in the wreckage of my own desperation. Not that. Never that. | pressed my palm flat against my stomach, and the words came out in a whisper that broke somewhere in the middle.

"lam sorry, little one." My thumb moved in a small, slow circle. "You deserve better." | did not make the decision lightly, no matter how quickly it came to me on that cold clinic wall. | turned 'ies over the way a woman turns over a stone in her palm, weighing each side before she throws it. Vacuum aspiration was the first answer my mind offered, and for a while it seemed the cleanest one. A quick procedure in the hands of a proper doctor, a short stay, and it would all be over.

But a procedure like that meant a hospital, and a hospital meant records, and records meant the long arm of my family reaching in to shake me like a broken toy. The risk was not something | could swallow. My family could not get wind of this. My younger sister, Vivian would have a field day. She had spent her whole life turning my misfortunes into entertainment, the way some people turn on the television, and this particular misfortune would keep her fed for a year.

And my parents, God, my parents, who had always played favorites as naturally as other people breathed, would never let me live it down. They would hold it over me at every dinner, every holiday, every phone call | was already too tired to answer. | could hear my mother's voice already, soft and disappointed and somehow more cutting than a shout.

chapters.title: Chapter 347
chapters.content:
Chapter 347 So | ruled out the hospital. That left the medication, misoprostol, the kind of thing a woman could manage in the privacy of her own home if she had a prescription and a strong stomach. | knew the name from my work. I knew exactly what it did and how it did it, which was more than most women got, and the knowledge was not as comforting as | had hoped it would be. | remembered a friend from university, a quiet man who had gone on to become a gynaecologist, and | spent the better part of an afternoon tracking him down.

The internet gave me the clinic where he now worked, and the clinic gave me his office, and his office gave mea man who looked at me across his desk like | had just asked him to rob a bank. "1 don't write those prescriptions, Patricia." His voice was low, and he would not quite meet my eyes. "I've never written one. It's not that simple." "Itis exactly that simple." | leaned forward, my hands folded on my knees, and made myself smile through the shame. "You write the word, | take the paper, and this whole thing stops being a problem for either of us." "Misoprostol isn't aspirin.

You don't just hand it to a woman and wave goodbye. There are risks. There are things that can go wrong." "Things have already gone wrong." | held his gaze. " That's why I'm here." He argued for a long while, circling the same objections until they had no corners left, and | answered every one of them with the patient calm of a woman who had already made her choice long before she walked through his door. In the end, he sighed and reached for his pad, and | watched his pen move across the page with a strange mix of relief and dread.

| took the prescription to a pharmacy far from Helix, far from anyone who might know my face, and | bought the medicine with my head down. Then | went home. I knew how much Celeste valued children. | knew the way she still carried the sister she had lost, the way that loss had shaped her into someone who saw every child as a thing to be protected. If | told her now, she would talk me out of it. She would hold my hands and promise to help and somehow make me believe there was a way through this that did not end with me alone and terrified.

So | decided | would tell her only after it was done, when there was nothing left to talk me out of. | stared at the tablets in my palm for a long time. They were small and white and unremarkable, and my stomach twisted just looking at them. | had not eaten since morning, but hunger felt like something that belonged to another woman, someone with a future | no longer recognized. | swallowed hard, tipped the pills into my mouth, and chased them down with water that tasted like nothing. It was supposed to be simple.

That was what the internet said, what the forums promised, what some women described with an offhand ease that now felt like a cruel joke. But my own things were always different. They had been different my whole life, and apparently my body had no intention of letting me forget it. The nausea came first. It rose up out of nowhere, sudden and violent, and | barely made it to the bathroom before my stomach turned itself inside out. | vomited until my throat burned and my eyes watered and | thought my intestines might follow everything else into the bowl.

Just when | caught my breath and believed it was over, the diarrhea hit, and | spent the next hour shuffling between the bed and the toilet like a woman twice my age. When it finally died down, | caught a glimpse of my own face in the mirror and did not recognize it. Pale, sunken, slick with sweat, the face of a woman who had been wrung out and left to dry. Then the cramping began.

chapters.title: Chapter 348
chapters.content:
Chapter 348 It started low in my stomach and spread outward, a deep and grinding pain that made me curl onto the couch in the living room, my knees drawn up, my phone clutched against my chest like a lifeline. | thought about calling Celeste. | thought about it so hard my thumb hovered over her name, and then | let the phone fall because | had already made my choice and | was going to see it through. Then the fever came, and with it a cold that sank into my bones.

| was burning and freezing at the same time, shivering so hard my teeth chattered, and my throat was so dry | could barely swallow. | wanted warm water. | wanted the thick fur coat buried in the back of my closet. | forced myself off the couch and took a few steps toward the kitchen, and that was when my hands began to tremble, and a cold sweat broke across my skin, and my vision blurred at the edges until the room swam. My heart pounded so hard I could hear it in my ears. My legs went weak beneath me. My thoughts scattered like startled birds.

| tried to turn back, tried to reach the phone on the couch, tried to make my feet carry me the few steps that separated me from help, and then the floor rose up to meet me and | collapsed onto it. I could not move. That was the worst of it, worse than the shivering, worse than the cramps that rolled through my stomach in waves. | lay there on the cold floor with my cheek pressed against it, and | reached for my phone over and over, and my fingers would not close around it.

Then | felt the warmth between my thighs, and the bleeding came harder and faster than | had ever imagined, and within minutes | was soaking through everything beneath me. | do not know how long | lay there. Time stretched and folded in on itself until it stopped meaning anything. All | knew was the cold and the pain and the slow, creeping certainty that | was more alone in that moment than | had ever been in my life. And for the first time, | welcomed it. | welcomed the thought of dying, of letting go of all of it, of leaving the pain behind like a coat | no longer had to wear.

When | opened my eyes, the light was wrong. It was soft and white and clean, and nothing about it belonged to my apartment. | was disoriented at first, swimming up through a fog so thick | could not find the surface, and then the room came into focus and | understood. | was in a hospital. An IV drip was hooked into my vein, a thin plastic line feeding something cold into my arm. | turned my head and saw them, Dominic and Celeste, huddled together on a couch against the wall, asleep, with Celeste's head resting against his shoulder.

Her hand lay in his, and his other arm was wrapped around her like a shield, and they both looked exhausted in a way that told me they had not left this room in hours. The clock on the wall showed that the day had just begun. Somewhere below the fog, the realization surfaced, that they must have found me in my apartment, that they must have brought me here and stayed, that | had not been alone at all. The feeling rose up in me so fast | could not stop it, and | began to cry. Just then, Celeste opened her eyes.

She stretched, slow and groggy, and looked toward my bed, and when she saw the tears on my face her whole body went still. "Pat!" She was on her feet before | could blink, rushing to my bedside and pulling me into her arms with a fierceness that made the IV line pull tight. "I'm sorry, Pat. I'm so sorry." Her voice broke against my shoulder. "This is all my fault." | pushed her back gently, my hands on her arms, and made myself meet her eyes. "No, Celeste. What are you saying? You can't put this on yourself. | refuse to allow you to do that." big sale: 100 bonus free fou you

chapters.title: Chapter 349
chapters.content:
Chapter 349 I smiled at her, and the smile felt strange on my face, like a muscle | had forgotten how to use. Dominic had woken up and was watching me with that calm, careful attention of his. "Good morning, Dominic," | said. "Good morning, Pat." His voice was warm. "How are you feeling today?" | looked at him, at this man who had carried Celeste's world on his shoulders and still had room for me, and the answer came out before | could think about it.

"Like I'm lucky to have wonderful people like you two looking after me." Dominic smiled, and | turned back to Celeste, who was still staring at me with that haunted look. | opened my mouth to speak, and then my eyes caught the ring on her finger, and the words | had been about to say vanished entirely. "Oh my God!" | shrieked, and Celeste flinched so hard she nearly fell off the bed. "Did Dominic put a ring on it?" Celeste let out a long breath and nodded, her hand coming up to show me properly. | pulled her into a warm hug, laughing through the tears that were still drying on my cheeks.

"Congratulations. | mean it. Deep down, | was still scared Dominic wouldn't do right by you, you know?" "I'm right here, you know?" Dominic said, and | laughed. Celeste looked back at him with a smile, then turned to me. "Yeah. In the end, he decided to make an honest woman out of me." We both laughed, and Dominic got to his feet with a dramatic sigh. "Alright. I'll leave you girls to your gossip while | go get breakfast ready for my favorite person in the world...

and her bestie." Celeste blew him a kiss from where she sat, and he caught it in a funny gesture, closing his fist around the air and tucking it into his jacket pocket before he walked out of the room. | watched him go, and then | turned back to Celeste, reaching for her hand to admire the ring. "You're so lucky," | said, and | meant it with every part of me. "You have no idea..." "Enough about me." She cut me off, and her expression turned serious so fast it gave me whiplash. "Tell me the truth, Pat.

What happened?" | opened my mouth to explain, and then the door swung open and the doctor came in. We exchanged greetings, the polite little rituals of a hospital morning, and he asked how | was doing. He checked the monitors, adjusted the IV, and said | would be discharged in no time. Then he straightened up, and | saw something flicker across his face that made my stomach drop. "| have very important information to share with you both," he said. "Go ahead, Doctor." Celeste's hand tightened around mine. The doctor was silent for a long moment, and the silence filled the room like water.

Then he spoke, and each word landed like a stone dropped into that silence. "The ultrasound showed a gestational sac, which implies that the pregnancy is still ongoing." | felt a lump rise in my throat, hard and sharp. "What exactly do you mean by ongoing, Doctor?" He shifted his weight, and | saw him choose his words with care. "What | mean to say is that, Miss Spears, you are still pregnant." My heart stopped. The room tilted, and for a moment | was not sure | had heard him at all. "What?"

chapters.title: Chapter 350
chapters.content:
Chapter 350 CELESTE The corridor went quiet around me, and | stood there with my hand pressed over my mouth, the doctor's words ringing in my ears. Misoprostol. Medication abortion. Pat was pregnant. Pat had tried to end her own pregnancy, alone in her apartment, with no one to hold her hand, and she had nearly bled out on her living room floor while | was sliding a diamond onto my finger in a garden full of roses. Dominic's hand settled on the small of my back, steady and warm. "Celeste. She is going to be fine.

The doctor said so." "She did this alone, Dominic." My voice came out thin at the edges. "She went through all of that by herself, and | did not even notice she was missing. | was too busy being happy." "Hey." He turned me to face him, his palms cupping my cheeks. "You found her. You broke into her apartment. You carried her out. She is alive because of you. Do you hear me?" "If | had only called her that morning, she would never have..." "Stop." His thumb caught a tear | had not felt falling. " Pat is alive.

That is what matters." The doctor reaffirmed that Pat would sleep through the night, that we should go home and come back in the morning. | turned to Dominic.
